content.value: A Letter to God — G. L. Fuentes

> **Syllabus note:** First Flight and Footprints Without Feet together carry 40 Literature marks. RBSE does not assign a separate chapter weight or guaranteed question format to this story. The questions below are original practice.
Story outline

Lencho is a farmer whose ripe corn needs rain. Rain arrives, then turns into hail and destroys the crop. Believing that God sees everything, Lencho writes asking for 100 pesos to sow again and support his family until the next crop. A postmaster and others contribute money to answer the letter. The narrator says the postmaster can send “a little more than half” of the requested amount. Lencho later counts 70 pesos and writes again, accusing the post-office employees of taking the rest.

The story presents two conflicts named in the textbook: people against nature, and people against one another. The ending is ironic because the postal staff’s generosity is met with Lencho’s suspicion. Readers may debate Lencho’s character; the text shows his request, faith, and accusation, but does not require a single label such as “greedy” or “stupid.”

### सरल हिन्दी सार

लैंचो की मक्के की फसल को वर्षा चाहिए। वर्षा के बाद ओले पड़ते हैं और फसल नष्ट हो जाती है। लैंचो भगवान से 100 पेसो माँगकर पत्र लिखता है। पोस्टमास्टर और अन्य लोग सहायता के लिए धन जुटाते हैं। कहानी में पोस्टमास्टर 100 पेसो से थोड़ा अधिक आधा भेज पाता है। लैंचो को गिनने पर 70 पेसो मिलते हैं; वह शेष राशि न मिलने पर डाकघर के कर्मचारियों पर चोरी का संदेह करता है। यही अंत कहानी की विडंबना पैदा करता है।
Key facts from the text

| Point | Text-supported account |
|:--|:--|
| Lencho’s work | He is a farmer; the story calls him “an ox of a man,” working like an animal in the fields. |
| Setting | His house is the only one in the valley, on the crest of a low hill overlooking a river and ripe cornfield. The story does not name a country or town. |
| Crop disaster | A hailstorm lasts about an hour; the corn is totally destroyed. |
| First letter | Lencho asks God for 100 pesos to sow his field again and live until the next crop. |
| Postmaster’s response | He asks employees for money, contributes part of his salary, and receives contributions from friends. The narrator says he can send only “a little more than half” of 100 pesos. |
| Lencho’s count | Lencho says only 70 pesos reached him. The story does not state that the postmaster set out to collect exactly 70 pesos. |
| Second letter | Lencho asks God to send the rest and not to use the post office because its employees are “a bunch of crooks.” |
Words and phrases

| Word or phrase | Meaning in context |
|:--|:--|
| crest | The top of a hill. |
| downpour | A heavy fall of rain. |
| hailstones | Small balls of ice that fall from clouds. |
| draped | Covered as if with cloth. |
| solitary | Alone or isolated. |
| amiable | Friendly and pleasant. |
| conscience | A person’s inner sense of right and wrong. |
| pesos | A currency unit used in several countries; the text does not name the story’s setting. |
Reading notes

- **Metaphor:** “An ox of a man” describes Lencho as a hard worker by comparing him to an ox. The text immediately adds that he knows how to write.
- **Rain and coins:** Lencho calls the raindrops “new coins” because the rain promises a good harvest. Later hailstones resemble silver coins but destroy the crop.
- **Irony:** The postmaster’s efforts to preserve Lencho’s faith lead Lencho to suspect the post-office staff.
- **Faith and human action:** The story lets readers consider how help reaches Lencho and how he interprets it. Avoid stating that the narrator proves a theological claim.
Practice questions

These are original practice questions, not authenticated RBSE past-paper questions.

1. Why does Lencho compare the raindrops to coins?
2. How does the weather change, and what happens to the crop?
3. Why does the postmaster answer Lencho’s letter?
4. What does the story say the postmaster was able to send? How much does Lencho later say he received?
5. Explain the irony in Lencho’s second letter.
6. What two kinds of conflict does the textbook identify in the story?

### Suggested answers

1. He expects rain to help his ripe corn and bring a harvest; he imagines the drops as money.
2. Rain changes to hail. After about an hour, the corn is totally destroyed.
3. He is moved by Lencho’s faith and wants to answer the letter so as not to shake it.
4. The narrator says he sent a little more than half of 100 pesos; Lencho says 70 pesos reached him.
5. People at the post office arranged the money, yet Lencho thinks they took the missing amount and calls them crooks.
6. Conflict between humans and nature, and conflict between humans themselves.
Quick self-check

1. What amount did Lencho request?
2. What event destroys the corn?
3. Does the story say exactly how much the postmaster collected?
4. What does Lencho call the post-office employees?

**Answer key:** 1. 100 pesos. 2. A hailstorm. 3. No; it says “a little more than half”; Lencho later counts 70 pesos. 4. “A bunch of crooks.”

**Syllabus source correction, 13 October 2026:** Scope/marks above use the [Madhyamik Class 10 syllabus, PDF pp. 3–5](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf), not the separate Praveshika scheme. This correction does not certify the remaining exercise keys.

chapters.title: Class 10 English First Flight (Prose) — Chapter 2: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

content.value: माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान (RBSE Class 10) — Smart Study Guide Master Notes

**विषय:** English (Compulsory) | **विषय कोड:** 02  
**कक्षा:** 10वीं (माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर — RBSE)  
**Textbook:** First Flight (Prose Section) | **Chapter:** 02  
**Author / Autobiographer:** Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela (South Africa's first democratically elected Black president; Nobel Peace laureate)
**Genre:** Historical Autobiography / Political Discourse / Memoir  
**Current syllabus note:** First Flight and Footprints Without Feet together carry 40 marks; RBSE does not publish chapter-specific mark weights.
**Study goal:** Build accurate understanding and clear answers for the RBSE English theory examination.

---
⚡ 1. 10-Second Mind Map & Chapter Essence (Core Themes, Blueprint marks mapping, Teacher's Exam Advice)

### 📌 10-सेकंड अवधारणात्मक माइंडमैप (Conceptual Mind Map)

```
├──────────────────────────────┤            ├──────────────────────────────┤             ├──────────────────────────────┤

                           │ • Mature Vision: Greater hunger for the freedom of all │

```

### 🌟 पाठ का केंद्रीय भाव एवं मुख्य विषय (Chapter Essence & Core Themes)

1. **The Inauguration of South Africa's First Democratically Elected, Non-Racial Government (प्रथम लोकतांत्रिक, गैर-नस्लीय सरकार का शपथ ग्रहण):**
   - On 10th May 1994, in the majestic sandstone amphitheatre formed by the Union Buildings in Pretoria, Nelson Mandela took the oath as the first Black President of South Africa.
   - It marked the end of centuries of white supremacy and institutionalized racial segregation (**Apartheid**), replaced by a society founded on human dignity, equality, and constitutional justice.
   - *हिन्दी भाव:* 10 मई 1994 को प्रिटोरिया के यूनियन बिल्डिंग्स के भव्य रंगशाला (एम्फीथिएटर) में विश्व नेताओं की उपस्थिति में रंगभेद (Apartheid) की अमानवीय व्यवस्था का अंत हुआ और दक्षिण अफ्रीका की पहली गैर-नस्लीय, लोकतांत्रिक सरकार स्थापित हुई।

2. **Mandela's Profound Definition of Courage (साहस की कालजयी परिभाषा):**
   - Mandela learned from freedom fighters (Sisulu, Tambo, Dadoo, Fischer, Sobukwe) that courage is not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it. A brave man is not he who does not feel afraid, but he who conquers that fear.
   - *हिन्दी भाव:* साहस का अर्थ भय की अनुपस्थिति नहीं, बल्कि भय पर विजय पाना है। वीर वह नहीं जिसे डर न लगे, बल्कि वह है जो डर को जीत लेता है।

3. **The Philosophy of Twin Obligations (दोहरे दायित्वों का दर्शन):**
   - Every human being has twin obligations:
     1. First obligation: Towards family, parents, wife, and children.
     2. Second obligation: Towards his people, his community, and his country.
   - Under Apartheid, a man of color attempting to fulfill duty to his people was ripped from his family and forced into a twilight existence of secrecy and rebellion.
   - *हिन्दी भाव:* प्रत्येक मनुष्य के दो कर्तव्य होते हैं—पहला परिवार के प्रति और दूसरा समाज व देश के प्रति। रंगभेदी शासन में काले लोगों को अपने देश के प्रति कर्तव्य निभाने पर विद्रोही मानकर परिवार से अलग कर दिया जाता था।

4. **Emancipation of Both the Oppressor and the Oppressed (शोषक और शोषित दोनों की मुक्ति):**
   - Mandela asserts that the oppressor is just as enslaved as the oppressed. The man who takes away another man's freedom is a prisoner of hatred, locked behind the bars of prejudice and narrow-mindedness. Both must be liberated.
   - *हिन्दी भाव:* शोषक (अत्याचारी) भी उतना ही गुलाम है जितना शोषित। जो दूसरे की आज़ादी छीनता है, वह स्वयं घृणा और संकीर्णता की सलाखों के पीछे कैद कैदी है। दोनों को मुक्त किया जाना अनिवार्य है।

5. **The Real Wealth of a Nation (राष्ट्र की वास्तविक संपदा):**
   - South Africa is exceptionally rich in gold and diamonds buried beneath its soil, but Mandela proclaims that the country's finest and truest wealth is its people, finer and truer than the purest diamonds.

### 🎓 शिक्षक की विशेष बोर्ड परीक्षा सलाह (Teacher's Board Exam Advice)
> 💡 **Answer-writing practice:**
> 1. **Memorize the Crucial Vocabulary:** For practice answers, refer accurately to key phrases such as: *"sandstone amphitheatre"*, *"extraordinary human disaster"*, *"rainbow gathering"*, *"curtain of apartheid"*, *"triumph over fear"*, *"twin obligations"*, and *"prisoner of hatred"*.
> 2. **Master the Date & Venue:** 10th May (autumn day in the Southern Hemisphere), Union Buildings in Pretoria.
> 3. **The 'Hunger for Freedom' Progression:** When discussing Mandela's changing understanding of freedom, organise the answer chronologically; no fixed four-part response is required (childhood illusion ➔ student transitory freedoms ➔ young man's basic freedoms ➔ ANC political struggle for all people).


---
🎭 2. Deep Character Sketches & Key Figures (Traits, actions, motivations, quotes)

### 1. Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela (The Pillar of Resilient Reconciliation / मुक्तिदूत व राजनेता)
* **Life Struggle & Transformation:**
  - Spent more than 27 years in prison, including time at Pretoria Local Prison, Robben Island, Pollsmoor and Victor Verster.
  - Transformed from a frightened young lawyer running from the law into a fearless rebel, from a family-loving husband into a man without a home, from a life-loving person into a monk-like ascetic dedicated to national liberation.
  - *हिन्दी विवरण:* मंडेला ने रंगभेद के विरुद्ध संघर्ष में 27 वर्ष से अधिक समय जेल में बिताया। वे एक भयभीत वकील से निर्भीक विद्रोही और परिवार-प्रेमी पति से राष्ट्र-समर्पित जननायक में बदल गए।
* **Key Character Traits:**
  - **Magnanimous Forgiveness & Reconciliation (उदार क्षमाशीलता):** Rather than seeking vengeance against white oppressors upon gaining power, he extended a hand of brotherhood, establishing a multi-racial democratic rainbow nation.
  - **Humility & Gratitude (विनम्रता एवं पूर्वजों के प्रति कृतज्ञता):** He saw himself merely as "the sum of all those African patriots who had gone before me", mourning that they could not live to see what their sacrifices had achieved.
  - **Profound Philosophical Insight (दार्शनिक गहराई):** He understood that hatred is learned; and if people can learn to hate, they can be taught to love, for love comes more naturally to the human heart than its opposite.
* **Useful textual references for practice answers (no score guarantee):**
  - *"I learned that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it."*
  - *"I am the sum of all those African patriots who had gone before me."*
  - *"Man's goodness is a flame that can be hidden but never extinguished."*
  - *"The oppressor must be liberated just as surely as the oppressed."*

### 2. The African Patriots & Comrades (Oliver Tambo, Walter Sisulu, Chief Luthuli, Yusuf Dadoo, Bram Fischer, Robert Sobukwe)
* **Embodiment of Unmatched Character:**
  - Giants of the liberation struggle whose courage, wisdom, and generosity were forged by the sheer brutality of white minority oppression.
  - Mandela observes that extraordinary depths of oppression produce extraordinary heights of character.
* *हिन्दी विवरण:* ये वे महान स्वतंत्रता सेनानी थे जिनके असाधारण त्याग, धैर्य और ज्ञान ने मंडेला को साहस का अर्थ सिखाया। रंगभेद के क्रूर दमन ने इन अद्वितीय चरित्रों को गढ़ा।

### 3. Zenani (The Supportive Daughter)
* Mandela's beloved daughter who accompanied him on the historic inauguration podium on 10th May, symbolizing family solidarity that endured through years of painful separation.

### 4. Mr. de Klerk and Thabo Mbeki
* **Mr. de Klerk:** Sworn in as second deputy president.
* **Thabo Mbeki:** Sworn in as first deputy president, standing united to steer South Africa into its democratic dawn.


---
📜 3. Key Extract-Based Passages with Board Model Questions & Detailed Explanations

### 📖 Extract 1: The Dawn of 10th May & The Rainbow Gathering (10 मई का ऐतिहासिक प्रभात)
```text
"10th May dawned bright and clear. For the past few days I had been pleasantly besieged by 
dignitaries and world leaders who were coming to pay their respects before the inauguration. 
The inauguration would be the largest gathering ever of international leaders on South 
African soil.
The ceremonies took place in the lovely sandstone amphitheatre formed by the Union Buildings 
in Pretoria. For decades this had been the seat of white supremacy, and now it was the site 
of a rainbow gathering of different colours and nations for the installation of South 
Africa's first democratic, non-racial government."
```

* **Glossary & Meanings (कठिन शब्दार्थ):**
  - **Dawned:** Began / broke out (प्रभात हुआ / उदय हुआ).
  - **Pleasantly besieged:** Happily surrounded by people (आदरपूर्वक चारों ओर से घिरे हुए).
  - **Dignitaries:** Important and famous persons / VIPs (प्रतिष्ठित व्यक्ति / गणमान्य अतिथि).
  - **Amphitheatre:** A circular open-air theatre with rows of seats rising in steps (खुली गोलाकार रंगशाला).
  - **Supremacy:** Superiority / domination (प्रभुत्व / वर्चस्व).
  - **Rainbow gathering:** A multi-racial, multi-cultural assembly of diverse people (इंद्रधनुषी सभा).
* **Text-based practice questions and suggested answers:**
  1. **Why was 10th May described as 'bright and clear'? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* It marked the dawn of freedom and democracy in South Africa after centuries of oppressive white rule.
  2. **Where did the inauguration ceremony take place? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* The ceremony took place in the sandstone amphitheatre formed by the Union Buildings in Pretoria.
  3. **Why is the gathering called a 'rainbow gathering'? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* It brought together dignitaries of various races, colors, and nationalities from across the world, just like the multiple colors of a rainbow.
  4. **Find a word from the passage that means 'surrounded closely'. (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Besieged.
  5. **What had the Union Buildings been for decades prior to this day? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* For decades, the Union Buildings had been the seat of white supremacy and racial domination.

---

### 📖 Extract 2: The Military Salute & The Two National Anthems (सैन्य सलामी एवं दो राष्ट्रगान)
```text
"A few moments later we all lifted our eyes in awe as a spectacular array of South African 
jets, helicopters and troop carriers roared in perfect formation over the Union Buildings. 
It was not only a display of pinpoint precision and military force, but a demonstration 
of the military's loyalty to democracy, to a new government that had been freely and fairly 
elected. Only moments before, the highest generals of the South African defence force and 
police, their chests bedecked with ribbons and medals from days gone by, saluted me and 
pledged their loyalty. I was not unmindful of the fact that not so many years before they 
would not have saluted but arrested me. Finally a chevron of Impala jets left a smoke trail 
of the black, red, green, blue and gold of the new South African flag.
The day was symbolised for me by the playing of our two national anthems..."
```

* **Glossary & Meanings (कठिन शब्दार्थ):**
  - **Spectacular array:** An impressive, eye-catching display (भव्य और प्रभावशाली प्रदर्शन).
  - **Pinpoint precision:** Exact accuracy (अचूक सटीकता).
  - **Bedecked:** Decorated with ornaments or medals (सजे हुए).
  - **Chevron:** A V-shaped pattern or formation (V-आकार की आकृति).
  - **Not unmindful:** Conscious of / fully remembering (भली-भांति याद होना).
* **Text-based practice questions and suggested answers:**
  1. **What did the spectacular display of military jets demonstrate? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* It demonstrated not only military precision, but the armed forces' absolute loyalty to democracy and the newly elected government.
  2. **How had the attitude of the military generals changed towards Mandela? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* The same generals whose chests were bedecked with medals now saluted Mandela and pledged loyalty, whereas years earlier they would have arrested him as a terrorist rebel.
  3. **Which two national anthems were sung on that historic day? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* The white citizens sang 'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika' and the black citizens sang the old anthem of the republic, 'Die Stem'.
  4. **Find a word in the passage which means 'decorated'. (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Bedecked.
  5. **What colors were left in the smoke trail by the Impala jets? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* The black, red, green, blue, and gold colors representing the new democratic South African national flag.

---

### 📖 Extract 3: The True Definition of Courage & Comrades (साहस का वास्तविक अर्थ)
```text
"I learned that courage was not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it. The brave 
man is not he who does not feel afraid, but he who conquers that fear.
I learned that through these comrades in the struggle I learned the meaning of courage. 
Time and again, I have seen men and women risk and give their lives for an idea. I have seen 
men stand up to attacks and torture without breaking, showing a strength and resilience that 
defies the imagination.
No one is born hating another person because of the colour of his skin, or his background, 
or his religion. People must learn to hate, and if they can learn to hate, they can be taught 
to love, for love comes more naturally to the human heart than its opposite."
```

* **Glossary & Meanings (कठिन शब्दार्थ):**
  - **Triumph:** Victory / conquest (विजय / फतह).
  - **Resilience:** The ability to endure hardships and recover quickly (कठिनाइयों को सहने की अदम्य शक्ति / लचीलापन).
  - **Defies:** Resists / goes beyond (चुनौती देना / परे होना).
  - **Naturally:** Innately / inherently (स्वाभाविक रूप से).
* **Text-based practice questions and suggested answers:**
  1. **What does Mandela mean by 'courage'? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Mandela defines courage not as the absence of fear, but as the triumph over fear. A brave man conquers his fears rather than never feeling them.
  2. **What has Mandela seen men and women do for an idea? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* He has seen brave men and women risk and sacrifice their lives, facing brutal torture without breaking their spirit.
  3. **Why does Mandela believe love can be taught if people can learn to hate? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Because no human is born with innate hatred; hatred is learned, whereas love springs forth much more naturally from the human heart.
  4. **Find the word in the passage that means 'the ability to deal with any kind of hardship and recover'. (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Resilience.
  5. **According to Mandela, what is man's goodness like? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Man's goodness is like a flame that can be hidden beneath adversity, but can never be permanently extinguished.

---

### 📖 Extract 4: The Oppressor & The Oppressed (शोषक एवं शोषित की परतंत्रता)
```text
"I knew that the oppressor must be liberated just as surely as the oppressed. A man who 
takes away another man's freedom is a prisoner of hatred; he is locked behind the bars of 
prejudice and narrow-mindedness. I am not truly free if I am taking away someone else's freedom, 
just as surely as I am not free when my freedom is taken from me. The oppressed and the 
oppressor alike are robbed of their humanity."
```

* **Glossary & Meanings (कठिन शब्दार्थ):**
  - **Liberated:** Freed / released from bondage (मुक्त किया गया).
  - **Prisoner of hatred:** Enslaved by malice and animosity (घृणा का बंदी).
  - **Prejudice:** A strong unreasonable feeling or dislike against a group (पूर्वाग्रह / बिना विचारे द्वेष).
  - **Narrow-mindedness:** Petty, intolerant thinking (संकीर्ण मानसिकता).
  - **Robbed:** Deprived of / stolen from (वंचित कर दिया गया).
* **Text-based practice questions and suggested answers:**
  1. **Why does Mandela believe that the oppressor must also be liberated? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Because the oppressor is enslaved by hatred and locked behind the bars of prejudice and narrow-mindedness; he is not spiritually free.
  2. **Who is a 'prisoner of hatred' according to the author? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* A person who deprives another human being of their freedom is a prisoner of hatred.
  3. **What is common between the oppressor and the oppressed? (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Both the oppressor and the oppressed are equally robbed of their essential humanity.
  4. **Find a word from the passage which means 'unjustified dislike or bias'. (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Prejudice.
  5. **Explain: 'The oppressed and the oppressor alike are robbed of their humanity.' (1 practice question)**
     - *Answer:* Cruelty dehumanizes the oppressor by poisoning his soul with malice, while suffering dehumanizes the victim through degradation and pain.


---
🎯 4. 8 Comprehensive Solved Model Archetypes (Step-by-Step model answers)

### 📌 Archetype 1: Historical Significance of 10th May (practice answer; suggested length 60–80 words)
* **Question:** Why was the 10th of May an 'autumn day' in South Africa? What was the historical significance of the ceremonies held on this day?
* **Step-by-Step Model Answer:**
  1. **Geographical Explanation:** South Africa is located in the Southern Hemisphere, where the seasons are reversed compared to the Northern Hemisphere. Hence, May corresponds to autumn rather than spring.
  2. **Historical Metaphor:** Metaphorically, autumn represents the ripening and harvest of long-sought fruits. The seeds of freedom sown by generations of martyrs finally ripened on 10th May 1994.
  3. **Inaugural Significance:**
     - It marked the official installation of South Africa's first democratically elected, non-racial government.
     - The textbook's introductory news item reports that dignitaries from more than 140 countries attended at Pretoria's Union Buildings. Mandela describes the gathering as a major international event marking a democratic, non-racial government.

---

### 📌 Archetype 2: Nelson Mandela's Concept of Courage (practice answer; suggested length 50–60 words)
* **Question:** How does Nelson Mandela define 'courage'? How did his comrades in the struggle exemplify this virtue?
* **Step-by-Step Model Answer:**
  - **Definition:** Mandela discovered that courage is **not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it**. A courageous person is not someone who never experiences terror, but one who successfully overcomes and masters that terror.
  - **Example of Comrades:** Giants like Walter Sisulu, Oliver Tambo, and Bram Fischer endured unspeakable torture, solitary confinement, and threats to their lives without bending or breaking. Their unwavering resilience taught Mandela that moral purpose elevates ordinary mortals above physical fear.

---

### 📌 Archetype 3: The Philosophy of 'Twin Obligations' (practice answer; suggested length 60–80 words)
* **Question:** What are the 'twin obligations' that every human being possesses according to Mandela? Why was it impossible for a black South African to fulfill them?
* **Step-by-Step Model Answer:**
  1. **The Twin Obligations Defined:**
     - **Obligation 1:** Personal duty to one's parents, spouse, children, and immediate family.
     - **Obligation 2:** Civic and moral duty to one's community, people, and nation.
  2. **The Apartheid Tragedy:**
     - In a normal, civilized society, an individual balances both duties naturally.
     - However, under the vicious apartheid regime in South Africa, a Black citizen who attempted to live as a responsible human and serve his oppressed community was branded a traitor, hunted by police, torn away from his home and family, and forced into an isolated existence of secrecy and rebellion.

---

### 📌 Archetype 4: Evolution of Mandela's Understanding of Freedom (practice answer; suggested length 60–80 words)
* **Question:** How did Mandela's understanding of freedom change from boyhood to adulthood? Trace the four distinct phases of his realization.
* **Step-by-Step Model Answer:**
  1. **Boyhood (An Illusion):** As a young boy, freedom meant running freely in the green fields near his mother's hut, swimming in the clear village stream, roasting mealies under the stars, and riding slow-moving bulls.
  2. **Youth / Student (Transitory Freedoms):** As a student, he hungered for individual freedoms: the ability to stay out late at night, read books of his choice, and travel wherever he pleased.
  3. **Early Adulthood (Basic Potential):** In Johannesburg, he yearned for the freedom to earn his livelihood, marry, raise a family, and not be obstructed in a lawful life.
  4. **Mature Political Realization (Collective Freedom):** He realized that not only was he unfree, but his brothers and sisters were equally enslaved. His personal hunger transformed into a blazing hunger for the collective freedom, self-respect, and dignity of his entire African race.

---

### 📌 Archetype 5: The Two National Anthems — Symbol of Unity (practice answer; suggested length 40–50 words)
* **Question:** Why were two national anthems sung at the inauguration? What did this musical gesture symbolize?
* **Step-by-Step Model Answer:**
  - **The Two Anthems:** On 10th May, the white South Africans sang *'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika'* (God Bless Africa), while the black South Africans sang *'Die Stem'* (The Voice of South Africa), the old anthem of the apartheid republic.
  - **Symbolism:** Mandela presents the singing of both anthems as a symbol of the country's transition and unity. The text says that neither group knew the lyrics of the anthem they had once despised; it does not say they did not know each other's anthem.

---

### 📌 Archetype 6: The Oppressor is Also a Prisoner (practice answer; suggested length 60–80 words)
* **Question:** "The oppressor must be liberated just as surely as the oppressed." Explain this paradoxical statement in light of Mandela's philosophical worldview.
* **Step-by-Step Model Answer:**
  1. **The Bondage of the Victim:** The oppressed suffers physical confinement, economic degradation, racial humiliation, and denial of basic human rights.
  2. **The Spiritual Prison of the Tormentor:** The oppressor, on the other hand, is enslaved by hatred. He is confined behind the impenetrable bars of prejudice, arrogance, and narrow-mindedness.
  3. **Moral Conclusion:** Anyone who snatches away another person's freedom forfeits his own inner liberty. Cruelty destroys the humanity of the oppressor just as profoundly as it degrades the victim. True liberation requires freeing both the victim from fear and the tyrant from hatred.

---

### 📌 Archetype 7: The True Mineral Wealth of South Africa (practice answer; suggested length 30–40 words)
* **Question:** What does Mandela consider the greatest wealth of his country? Compare it with geological wealth.
* **Step-by-Step Model Answer:**
  - South Africa is world-famous for its glittering minerals, vast gold deposits, and diamonds extracted from its deep mines.
  - However, Mandela firmly proclaims that the country's greatest, truest, and most enduring wealth is **its people**—who are finer, truer, and purer than the most precious diamonds when tested in the crucible of moral character.

---

### 📌 Archetype 8: Transformation of Mandela's Life by the African National Congress (practice answer; suggested length 50–60 words)
* **Question:** How did the desire for freedom for his people transform Nelson Mandela's personal lifestyle?
* **Step-by-Step Model Answer:**
  - Joining the African National Congress (ANC) transformed Mandela completely:
    1. It turned a timid, frightened young lawyer into a bold and defiant public rebel.
    2. It drove a lawful attorney to become a fugitive hunted by the state.
    3. It forced a devoted, family-loving husband to live without a home.
    4. It compelled a life-loving young man to adopt the austere, self-denying existence of a monk dedicated solely to the liberation of his motherland.


---
⚠️ 5. Common answer-writing errors (सामान्य त्रुटियाँ एवं समाधान)

| ❌ Common Mistake (छात्रों की सामान्य गलती) | ⚠️ Possible issue | ✅ Correct Board-Standard Answer (सही उत्तर) |
|---|---|---|
| Writing that May 10th is spring in South Africa. | Factual error showing geographical ignorance. | South Africa is in the Southern Hemisphere; May is an **autumn month** there. |
| Defining courage as "having no fear at all". | Complete contradiction of Mandela's central message. | Courage is **not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it** (fear par vijay). |
| Omitting the names of the two anthems when a question asks for them. | Naming them helps answer that specific question; no exact marking rule is established here. | The text identifies *'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika'* with the white group and *'Die Stem'* with the black group. |
| Claiming Mandela hated white people. | Misrepresents his philosophy of reconciliation. | Mandela hated the **system of Apartheid**, but advocated forgiving white citizens to build a unified nation. |
| Giving an incomplete venue description. | The answer may omit a useful detail. | The ceremony was held in the sandstone amphitheatre formed by the Union Buildings in Pretoria. |
| Confusing "Prejudice" with ordinary anger. | Evaluators check vocabulary accuracy. | *Prejudice* means unreasonable negative bias, pre-judgment, or intolerance against a specific group. |
| Describing the smoke trail with random colors. | Evaluators check the exact flag colors. | The Impala jets emitted smoke of **black, red, green, blue, and gold** (the new South African flag). |

---
Practice question bank (not authenticated RBSE past papers)

### 1. [Practice set] What does Nelson Mandela mean by 'courage'?
* **Model Answer:** Nelson Mandela explains that courage is not the absence of fear, but triumph over it. A brave man is not someone who never feels afraid, but someone who conquers that fear with moral resilience.

### 2. [Practice set] Where did the ceremonies take place and what was the historic occasion?
* **Model Answer:** The ceremonies took place in the sandstone amphitheatre formed by the Union Buildings in Pretoria. The occasion was the installation of South Africa's first democratic, non-racial government led by President Nelson Mandela.

### 3. [Practice set] What are the 'twin obligations' referred to by Nelson Mandela?
* **Model Answer:** The twin obligations are: first, a person's obligation to his family, parents, wife, and children; second, his obligation to his people, his community, and his country.

### 4. [Practice set] Why were two national anthems sung on the day of the inauguration?
* **Model Answer:** Two national anthems were sung to symbolize the equality, harmony, and mutual respect between the white and black citizens of South Africa, demonstrating the birth of a unified, non-racial nation.

### 5. [Practice set] What does Mandela say about the oppressor and the oppressed?
* **Model Answer:** Mandela states that the oppressor must be liberated just like the oppressed. A person who takes away another's liberty is a prisoner of hatred, trapped behind prejudice and narrow-mindedness. Both are robbed of their humanity.

### 6. [Practice set] How did the South African military demonstrate its attitude towards the new government?
* **Model Answer:** The military staged a spectacular jet flypast over the Union Buildings. Top defense and police generals saluted Mandela and pledged loyalty to democracy, in sharp contrast to earlier years when they would have arrested him.

### 7. [Practice set] What does Mandela think is the greatest wealth of South Africa?
* **Model Answer:** While South Africa is rich in minerals and diamonds, Mandela believes its greatest and purest wealth is its people, whom he describes as finer and truer than the purest diamonds.

### 8. [Practice set] What did freedom mean to Mandela as a student and as a boy?
* **Model Answer:** As a boy, freedom meant running in the fields, swimming in streams, and roasting mealies under the stars. As a student, it meant transitory individual freedoms—staying out late, reading desired books, and traveling freely.

### 9. [Practice set] Name any three freedom fighters mentioned by Mandela who fought against apartheid.
* **Model Answer:** Oliver Tambo, Walter Sisulu, Chief Luthuli, and Yusuf Dadoo were prominent freedom fighters who demonstrated extraordinary courage and sacrifice against apartheid.


---
📝 7. Practice Question Bank (Comprehensive MCQs, Short & Long Answers)

### Section A: Multiple Choice Practice Questions
1. On which date was the inauguration ceremony held?
   (A) 15th August  
   (B) 10th May  
   (C) 26th January  
   (D) 2nd October  
   *Answer:* (B) 10th May

2. Where was the inauguration ceremony conducted?
   (A) Johannesburg Stadium  
   (B) Cape Town Parliament  
   (C) Sandstone amphitheatre of Union Buildings in Pretoria  
   (D) Durban Town Hall  
   *Answer:* (C) Sandstone amphitheatre of Union Buildings in Pretoria

3. Nelson Mandela was accompanied on the podium by his daughter:
   (A) Winnie  
   (B) Zenani  
   (C) Graça  
   (D) Miriam  
   *Answer:* (B) Zenani

4. Who was sworn in as the first deputy president?
   (A) Nelson Mandela  
   (B) Thabo Mbeki  
   (C) Mr. de Klerk  
   (D) Walter Sisulu  
   *Answer:* (B) Thabo Mbeki

5. According to Mandela, what is courage?
   (A) Absence of fear  
   (B) Fighting with weapons  
   (C) Triumph over fear  
   (D) Lack of emotion  
   *Answer:* (C) Triumph over fear

6. What did the Impala jets leave behind in the sky?
   (A) A circle of silver smoke  
   (B) A chevron of black, red, green, blue, and gold smoke  
   (C) A single white stripe  
   (D) Golden sparks  
   *Answer:* (B) A chevron of black, red, green, blue, and gold smoke

7. The policy of Apartheid created a:
   (A) Temporary disagreement  
   (B) Deep and lasting wound in South Africa  
   (C) Golden age of economy  
   (D) Scientific revolution  
   *Answer:* (B) Deep and lasting wound in South Africa

8. Man's goodness is like a flame that can be:
   (A) Extinguished easily  
   (B) Hidden but never extinguished  
   (C) Destroyed by laws  
   (D) Seen only in churches  
   *Answer:* (B) Hidden but never extinguished

9. According to Mandela, South Africa's truest wealth is:
   (A) Its gold mines  
   (B) Its vast diamond reserves  
   (C) Its people  
   (D) Its wild animals  
   *Answer:* (C) Its people

10. A man who takes away another man's freedom is a prisoner of:
    (A) Law  
    (B) Hatred  
    (C) Poverty  
    (D) Superstition  
    *Answer:* (B) Hatred

---

### Section B: Fill-in-the-blank Practice Questions
11. 10th May dawned bright and clear, an __________ day in the Southern Hemisphere.
    *Answer:* autumn
12. The highest generals of the defence force had their chests bedecked with __________ and medals.
    *Answer:* ribbons
13. The White citizens sang 'Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika' while the Black citizens sang __________.
    *Answer:* Die Stem
14. A man who takes away another man's freedom is locked behind the bars of prejudice and __________.
    *Answer:* narrow-mindedness
15. Extraordinary depths of oppression create extraordinary heights of __________.
    *Answer:* character
16. Mandela spent __________ years of his life imprisoned for fighting against racial injustice.
    *Answer:* 27 (or nearly three decades)

---

### Section C: Short-answer practice questions (suggested concise responses)
17. **Why was Mandela overwhelmed with a sense of history during the inauguration?**
    - *Answer:* He recalled how, in the early twentieth century after the Anglo-Boer war, white South Africans established a system of racial domination against black people, which was now finally replaced by equality.
18. **What unintended effect did the decades of oppression have on the South African people?**
    - *Answer:* The brutality of apartheid inadvertently produced men of extraordinary courage, wisdom, and magnanimity like Oliver Tambo, Walter Sisulu, and Chief Luthuli.
19. **Why did Mandela say he was 'simply the sum of all those African patriots'?**
    - *Answer:* He acknowledged with deep humility that the democratic victory was not his personal achievement alone, but the culmination of the untold sacrifices of thousands of martyrs who preceded him.
20. **What does Mandela mean when he says 'love comes more naturally to the human heart than its opposite'?**
    - *Answer:* He believes humans are innately wired for empathy and affection; hatred is an unnatural, learned social prejudice that can always be unlearned.
21. **What pledge did Nelson Mandela make in his presidential address?**
    - *Answer:* He pledged to liberate all people from the continuing bondage of poverty, deprivation, suffering, gender bias, and all other forms of discrimination.

---

### Section D: Long-answer practice questions (suggested response lengths only)
22. **Discuss Nelson Mandela's journey from a life of fear to a life of fearless leadership. What sacrifices did this transformation demand?**
    - *Model Answer:* Mandela describes how his understanding of freedom changed from personal freedoms in boyhood and youth to a commitment to collective freedom. His political work and imprisonment separated him from family life. The chapter presents him as committed to reconciliation and to ending apartheid; this answer is a literary summary, not a full biography.

23. **"True freedom is not merely casting off one's chains, but living in a way that respects and enhances the freedom of others." Analyze this statement in the context of the chapter.**
    - *Model Answer:* Mandela's profound moral philosophy reaches its zenith in his realization that freedom is indivisible. Freedom is not an individual luxury or the mere legal abolition of physical slavery. It requires an active moral responsibility to safeguard and nurture the liberty and human dignity of every person in society. Mandela stresses that as long as hatred, prejudice, poverty, and inequality persist, humanity remains in chains. True freedom demands that former oppressors and former victims live side-by-side without bitterness or fear. By welcoming former white rulers into his democratic cabinet and championing constitutional harmony, Mandela proved that to be truly free, one must liberate society from the cycle of retribution and build a world founded on shared human dignity.

### 🌟 पाठ का केंद्रीय भाव एवं मुख्य विषय (Chapter Essence & Core Themes)

#### Story I: His First Flight (Liam O'Flaherty)
1. **Conquering Fear and Self-Doubt (भय और आत्म-संदेह पर विजय):**
   - The young seagull's two brothers and little sister had much shorter wings than his, yet they ran to the brink, flapped their wings, and flew away. The young seagull lacked confidence in his own wings, terrified by the sheer expanse of the sea below.
   - *हिन्दी भाव:* छोटे समुद्री बगुले के भाई-बहन जिनके पंख उससे भी छोटे थे, उड़ गए; परंतु वह अगाध समुद्र को देखकर डर गया कि उसके पंख उसका साथ नहीं देंगे।
2. **The familys response (माता-पिता की प्रतिक्रिया):**
   - The parents scolded him and threatened to let him starve on the ledge unless he flew. Later, the mother brought a piece of fish and held it just beyond his reach; hunger helped prompt him to dive.
   - She held a piece of fish almost within his reach. Maddened by hunger, he dived towards it.
   - *हिन्दी भाव:* माता-पिता ने उसे डांटा और भूखा रहने की चेतावनी दी। अंततः माँ ने मछली का टुकड़ा दिखाकर उसकी भूख को उसकी उड़ान की शक्ति बना दिया।
3. **The Ecstasy of Self-Realization (आत्म-विश्वास का परमानंद):**
   - The moment he plunged, monstrous terror seized him, but a minute later his wings spread outward, wind rushed against his breast feathers, and he discovered he was not falling headlong but soaring gracefully.

#### Story II: The Black Aeroplane (Frederick Forsyth)
1. **The Peril of Complacency and Reckless Desire (अति-उत्साह और खतरे की अनदेखी):**
   - The narrator was flying his old Dakota airplane from France to England under a serene starlit sky, dreaming of joining his family for a grand English breakfast.
   - When massive storm clouds resembling black mountains blocked his path, his longing for home made him take the reckless decision to fly straight into the tempest rather than returning to Paris.
   - *हिन्दी भाव:* पायलट अपने घर पहुँचकर परिवार के साथ 'अंग्रेजी नाश्ता' करने की लालसा में तूफानी बादलों को देखकर भी पेरिस वापस लौटने के बजाय खतरे में सीधा घुस जाता है।
2. **The Mystery of the Black Aeroplane (काले रहस्यमयी विमान का विस्मय):**
   - Inside the storm, the compass, radio and other instruments failed. Another pilot appeared in a black aeroplane with no lights on its wings and signalled him to follow.
   - After landing, the narrator asked the woman at the control centre about the other aeroplane. She said the Dakota was the only one she could see on the radar.
   - *हिन्दी भाव:* जब उसके सारे यंत्र बंद हो गए, तो एक अनाम काले विमान के पायलट ने उसे रास्ता दिखाया। सुरक्षित उतरने पर पता चला कि रडार पर उसके अलावा कोई दूसरा विमान था ही नहीं!
3. **Providence, Willpower, or Subconscious Hallucination (ईश्वरीय कृपा या अंतर्मन का विश्वास):**
   - The story leaves the black aeroplane's identity unexplained. The NCERT teacher's note explicitly invites discussion about whether it was real or imagined; supernatural aid is one possible interpretation, not a stated fact.

### 🎓 शिक्षक की विशेष बोर्ड परीक्षा सलाह (Answer-writing practice (not an official marking scheme))
> 💡 **Answer-writing practice:**
> 1. **Differentiate Both Authors:** Liam O'Flaherty for Story I; Frederick Forsyth for Story II. 
> 2. **Part I Crucial Phrases:** *"monstrous terror"*, *"scrap of fish"*, *"maddened by hunger"*, *"legs sank into green sea"*, and *"first flight"*.
> 3. **Part II Crucial Phrases:** *"Old Dakota DS 088"*, *"English breakfast"*, *"black mountains"*, *"compass turned round and round"*, *"no lights on its wings"*, and *"radar control room"*.

  - Fear dissolved within seconds, replaced by the triumphant thrill of flapping his wings and floating on the green sea.

* **Actions in the story:**

### 📖 Extract 1: The Young Seagull's Terror & Parental Admonition (Story I)
```text
"The young seagull was alone on his ledge. His two brothers and his sister had already flown 
away the day before. He had been afraid to fly with them. Somehow when he had taken a little 
run forward to the brink of the ledge and attempted to flap his wings he became afraid. 
The great expanse of sea stretched down beneath, and it was such a long way down — miles down. 
He felt certain that his wings would never support him; so he bent his head and ran away back 
to the little hole under the ledge where he slept at night.
Even when each of his brothers and his little sister, whose wings were far shorter than his own, 
ran to the brink, flapped their wings, and flew away, he failed to muster up courage to take 
that plunge which appeared to him so desperate."
```

* **Glossary & Meanings (कठिन शब्दार्थ):**
  - **Ledge:** A narrow horizontal shelf projecting from a wall or cliff (चट्टान का उभरा हुआ किनारा).
  - **Brink:** The extreme edge of land before a steep drop (कगार / किनारा).
  - **Expanse:** A wide, continuous area of land or water (विशाल फैलाव).
  - **Muster up:** Gather / summon up with effort (हिम्मत जुटाना).
  - **Plunge:** A sudden dive or jump from a high place (छलांग लगाना).
* **Text-based practice questions and suggested answers:**
  1. **Why was the young seagull alone on the ledge?**
     - *Answer:* He was alone because his brothers and sister had already flown away the previous day, while he had been terrified to fly with them.
  2. **What convinced the young seagull not to fly?**
     - *Answer:* The vast expanse of the deep sea miles beneath him convinced him that his wings would never support his weight.
  3. **How did his siblings compare to him in terms of wing size?**
     - *Answer:* His brothers and sister had wings that were far shorter than his own, yet they flew confidently.
  4. **Find a phrase in the passage that means 'gather or collect courage'.**
     - *Answer:* Muster up courage.
  5. **Where did the young seagull sleep at night?**
     - *Answer:* In a little hole under the ledge.

### 📖 Extract 2: Maddened by Hunger — The Leap of Faith (Story I)
```text
"He waited a moment in surprise, wondering why she did not come nearer, and then, maddened 
by hunger, he dived at the fish. With a loud scream he fell outwards and downwards into space. 
Then a monstrous terror seized him and his heart stood still. He could hear nothing. But it 
only lasted a minute. The next moment he felt his wings spread outwards. The wind rushed 
against his breast feathers, then under his stomach, and against his wings. He could feel 
the tips of his wings cutting through the air. He was not falling headlong now. He was soaring 
gradually downwards and outwards. He was no longer afraid."
```

* **Glossary & Meanings (कठिन शब्दार्थ):**
  - **Maddened by hunger:** Driven crazy by extreme starvation (भूख से बावला हो जाना).
  - **Monstrous terror:** Huge, overpowering fear (अति-भयानक आतंक).
  - **Seized:** Gripped tightly (जकड़ लिया).
  - **Soaring:** Flying high in the air without flapping hard (हवा में ऊपर उठना/उड़ना).
  - **Headlong:** Falling with head first / diving uncontrollably (सिर के बल गिरना).
* **Text-based practice questions and suggested answers:**

     - *Answer:* He was driven mad by extreme hunger when he saw the fish in his mother's beak, which made him dive blindly at the food.
  2. **What happened immediately after he fell into space?**
     - *Answer:* A monstrous terror gripped him and his heart stood still, but this paralyzed fear lasted only for about a minute.
  3. **How did he realize he was flying rather than plummeting to death?**
     - *Answer:* He felt his wings spreading outward, the wind rushing against his breast feathers, and the tips of his wings slicing through the air.
  4. **Find the word in the passage that means 'flying gracefully upward or through air'.**
     - *Answer:* Soaring.
  5. **What emotional change occurred in the young seagull at the end of the passage?**
     - *Answer:* His overpowering fear vanished completely and was replaced by the joyful thrill of flight.

### 📖 Extract 3: Flying the Old Dakota into the Black Storm (Story II)
```text
"Paris was about 150 kilometres behind me when I saw the clouds. Storm clouds. They were huge. 
They looked like black mountains standing in front of me across the sky. I knew I could not fly 
up and over them, and I did not have enough fuel to fly around them to the north or south.
'I ought to go back to Paris,' I thought, but I wanted to get home. I wanted that breakfast.
'I'll take the risk,' I thought, and flew that old Dakota straight into the storm.
Inside the clouds, everything was suddenly black. It was impossible to see anything outside 
the aeroplane. The old aeroplane jumped and twisted in the air. I looked at the compass. 
I couldn't believe my eyes: the compass was turning round and round and round. It was dead. 
It would not work. The other instruments were suddenly dead, too. I tried the radio."
```

* **Glossary & Meanings (कठिन शब्दार्थ):**
  - **Storm clouds:** Ominous, heavy rain clouds (तूफानी बादल).
  - **Huge:** Enormous / gigantic (विशालकाय).
  - **Instruments:** Measuring gauges like compass, altimeter, and speedometer (विमान के यंत्र).
  - **Dead:** Ceased to function (खराब हो गए / बंद पड़ गए).
  - **Twisted:** Turned sharply and violently (हवा में हिचकोले खाना).
* **Text-based practice questions and suggested answers:**
  1. **What did the storm clouds look like to the pilot?**
     - *Answer:* The storm clouds looked like gigantic black mountains standing across the sky.
  2. **Why didn't the pilot fly around the storm clouds?**
     - *Answer:* He did not have enough fuel left in his tanks to fly around them to the north or south.
  3. **Why did the pilot decide to take the risk instead of returning to Paris?**
     - *Answer:* He was desperate to reach home to celebrate the holiday and enjoy an English breakfast with his family.
  4. **What happened to the instruments inside the storm?**
     - *Answer:* The compass turned round and round and went dead, followed by the failure of all other instruments including the radio.
  5. **Which airplane was the narrator flying?**
     - *Answer:* The narrator was flying an old Dakota with the call-sign DS 088.

```text

I went and asked a woman in the control centre where I was and who the other pilot was.
```

| ❌ Common Mistake (छात्रों की सामान्य गलती) | ⚠️ Possible issue (no fixed deduction established) | ✅ Correct Board-Standard Answer (सही उत्तर) |
|---|---|---|
| Attributing 'The Black Aeroplane' to Liam O'Flaherty. | This confuses the authors; no fixed deduction is established. | *His First Flight* is by **Liam O'Flaherty**; *The Black Aeroplane* is by **Frederick Forsyth**. |
| Writing that the young seagull's father pushed him off the ledge. | Factual error. This differs from the story. | The **mother** flew close with a fish; maddened by hunger, the chick **dived on his own**. |
| Stating that the black aeroplane had lights on its wings. | Contradicts the text's description. | The narrator says it had **no lights on its wings**. |
| Claiming to know exactly who or what the black plane was. | The text leaves the identity unexplained. | Present any explanation as an interpretation, not a confirmed fact. |
| Forgetting the call-sign of the Dakota. | Evaluators look for the exact identifier. | The aircraft was the **Old Dakota DS 088**. |
| Writing that the narrator was flying from England to France. | Inverts the direction of flight. | He was flying **from France (Paris) to England**. |
| Missing the fish species. | Textual vocabulary matters for high scores. | The fish mentioned are **herring** and **dogfish**. |

  - **The Peril:** Flew into storm clouds; compass, radio and other instruments failed, and fuel was running low.
  - **The Mystery:** Black plane with no wing lights guided him to safety; the woman said the Dakota was the only plane she could see on radar.
* **Key Vocabulary for Evaluators:** *Ledge, brink, muster up courage, monstrous terror, soaring, dogfish, Old Dakota DS 088, black mountains, compass dead, radar control room.*

---

### 🎯 Practice Bank Complete Answer Key
* **Section A (MCQs):** 1-(B), 2-(B), 3-(B), 4-(B), 5-(B), 6-(B), 7-(C), 8-(B), 9-(B), 10-(B).
* **Section B (Blanks):** 11-courage, 12-beak, 13-family, 14-dead, 15-half an, 16-float.
* **Section C (Short Answers):** Evaluated as provided in Section C above.
* **Section D (Long Answers):** Evaluated per structured criteria (Comparative Theme & Psychological Analysis).

---

### 🏆 10-Mark Self Assessment Test (Time: 15 Minutes)

1. **Who wrote 'His First Flight'?**
2. **What food did the mother seagull offer to trick the young seagull?**
3. **Why did the Dakota pilot refuse to turn back to Paris?**
4. **What happened to the instruments inside the storm clouds?**
5. **What did the woman in the radar control centre reveal to the pilot, and what mystery did it create?**

#### 🎯 Complete Scoring Guide & Marking Scheme:
- **Q1 (1M):** Liam O'Flaherty.
- **Q2 (1M):** A piece of fish / dogfish.
- **Q3 (2M):** Longed to reach home in England (1M) + Wanted to enjoy a grand English breakfast with family (1M).
- **Q4 (2M):** Compass turned round and round and went dead (1M) + Radio and all other navigation instruments failed completely (1M).
- **Q5 (4M):** Woman revealed no other plane was flying; his was the only plane visible on radar (2M) + Created the mystery of who the pilot of the black plane was and how he vanished (2M).
