chapters.title: The Making of a Scientist — Chapter 6

content.value:
**Book:** *Footprints Without Feet* (Supplementary Reader)  
**Author:** Robert W. Peterson  
**Class:** 10 (English)  
**Source checked:** NCERT, 2026–27 reprint, [Chapter 6 PDF](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/jefp106.pdf)
Accurate chapter summary

The chapter traces Richard H. Ebright’s development from a child who collected butterflies and other objects to a student conducting experiments. His mother encouraged his curiosity, helped him find activities and bought him learning equipment. A children’s book, *The Travels of Monarch X*, introduced him to monarch migration research. His mother contacted Dr Frederick A. Urquhart, and Ebright began tagging monarchs.

In seventh grade he lost a science fair with microscope slides of frog tissues. He concluded that a display alone was not a real experiment. Subsequent projects investigated a disease affecting monarch caterpillars, the proposed resemblance between viceroy and monarch butterflies, and the function of gold spots on monarch pupae. The chapter describes later work with a fellow student on cells grown from monarch wings and a theory about how cells read DNA. It also notes Ebright’s debating, public speaking, canoeing and nature photography. The textbook identifies curiosity, a first-rate mind, and the desire to do one’s best for the right reasons as ingredients in becoming a scientist.
Text-based facts

| Point | What the chapter reports |
|---|---|
| Early interests | Butterfly, rock, fossil and coin collecting; astronomy and star-gazing. |
| Mother’s support | She encouraged learning, arranged activities and trips, obtained equipment, and wrote to Dr Urquhart after reading *The Travels of Monarch X*. |
| Seventh-grade fair | Ebright displayed frog-tissue slides under a microscope and did not win; he learned that a project should involve a real experiment. |
| Caterpillar disease project | He tested whether beetles might carry a disease, but reports getting no real results. |
| Viceroy project | The chapter describes his project testing whether birds would eat monarchs and records its fair placement. It says later research by others suggested viceroys probably copy monarchs. |
| Gold spots | The chapter says Ebright and another student built a device to show the spots produced a hormone needed for the butterfly’s full development. |
| Cell research | The chapter describes experiments with monarch-wing cells and a theory about how a cell reads DNA; it does not say Ebright discovered DNA or independently proved the theory. |
| Other activities | Debating, public speaking, canoeing and nature photography. |
Interpretation, kept separate from fact

The chapter presents curiosity, persistence, careful experimentation and support from others as important to Ebright’s development. Its closing “ingredients” are the author’s summary of the profile, not a complete scientific formula or a guarantee that anyone who has them will become a scientist. Scientific milestones above are reported as the textbook presents them; this study note does not independently reassess the current state of butterfly or cell biology.
Practice questions

These are study questions, not verified predictions about the RBSE examination.

1. **How did *The Travels of Monarch X* influence Ebright?**  
   It introduced him to monarch migration and invited readers to help with research by tagging butterflies.

2. **What did Ebright learn from losing the seventh-grade science fair?**  
   He realized that a neat display was not enough; he needed to conduct a real experiment.

3. **What did Ebright investigate about the gold spots on a monarch pupa?**  
   He investigated their function. The chapter reports that his team showed they produced a hormone needed for the butterfly’s full development.

4. **What qualities does the chapter associate with becoming a scientist?**  
   It names a first-rate mind, curiosity and the will to do one’s best for the right reasons.
Corrections made in this review

- Removed “revolutionary paper on cell theory”; the chapter describes a theory about how cells work and how a cell reads DNA, not a new cell theory.
- Corrected oversimplifications of the viceroy project: Ebright tested an explanation; the chapter attributes the later conclusion that viceroys probably copy monarchs to subsequent research by others.
- Removed claims that Ebright discovered DNA, conclusively established a modern biological law, or succeeded solely through innate genius.
- Kept the scientific-history details explicitly attributed to the textbook and removed unsupported author/mentor embellishments, exam predictions and scoring guarantees.

chapters.title: The Necklace — Chapter 7

content.value:
**Book:** *Footprints Without Feet* (Supplementary Reader)  
**Author:** Guy de Maupassant  
**Class:** 10 (English)  
**Source checked:** NCERT, 2026–27 reprint, [Chapter 7 PDF](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/jefp107.pdf)
Accurate chapter summary

Matilda Loisel is unhappy with her modest home and longs for luxury. Her husband brings home an invitation to a minister’s ball. She says she has no suitable dress; he gives her the 400 francs he had saved for a gun. Still unhappy about having no jewellery, Matilda borrows a diamond necklace from her wealthy friend Mme Forestier.

Matilda enjoys the ball and notices the admiration she receives. When she and her husband return home, she discovers that the necklace is missing. They search and try to trace the cab without success. They buy a replacement necklace for 36,000 francs; its shop valuation was 40,000 francs. Her husband uses 18,000 francs inherited from his father and borrows the rest. The Loisels spend ten years repaying the debt. When Matilda eventually tells Mme Forestier what happened, Forestier says the original necklace was imitation jewellery worth no more than 500 francs.
Text-based facts

| Point | What the text says |
|---|---|
| Invitation | A minister and Madame George Ramponneau invite the Loisels to a ball on Monday evening, January 18. No year is given. |
| Dress money | Matilda asks for 400 francs; her husband gives her the amount he had saved for a hunting gun. |
| Borrowed necklace | Mme Forestier lends Matilda a diamond necklace from her jewel case. |
| Loss | Matilda discovers it is missing after they return from the ball; the couple cannot find it. |
| Replacement | They pay 36,000 francs for a necklace valued at 40,000 francs. |
| Repayment | The Loisels spend ten years repaying the debt. |
| Twist | Mme Forestier says her original necklace was false and worth no more than 500 francs. |
Interpretation, kept separate from fact

The ending creates dramatic irony: the Loisels sacrifice ten years to replace an imitation necklace, while Matilda’s friend had not told her it was false. Matilda’s longing for luxury and the couple’s decision to conceal the loss shape the plot, but broad claims that the story proves a single moral about wealth, vanity or contentment are interpretations rather than stated facts.
Practice questions

These are study questions, not verified predictions about the RBSE examination.

1. **Why does Matilda borrow a necklace?**  
   She has a suitable dress but feels she has no jewellery to wear to the minister’s ball, so she borrows one from Mme Forestier.

2. **How do the Loisels replace the necklace?**  
   They buy a similar necklace for 36,000 francs, using 18,000 francs that Mr Loisel had inherited and borrowing the rest.

3. **How long do the Loisels take to repay the debt?**  
   The text says that their difficult life lasts ten years, by the end of which they have repaid everything.

4. **What does Mme Forestier reveal at the end?**  
   She says her original necklace was imitation jewellery worth no more than 500 francs.
Corrections made in this review

- Kept the invitation date as January 18 without inventing a year.
- Distinguished the replacement’s 40,000-franc valuation from the 36,000 francs paid; kept the original necklace’s value as “not over five hundred francs,” as in the text.
- Removed unsupported details about the exact borrowing terms, interest rate and specific lenders beyond the text’s reference to usurers and lenders.
- Removed deterministic moral lessons, invented exam predictions and score guarantees.

chapters.title: Bholi — Chapter 8

content.value:
**Book:** *Footprints Without Feet* (Supplementary Reader)  
**Author:** K. A. Abbas  
**Class:** 10 (English)  
**Source checked:** NCERT, 2026–27 reprint, [Chapter 8 PDF](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/jefp108.pdf)
Accurate chapter summary

Bholi’s given name is Sulekha. As a child she falls from a cot, and at age two she has smallpox that leaves pockmarks. She begins speaking at five and stammers; other children mock her, and she speaks little. When a girls’ primary school opens in the village, the Tehsildar tells her father, Ramlal, to send his daughters. Ramlal’s wife suggests sending Bholi because she thinks the other daughters’ marriage prospects could be affected by schooling.

At school, Bholi is frightened and cannot say her name at first. Her teacher speaks gently, encourages her, and gives her a picture book. Bholi begins to feel hopeful. Years pass; the village school becomes a high school. Ramlal and his wife agree to Bholi’s marriage to Bishamber Nath, a prosperous grocer who is older, limps and has grown children from his first marriage. When Bishamber sees Bholi’s pockmarks, he demands 5,000 rupees. Ramlal pays. Bholi then refuses to marry him, asks her father to take back the money, and says she will teach at the school that taught her. Her teacher supports her decision.
Text-based facts

| Point | What the story says |
|---|---|
| Birth name | Sulekha; “Bholi” is the name people have used since childhood. |
| Speech and appearance | She stammers and has pockmarks from smallpox. The story connects her learning difficulties to a fall from a cot, but describes this as a possibility (“perhaps”), not a medically confirmed diagnosis. |
| Why she is sent to school | The Tehsildar urges Ramlal to send his daughters; Ramlal’s wife proposes Bholi because she expects less from her marriage prospects. |
| Teacher | Encourages Bholi kindly, helps her say her name, and gives her a picture book. |
| Bishamber | A well-to-do grocer, older than Bholi, limps and has grown children from his first wife. |
| Dowry demand | At the wedding, Bishamber demands 5,000 rupees after seeing her pockmarks. Ramlal pays it; Bholi rejects the marriage and tells him to take the money back. |
| Ending | Bholi says she will care for her parents in their old age and teach at the school. |
Interpretation, kept separate from fact

The story links education and the teacher’s encouragement with Bholi’s growing confidence. Her refusal of the marriage is an assertion of choice in the face of humiliation and a dowry demand. The story does not provide a clinical diagnosis for her learning or speech differences, nor does it establish that schooling alone cures stammering: the wedding scene occurs years later, and the text presents her speech as clear at that moment.
Practice questions

These are study questions, not verified predictions about the RBSE examination.

1. **Why does Bholi’s teacher matter to her?**  
   The teacher treats her kindly, encourages her to speak, and gives her a picture book. Bholi begins to feel hopeful about learning.

2. **Why do Bholi’s parents accept Bishamber’s proposal?**  
   They think he is well-to-do and that he is not asking for dowry. They also believe Bholi may have few other marriage prospects.

3. **Why does Bholi reject the marriage?**  
   Bishamber demands 5,000 rupees after seeing her pockmarks. Bholi refuses to marry a man she calls mean and greedy, and asks her father to take the money back.

4. **What does Bholi say she will do after refusing the marriage?**  
   She tells her father that she will care for him and her mother in their old age and teach at the school.
Corrections made in this review

- Preserved the text’s uncertainty (“perhaps”) about the head injury; removed asserted medical diagnoses and claims that the fall is established as the cause of a disability.
- Corrected the marriage sequence: Bishamber first says he wants five thousand rupees; Ramlal pays; Bholi then rejects the marriage and tells him to take back the money.
- Removed claims that Bholi’s stammer is simply cured by education or that the wedding scene alone proves its medical cause.
- Removed absolute moral formulas, invented exam predictions, fixed mark allocations and score guarantees.

chapters.title: The Book That Saved the Earth — Chapter 9

content.value:
**Book:** *Footprints Without Feet* (Supplementary Reader)  
**Playwright:** Claire Boiko  
**Class:** 10 (English)  
**Source checked:** NCERT, 2026–27 reprint, [Chapter 9 PDF](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/jefp109.pdf)
Accurate play summary

The play is framed by a Historian in the twenty-fifth century, who recounts a fictional Martian invasion attempt in 2040. Think-Tank, Mars’s self-important commander, sends Captain Omega, Lieutenant Iota and Sergeant Oop to Earth. They enter the Centerville Public Library but mistake it for a storage place and its books for sandwiches. Think-Tank misinterprets nursery rhymes in a copy of *Mother Goose* as evidence of Earth’s power and a threat to Mars.

The crew first reads “Mistress Mary” as evidence that Earthlings can grow metals and explosives. Think-Tank then interprets “Hey Diddle Diddle” as showing that Earth’s animals have advanced culture and could attack with millions of cows. The “Humpty Dumpty” rhyme and illustration make him think Earthlings have discovered his appearance and plan to capture him. He orders the invasion called off and flees with the Martian forces. The Historian says that, centuries later, Earth and Mars become friendly, Noodle replaces Think-Tank, and Earth teaches the Martians to read. The Martians still avoid *Mother Goose*.
Text-based facts

| Point | What the play says |
|---|---|
| Frame setting | The Historian speaks from the twenty-fifth century and describes the twentieth century as the “Era of the Book.” |
| Invasion attempt | The play’s account is set in 2040; Think-Tank plans an invasion of Earth. |
| Earth location | The crew enters the Centerville Public Library. |
| Crew | Captain Omega, Lieutenant Iota and Sergeant Oop; Noodle is Think-Tank’s apprentice at Mars Space Control. |
| *Mother Goose* | The Martians mistake it for a “sandwich” and misread the nursery rhymes as reports or codes. |
| Outcome | Think-Tank calls off the invasion and orders the Martians to leave Earth; later contact between Earth and Mars is friendly. |
| Later history in the frame | The Historian says Noodle has replaced Think-Tank and the Martians have been taught to read. |
Interpretation, kept separate from fact

The play uses mistaken readings of books and Think-Tank’s vanity for comic effect. Noodle often corrects him tactfully, while Think-Tank repeatedly takes credit for Noodle’s suggestions. The title’s “saved the Earth” claim is part of this fictional comic frame; the play is not a historical account or evidence about real extraterrestrial life.
Practice questions

These are study questions, not verified predictions about the RBSE examination.

1. **Why do the Martians call books sandwiches?**  
   They find books in a library but do not understand what books are, so Think-Tank mistakes them for food.

2. **How does “Mistress Mary” alarm Think-Tank?**  
   He misunderstands its mention of cockle shells, silver bells and maids as proof that Earthlings can grow metals and explosives.

3. **What does Think-Tank infer from “Humpty Dumpty”?**  
   Seeing the illustration, he thinks it resembles his own large head and concludes Earthlings know what he looks like and plan to capture him.

4. **How does the book save Earth in the play?**  
   Think-Tank’s misreading of the rhymes makes him fear Earth’s supposed power, so he cancels the invasion and orders the Martians away.
Corrections made in this review

- Confirmed the playwright as Claire Boiko and retained the play’s fictional 2040 invasion attempt and twenty-fifth-century frame.
- Corrected any suggestion that the Martians correctly understand books, nursery rhymes or Earth technology; their readings are comic misinterpretations.
- Kept the “sandwich” and “code” ideas as Think-Tank’s mistakes, not narrator-approved explanations.
- Removed unsupported claims about actual history, real extraterrestrial life, fixed exam formats, score guarantees and guaranteed questions.

chapters.title: RBSE Class 10 English Grammar: Unit 1 — Tenses (Correct Form of the Verbs)

content.value: माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर (कक्षा 10वीं — अंग्रेजी अनिवार्य)

### 🎯 पाठ्यक्रम भार: Tenses के लिए 2 अंक (2026–27 RBSE syllabus)

---
🧭 1. Current syllabus scope and practice guidance

RBSE 2026–27 English grammar syllabus में Tenses के लिए 2 अंक निर्धारित है। प्रश्न का सटीक रूप syllabus में तय नहीं है; grammar के चारों क्षेत्रों को gap-filling, editing या transformation के माध्यम से परखा जा सकता है।
- **अभ्यास स्वरूप:** क्रिया का सही रूप भरने और वाक्य-संदर्भ से tense पहचानने का अभ्यास करें। प्रश्न में दिए निर्देशों और वाक्य के अर्थ को प्राथमिकता दें।
- **अभ्यास संकेत:** *usually, yesterday, already, tomorrow, since/for, while, before/after,* और *by next year* संकेत दे सकते हैं, पर अकेले इनसे tense तय नहीं होता।

---
⚡ 2. Reference Table: 12 Tenses and Common Time Expressions

नीचे दी गई तालिका पारंपरिक 12-tense शिक्षण-ढाँचे का संक्षिप्त संदर्भ है। समय-सूचक शब्द अकेले tense तय नहीं करते; पूरे वाक्य का अर्थ और संदर्भ देखें:

| क्र. सं. | काल (Tense) | सहायक क्रिया (Helping Verb) | मुख्य क्रिया (Main Verb) | संभावित समय-सूचक शब्द (Time Expressions; Check Context) |
|:---:|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Present Simple** | `do / does` (नकारात्मक/प्रश्नवाचक) | \(V_1\) या \(V_1 + s/es\) (तीसरे पुरुष एकवचन के साथ) | *always, usually, generally, normally, often, frequently, daily, regularly, seldom, rarely, never, hardly, scarcely, every day/week/month/year, once a week, on Sundays*, सार्वभौमिक सत्य (Universal truth), वैज्ञानिक नियम, कहावतें। |
| **2** | **Present Continuous** | `is / am / are` | \(V_1 + ing\) (\(V_4\)) | *now, still, at present, at this moment, at this time, nowadays, these days, look!, listen!, hurry up!, keep quiet!* |
| **3** | **Present Perfect** | `has / have` | \(V_3\) (Past Participle) | *already, just, yet (नकारात्मक/प्रश्न में), recently, lately, so far, up to now, ever* (संदर्भानुसार)। *Just now* सामान्यतः past simple के साथ आता है। |
| **4** | **Present Perfect Continuous** | `has been / have been` | \(V_1 + ing\) + `since / for` + Time | *since / for* + समय (परन्तु वाक्य में भूतकाल का कोई अन्य संकेत न हो), *all morning, all day*. |
| **5** | **Past Simple (Indefinite)** | `did` (नकारात्मक/प्रश्नवाचक) | \(V_2\) (सकारात्मक में), \(V_1\) (`did` के बाद) | *yesterday, ago, last night/week/month/year, in 1947 (बीता हुआ वर्ष), the other day, once, that day, just now*; *as soon as* का tense पूरे वाक्य के संदर्भ से तय करें। |
| **6** | **Past Continuous** | `was / were` | \(V_1 + ing\) | *at that time, at that moment, those days, while, as, when* (जब एक कार्य चल रहा था और दूसरा घटित हुआ). |
| **7** | **Past Perfect** | `had` | \(V_3\) | *before, after, by the time, when* (दो भूतकालीन घटनाओं का संयोजन; जो कार्य पहले समाप्त हुआ = `had + V3`). |
| **8** | **Past Perfect Continuous** | `had been` | \(V_1 + ing\) + `since/for` + Past marker | *since / for* + समय + भूतकाल का संदर्भ (जैसे: *when I met him, yesterday, in those days*). |
| **9** | **Future Simple** | `will / shall` | \(V_1\) | *tomorrow, next day/week/month/year, the coming week, in a few days, soon, shortly, in 2030 (भविष्य का वर्ष)*. |
| **10** | **Future Continuous** | `will be / shall be` | \(V_1 + ing\) | *at this time tomorrow, at this moment next week, tomorrow morning*. |
| **11** | **Future Perfect** | `will have / shall have` | \(V_3\) | *by + भविष्य का समय* (उदा. *by tomorrow, by next Monday, by 5 o'clock, by next year, by the end of this month*). |
| **12** | **Future Perfect Continuous** | `will have been / shall have been`| \(V_1 + ing\) | *by + भविष्य का समय + for / since + समय* (उदा. *by next June, he will have been teaching for 10 years*). |

---
🔍 3. Tense-by-Tense Comprehensive Breakdown & High-Yield Rules

### 📘 Unit 1.1: Present Simple Tense (सामान्य वर्तमान काल)
- **संरचना (Structure):**
  - Affirmative: $\text{Subject} + V_1 / (V_1 + s/es) + \text{Object/Other}$
    * *Subject Singular (He, She, It, Singular Noun)* $\rightarrow V_1 + s/es$
    * *I / You / We / They / Plural Noun* $\rightarrow V_1$
  - Negative: $\text{Subject} + \text{do/does} + \text{not} + V_1 + \text{Object}$
  - **अपवाद/सीमा:** ऊपर की do/does संरचना सामान्य lexical verbs के लिए है। *Be* के रूप *am/is/are* सीधे नकारात्मक/प्रश्न बनाते हैं (*She is not late; Is she late?*); modals भी अलग संरचना लेते हैं। *I* एकवचन है और *you* एक/बहुवचन हो सकता है, फिर भी इनमें lexical verb पर third-person *s* नहीं लगता।
  - Interrogative: $\text{Do/Does} + \text{Subject} + V_1 + \text{Object}?$
- **High-Yield Board Rules:**
  1. **Rule 1 (Habitual / Repeated Action):** *Always, never, often, seldom, usually, generally, daily,* और *every day/month* अक्सर आदत या सामान्य स्थिति दिखाते हैं; tense संदर्भ से तय करें।
     * *Example:* My father **goes** (go) for a morning walk daily.
     * *Example:* Sneha usually **takes** (take) tea in the morning.
  2. **Rule 2 (Universal Truth / Scientific Fact / General Principles):**
     * *The sun* **rises** (rise) in the east and **sets** (set) in the west. (सार्वभौमिक सत्य)
     * *Pure water* **boils** (boil) at about $100^\circ\text{C}$ at normal atmospheric pressure. (वैज्ञानिक तथ्य)
     * *Two and two* **make** (make) four. (गणितीय सत्य)
  3. **Rule 3 (Proverbs / Idiomatic Truths):**
     * *A bad workman* **quarrels** (quarrel) with his tools.
     * *Barking dogs* **seldom** bite.
  4. **Rule 4 (Fixed Timetable / Official Programme in Near Future):**
     * *The Prime Minister* **visits** (visit) Jaipur tomorrow.
     * *The school* **reopens** (reopen) on 1st July.

---

### 📗 Unit 1.2: Present Continuous Tense (अपूर्ण वर्तमान काल)
- **संरचना (Structure):**
  - Affirmative: $\text{Subject} + \text{is/am/are} + (V_1 + ing) + \text{Object}$
    * *He/She/It/Singular* $\rightarrow \text{is}$ | *I* $\rightarrow \text{am}$ | *We/You/They/Plural* $\rightarrow \text{are}$
- **High-Yield Board Rules:**
  1. **Rule 1 (Actions Happening at the Time of Speaking):**
     * Adverbials: *now, at present, at this time, at this moment, nowadays, these days, currently*.
     * *Example:* The children **are playing** (play) in the garden now.
     * *Example:* What **are** you **doing** (do) at this moment?
  2. **Rule 2 (Action in progress):** *Look!* या *Listen!* के बाद जारी क्रिया को अक्सर Present Continuous में व्यक्त किया जाता है; ये शब्द अपने-आप tense तय नहीं करते।
     * *Example:* Look! The bus **is coming** (come).
     * *Example:* Listen! Someone **is knocking** (knock) at the door.
     * *Example:* Keep quiet! The baby **is sleeping** (sleep).
  3. **Rule 3 (Stative verbs):** कुछ क्रियाएँ सामान्यतः continuous रूप में नहीं आतीं, जब वे अवस्था या भाव बताती हैं (जैसे *know, believe, own, belong*)। कई क्रियाएँ अर्थ के अनुसार state या action बता सकती हैं; इसलिए इसे पूर्ण निषेध न मानें।
     * ❌ *Incorrect:* I am knowing him very well.
     * ✔️ *Correct:* I **know** him very well.

---

### 📙 Unit 1.3: Present Perfect Tense (पूर्ण वर्तमान काल)
- **संरचना (Structure):**
  - Affirmative: $\text{Subject} + \text{has/have} + V_3 + \text{Object}$
    * *He/She/It/Singular* $\rightarrow \text{has}$ | *I/We/You/They/Plural* $\rightarrow \text{have}$
- **High-Yield Board Rules:**
  1. **Rule 1 (Recently Completed Actions with Present Relevance):**
     * Adverbials: *already, just, recently, lately, yet, so far, up to now, ever*; *just now* प्रायः past simple के साथ आता है।
     * *Example:* The train **has already left** (already leave) the platform.
     * *Example:* He **has just finished** (just finish) his homework.
     * *Example:* The postman **has not come** (not come) yet. (*yet* का प्रयोग नकारात्मक/प्रश्नवाचक वाक्यों में होता है)।
     * *Example:* Have you ever **visited** (visit) the Taj Mahal?

---

### 📕 Unit 1.4: Present Perfect Continuous Tense (पूर्णापूर्ण वर्तमान काल)
- **संरचना (Structure):**
  - Affirmative: $\text{Subject} + \text{has/have} + \text{been} + (V_1 + ing) + \text{Object} + \text{since/for} + \text{Time}$
- **Since vs For (काल चुनने के लिए पूरा वाक्य देखें):**
  - **Since (Point of Time - निश्चित समय बिन्दु):**
    * घड़ी का समय: *since 4 o'clock, since 7:30 a.m.*
    * वार व माह: *since Monday, since July*
    * वर्ष: *since 1995, since 2020*
    * दिन के प्रहर: *since morning, since evening, since noon, since midnight*
    * जीवन की अवस्थाएं / घटनाएं: *since childhood, since his birth, since yesterday*
  - **For (Period of Time - समयावधि):**
    * गिनती वाले घंटे/दिन/महीने/वर्ष: *for two hours, for five days, for three months, for ten years, for a long time, for several weeks*.
- **अभ्यास संकेत:**
  * *Since/for* अवधि की शुरुआत/अवधि बताते हैं, लेकिन अपने-आप Present Perfect Continuous तय नहीं करते। चल रही क्रिया के लिए यह tense सामान्य है; अवस्था बताने वाली क्रियाओं के साथ Present Perfect Simple भी आ सकता है, जैसे *I have known her since childhood*।
  * *Example:* She **has been reading** (read) this novel for two hours.
  * *Example:* It **has been raining** (rain) since morning.

---

### 📓 Unit 1.5: Past Simple (Indefinite) Tense (सामान्य भूतकाल)
- **संरचना (Structure):**
  - Affirmative: $\text{Subject} + V_2 + \text{Object}$
  - Negative: $\text{Subject} + \text{did not} + V_1 + \text{Object}$ (सावधान: `did` के बाद हमेशा $V_1$ आता है!)
  - Interrogative: $\text{Did} + \text{Subject} + V_1 + \text{Object}?$
- **High-Yield Board Rules:**
  1. **Rule 1 (Past Time Indicators):**
     * Adverbials: *yesterday, ago, last night, last week, last month, last year, in ancient times, once, in 1947, on 15th August*.
     * *Example:* India **became** (become) independent in 1947.
     * *Example:* I **met** (meet) him three days ago.
     * *Example:* She **did not attend** (not attend) the class yesterday.
  2. **Rule 2 (Historical Events / Completed Past Deeds):**
     * *Example:* Alexander **invaded** (invade) India long ago.
     * *Example:* Columbus **reached** (reach) the Caribbean in 1492. (यहाँ पहले से बसे लोगों की भूमि को पहली बार खोज लेने का दावा नहीं है।)

---

### 📒 Unit 1.6: Past Continuous Tense (अपूर्ण भूतकाल)
- **संरचना (Structure):**
  - Affirmative: $\text{Subject} + \text{was/were} + (V_1 + ing) + \text{Object}$
    * *I/He/She/It/Singular* $\rightarrow \text{was}$ | *We/You/They/Plural* $\rightarrow \text{were}$
- **High-Yield Board Rules:**
  1. **Rule 1 (While / As Clauses - दो समानांतर कार्य):**
     * जब भूतकाल में दो जारी कार्यों पर जोर हो, तो दोनों में Past Continuous आ सकता है; यह *while* का अनिवार्य नियम नहीं है:
     * *Formula:* $\text{While} + \text{Subject} + \text{was/were} + V_4, \text{Subject} + \text{was/were} + V_4$
     * *Example:* While my mother **was cooking** (cook), I **was studying** (study).
  2. **Rule 2 (Interrupted Action: When / While Combination - अभ्यास उदाहरण):**
     * जब एक कार्य जारी था (\(\text{was/were} + V_4\)) और उसी बीच दूसरा कार्य अचानक घटित हो गया (\(V_2\)):
     * *Formula A:* $\text{When} + \text{Subject} + V_2, \text{Subject} + \text{was/were} + V_4$
     * *Formula B:* $\text{Subject} + \text{was/were} + V_4 + \text{when} + \text{Subject} + V_2$
     * *Example:* When the teacher entered the classroom, the students **were making** (make) a noise.
     * *Example:* I was watching TV when the telephone bell **rang** (ring).
     * *Example:* While he **was crossing** (cross) the road, a speeding car knocked him down.

### 📓 Unit 1.7: Past Perfect Tense (पूर्ण भूतकाल — The Golden "Before / After" Rules)
Past Perfect किसी बीते समय से पहले की घटना/स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। वार्षिक प्रश्न-आवृत्ति का प्रमाणित paper register यहाँ नहीं है।

#### 🏆 Golden Rule 1: 'Before' Pattern
भूतकाल में यदि दो कार्य एक के बाद एक हुए हों, तो पहले कार्य की पूर्वता पर जोर देने के लिए $\text{had} + V_3$ और बाद वाले के लिए $V_2$ लिया जा सकता है। *Before/after* से क्रम स्पष्ट हो तो दोनों clauses में Past Simple भी संभव है; नीचे केवल एक उपयोगी pattern है।
$$\mathbf{\text{Subject} + \text{had} + V_3 \quad+\quad \text{BEFORE} \quad+\quad \text{Subject} + V_2}$$
- *Example 1:* The train **had left** (leave) before we reached the station.
- *Example 2:* The patient **had died** (die) before the doctor came.
- *Example 3:* The students **had finished** (finish) their paper before the bell rang.

#### 🏆 Golden Rule 2: 'After' Pattern
नीचे के pattern में 'after' clause में Past Perfect पूर्व घटना स्पष्ट करता है। *After* हर वाक्य में *had + V3* अनिवार्य नहीं करता:
$$\mathbf{\text{Subject} + V_2 \quad+\quad \text{AFTER} \quad+\quad \text{Subject} + \text{had} + V_3}$$
- *Example 1:* We reached the station after the train **had left** (leave).
- *Example 2:* The doctor came after the patient **had died** (die).
- *Example 3:* She went to bed after she **had locked** (lock) all the doors.

#### 🏆 Golden Rule 3: 'By the time' Pattern
$$\mathbf{\text{By the time} + \text{Subject} + V_2, \quad \text{Subject} + \text{had} + V_3}$$
- *Example:* By the time the police arrived, the thief **had escaped** (escape).

### 📘 Unit 1.8: Past Perfect Continuous Tense
- **संरचना (Structure):**
  - Affirmative: $\text{Subject} + \text{had been} + (V_1 + ing) + \text{Object} + \text{since/for} + \text{Time} + \text{Past Context}$
- **प्रयोग:** किसी बीते समय से पहले शुरू हुई जारी क्रिया/अवधि पर जोर हो तो Past Perfect Continuous उपयोगी है। *For/since* और past clause अपने-आप इसे तय नहीं करते; अवस्था/पूर्णता के लिए Past Perfect Simple भी संभव है:
  * *Example:* When I reached his home, he **had been sleeping** (sleep) for two hours.
  * *Example:* She **had been working** (work) in this bank for five years when she got married.

### 📙 Unit 1.9: Future Simple (Indefinite) Tense
- **संरचना (Structure):**
  - Affirmative: $\text{Subject} + \text{shall / will} + V_1 + \text{Object}$
    * पुरानी शिक्षण-परंपरा में *I/We* के साथ *shall* सिखाया जाता था। आधुनिक अंग्रेजी में *will* सभी persons के साथ सामान्य है; *shall* मुख्यतः औपचारिक प्रयोग तथा *Shall I/we ...?* जैसे प्रस्तावों में आता है। यह *I/We = shall* का अनिवार्य नियम नहीं है।
- **Adverbials:** *tomorrow, next week/month/year, soon, shortly, in a few days, coming Monday*.
  * *Example:* We **shall celebrate** (celebrate) our school annual day next week.
  * *Example:* My brother **will buy** (buy) a new laptop tomorrow.

---

### 📗 Unit 1.10: Future Continuous Tense
- **संरचना:** $\text{Subject} + \text{will be / shall be} + (V_1 + ing) + \text{Object}$
- **Adverbials:** *at this time tomorrow, at this moment next week, tomorrow evening*.
  * *Example:* At this time tomorrow, we **shall be playing** (play) a cricket match.
  * *Example:* She **will be travelling** (travel) by train at this time next Monday.

---

### 📕 Unit 1.11: Future Perfect Tense (भविष्य के समय तक पूर्णता)
*By + future time* के साथ Future Perfect पूर्णता पर जोर दे सकता है। Future Simple भी संभव है, जैसे *I will finish by Friday*; इसलिए नीचे का सूत्र एक संभावित रूप है:
$$\mathbf{\text{BY} + \text{Future Time Point} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{will have / shall have} + V_3}$$
- **Clue Words:** *by tomorrow, by next Monday, by the end of this month, by next year, by 5 p.m., by 2030*.
- **Examples:**
  * *Example 1:* The carpenter **will have finished** (finish) the work by next evening.
  * *Example 2:* By the end of this month, our syllabus **will have been completed** (complete, passive). Active alternative: *we will have completed the syllabus*.
  * *Example 3:* She **will have returned** (return) home by 8 p.m.
  * *Example 4:* By next year, he **will have built** (build) his new house.

---

### 📓 Unit 1.12: Future Perfect Continuous Tense
- **संरचना:** $\text{will have been / shall have been} + (V_1 + ing) + \text{for/since} + \text{Time}$
- **Formula:** $\text{By} + \text{Future Time} + \text{for} + \text{Period of Time}$
  * *Example:* By next July, Mr. Sharma **will have been teaching** (teach) in this school for twenty years.

🎯 4. Conditional Sentences (शर्त सूचक वाक्य — अतिरिक्त व्याकरण अभ्यास)

नीचे चार सामान्य शिक्षण-पैटर्न (zero, first, second, third) हैं। ये सभी संभावित conditional structures या बोर्ड में पूछे जाने वाले प्रश्नों का प्रमाणित वर्गीकरण नहीं हैं: | Condition Type | 'If' Clause (शर्त वाला उपवाक्य) | Main Clause (मुख्य परिणामी उपवाक्य) | उदाहरण (Exam Archetype) | |---|---|---|---| | **Type 0 (Universal/Scientific)** | Present Simple ($V_1 / V_1+s/es$) | Present Simple ($V_1 / V_1+s/es$) | If you **heat** ice, it **melts**. | | **Type 1 (Probable / Open Condition)** | **Present Simple** ($V_1 / V_1+s/es$) | **will / shall / can / may + $V_1$** | If he **works** (work) hard, he **will pass** (pass) the exam. | | **Type 2 (Improbable / Hypothetical)** | **Past Simple** ($V_2$ / 'were') | **would / should / could / might + $V_1$** | If I **had** (have) wings, I **would fly** (fly) to you.
If I **were** (be) a bird, I would fly. | | **Type 3 (Impossible Past Condition)** | **Past Perfect** ($\text{had} + V_3$) | **would have / could have + $V_3$** | If you **had invited** (invite) me, I **would have attended** (attend) your party. | ### ⚠️ Trap Alert on Conditionals: - सामान्य भविष्य-शर्त में *if* clause में Present Simple लिया जाता है; पर इच्छा/तत्परता या विनम्र अनुरोध में *will/would* संभव हैं। जैसे *If you will help (= are willing to help), we can finish sooner.* यह पूर्ण निषेध नहीं है। * *सामान्य भविष्य-शर्त में अपेक्षित:* If you come, I will help you. (*If you will come* इच्छा/तत्परता के अलग अर्थ में संभव है।) * ✔️ *Correct:* If you **come** (come), I will help you. - *Unless* का अर्थ सामान्यतः *if ... not* है, इसलिए सामान्य positive condition में अतिरिक्त *not* अर्थ बदल देगा। लेकिन *until* समय बताता है और इसे negative clause के साथ लिया जा सकता है: *Do not leave until I return.* अतः *unless* और *until* को एक नियम न मानें: * *Example:* Unless you **run** (run) fast, you cannot catch the bus. - 'As soon as' के बाद यदि दोनों घटनाएं भविष्य की हों, तो पहले उपवाक्य में Present Simple और दूसरे में Future Simple आता है: * *Example:* As soon as the teacher **enters** (enter) the class, the students will stand up. ---
🚫 5. Mistake Busters: शीर्ष 8 गलतियाँ जिनसे छात्र अंक गंवाते हैं

1. **Mistake 1:** 'Since/For' देखते ही आंख मूंदकर 'has been/have been' भर देना बिना यह देखे कि आगे भूतकाल जुड़ा है या नहीं!
   * *Trap:* When I reached his office, he ______ (work) for three hours.
   * ❌ *Wrong:* has been working | ✔️ *Correct:* **had been working** (क्योंकि *reached* भूतकाल है)।
2. **Mistake 2:** 'Did not' के बाद $V_2$ लगा देना!
   * ❌ *Wrong:* He did not wrote a letter. | ✔️ *Correct:* He did not **write** a letter. (`did` के बाद सदैव $V_1$).
3. **Mistake 3:** 'Before' और 'After' के क्रम को उलट देना!
   * याद रखने का मंत्र: Past Perfect का संबंध पहले की घटना से है; *before/after* की जगह देखकर यांत्रिक रूप न भरें। क्रम पहले से स्पष्ट हो तो Past Simple भी सही हो सकता है।
4. **Mistake 4:** 'By + Time' में 'will + $V_1$' भर देना!
   * *By tomorrow* समय-सीमा है। *I will have finished by tomorrow* और *I will finish by tomorrow* दोनों संभव हैं; पहला पूर्णता पर जोर देता है।
5. **Mistake 5:** Subject-Verb में $s/es$ का भ्रम:
   * He, She, It, Ramesh $\rightarrow$ $V_1 + s/es$ (जैसे: *He writes*).
   * I, We, You, They $\rightarrow$ $V_1$ (जैसे: *They write*). 'I' के साथ $s/es$ कभी नहीं लगता!
6. **Mistake 6:** जारी क्रिया के संदर्भ की अनदेखी करना; *Look/Listen* खुद tense का नियम नहीं हैं:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* Look! It rains. | ✔️ *Correct:* Look! It **is raining**.
7. **Mistake 7:** 'Be' क्रिया का रूप न पहचान पाना:
   * कोष्ठक में दिया गया `(be)` $\rightarrow$ Present में `is/am/are`, Past में `was/were`, Perfect में `been` होता है।
   * *Example:* Water **is** (be) life. / Gandhiji **was** (be) a great leader.
8. **Mistake 8:** Conditional Type 3 में main clause को 'would + $V_1$' लिख देना:
   * If + had + $V_3$ $\rightarrow$ मुख्य उपवाक्य में **would/could/might have + $V_3$** जैसे रूप आ सकते हैं; main clause का अर्थ/modal देखें।

### 📝 Practice set (not authenticated past-paper questions):

   * **Answer:** **was reading**

2. The train ______ (already leave) before we reached the platform.
   * **Answer:** **had already left**
   * *कारण:* पूर्व घटना की पूर्णता पर जोर देने के लिए Past Perfect लिया गया है; *before* हर वाक्य में यह tense अनिवार्य नहीं करता।
3. Look! The stars ______ (shine) brightly in the sky.
   * **Answer:** **are shining**

4. My uncle ______ (buy) a new car next week.
   * **Answer:** **will buy**
   * *कारण:* 'next week' भविष्य काल (Future Simple) का समय-सूचक है।

🔑 Complete Answer Key with Explanatory Notes (Q1 – Q120)

### Set A Answers:

**Alternative-answer notes:** Q5 *have studied*, Q9 *has taught*, Q11 *use*, Q17 *has watered* (completed spell), Q25 *have ... waited*, Q29 *has learned/learnt* can be grammatical with suitable meanings. The listed continuous forms emphasise the ongoing activity. Q28 permits future reference via simple present, present continuous or *will*; the prompt does not force one form.
1. **speaks** (*always* $\rightarrow$ Present Simple, singular subject *He*)
2. **gives** (Universal truth / fact)
3. **is explaining** (*Keep quiet!* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
4. **has not finished** (*yet* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect negative)
5. **have been studying** (*for three years* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect Continuous)
6. **arrives** (*usually* $\rightarrow$ Present Simple)
7. **is running** (*Look!* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
8. **have already seen** (*already* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect)
9. **has been teaching** (*since 2010* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect Continuous)
10. **fly** (General truth, plural subject *Birds*)
11. **are using** (*Nowadays* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
12. **has just received** (*just* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect)
13. **has been raining** (*since last night* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect Continuous)
14. **tell** (*never* + plural subject *Honest people* $\rightarrow$ $V_1$)
15. **is making** (*Listen!* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
16. **have not seen** (*for a long time* + stative sense $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect)
17. **has been watering** (*for two hours* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect Continuous)
18. **floats** (Scientific law)
19. **are constructing** (*At present* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
20. **eaten** (*Have you ever* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect $V_3$)
21. **is crying** (*now* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
22. **bite** (Proverb $\rightarrow$ Present Simple)
23. **is writing** (*at this moment* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
24. **has already repaired** (*already* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect)
25. **have ... been waiting** (Present Perfect Continuous interrogative)
26. **is** (General fact, *be* verb $\rightarrow$ is)
27. **are ... making** (*today* with continuous sense $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
28. **addresses / is addressing / will address** (Scheduled event, arranged event or future announcement; verb is *address*, not *visit*.)
29. **has been learning** (*for six months* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect Continuous)
30. **favours** (Proverb)

### Set B Answers:

**Alternative-answer notes:** Q36 *lived* is possible for a past residence. In Q38, 43, 48, 53, 56 and 60, *before/after* already show the order, so the corresponding Past Simple can also work. Q46 *had waited* stresses the completed duration; Q51 *had been suffering* stresses the ongoing illness. The keys below show one conventional reading.
31. **won** (*in 1983* $\rightarrow$ Past Simple $V_2$)
32. **fell** (Action interrupted $\rightarrow$ Past Simple $V_2$ of fall)
33. **reached** (इस वाक्य में बाद की घटना का Past Simple $V_2$)
34. **did not go** (*yesterday* $\rightarrow$ Past Simple negative did not + $V_1$)
35. **had already begun** (Before/when past context $\rightarrow$ Past Perfect)
36. **were living** (*At that time* $\rightarrow$ Past Continuous)
37. **bought** (*last week* $\rightarrow$ Past Simple $V_2$)
38. **had passed** (पहले की घटना पर जोर: Past Perfect $\text{had} + V_3$)
39. **found** (Single past event $\rightarrow$ Past Simple $V_2$)
40. **had destroyed** (By the time clause $\rightarrow$ Past Perfect)
41. **travelled** (*In ancient times* $\rightarrow$ Past Simple)
42. **was cooking** (While clause $\rightarrow$ Past Continuous)
43. **had stopped** (पहले की घटना पर जोर: Past Perfect)
44. **formulated** (Completed historical action; not discovery of an unknown force.)
45. **were fighting** (Action in progress when entered)
46. **had been waiting** (*for an hour before* $\rightarrow$ Past Perfect Continuous)
47. **received** (*two hours ago* $\rightarrow$ Past Simple)
48. **had taken** (पहले की घटना पर जोर: Past Perfect)
49. **were playing** (Action in progress when lights went out)
50. **break** (`did` के बाद $V_1$)
51. **had suffered** (पहले की घटना पर जोर: Past Perfect)
52. **caught** (Past sudden action $\rightarrow$ Past Simple $V_2$)
53. **had rung** (पहले की घटना पर जोर: Past Perfect)
54. **set** (Historical date $\rightarrow$ Past Simple $V_2$ of set = set)
55. **was dancing** (Two parallel actions in past with while)
56. **had taken** (पहले की घटना पर जोर: Past Perfect)
57. **did not write** (*last month* $\rightarrow$ Past Simple negative)
58. **was repairing** (Action in progress when seen)
59. **returned** (After + had + $V_3$, main clause takes $V_2$)
60. **had flown** (पहले की घटना पर जोर: Past Perfect)

### Set C Answers:

**Alternative-answer notes:** Future time words alone do not choose the form. Q65 *will have lived* and Q104 *will have worked* are possible alongside the continuous forms. Q71 *reopens/is reopening* and Q79 *departs/is departing* suit timetables or arrangements; Q76 *am meeting* suits an arrangement. For deadline examples (*by ...*), a Future Simple completion statement may also be grammatical. These are intended grammar examples, not factual forecasts.
61. **shall celebrate / will celebrate** (*next week* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
62. **will have completed** (*By next month* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
63. **will be flying** (*At this time tomorrow* $\rightarrow$ Future Continuous)
64. **will pass** (Expectation in future)
65. **will have been living** (*By the end of this year + for ten years* $\rightarrow$ Fut. Perf. Cont.)
66. **will examine** (*in a few minutes* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
67. **shall have finished / will have finished** (*By 5 p.m.* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
68. **will organize** (*tomorrow* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
69. **shall be enjoying** (*At this moment next Sunday* $\rightarrow$ Future Continuous)
70. **will have declared** (*By next March* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
71. **will reopen** (*Monday next* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
72. **will have melted** (*By tomorrow morning* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
73. **will ... be doing** (*at this time tomorrow* $\rightarrow$ Future Continuous)
74. **will help** (Promise for future)
75. **will have constructed** (*By next Diwali* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
76. **shall meet / will meet** (*tomorrow* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
77. **will have launched** (*By next year* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
78. **shall be watching / will be watching** (Specific point in future)
79. **will depart** (*in ten minutes* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
80. **will have read** (*By the end of this week* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
81. **shall shift / will shift** (*coming month* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
82. **will have found** (*By 2030* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
83. **will play** (*next Friday* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
84. **will have reached** (*By sunset* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
85. **will perform** (*Soon* $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)

### Set D Answers:

**Alternative-answer notes:** Q106 *is flowing* is possible for an observation now; *flows* describes the usual course. Q114 *breaks* expresses a general conditional, while *will break* predicts this occasion. Q119 *was* occurs in less formal usage, while *were* clearly signals the unreal comparison. Many conditional main clauses can take *could/might* for possibility instead of *would/will* for the result; follow the requested meaning.
86. **will succeed** (Conditional Type 1: Present Simple $\rightarrow$ will + $V_1$)
87. **would buy** (Conditional Type 2: Past Simple $\rightarrow$ would + $V_1$)
88. **would have helped** (Conditional Type 3: Past Perfect $\rightarrow$ would have + $V_3$)
89. **practises** (Unless + Present Simple, singular subject *she*)
90. **turns** (Given verb is *turn*: *turns into water*. *Melts* would require the prompt verb *melt* and removal of *into water*.)
91. **would eradicate** (Hypothetical condition: If I were $\rightarrow$ would + $V_1$)
92. **would not have made** (Conditional Type 3: had listened $\rightarrow$ would not have + $V_3$)
93. **will leave** (Time clause: As soon as + Present Simple $\rightarrow$ Future Simple)
94. **invites** (Conditional Type 1: if clause takes Present Simple)
95. **would have come** (Conditional Type 3: had known $\rightarrow$ would have + $V_3$)
96. **will be pardoned** (Conditional Type 1 in passive)
97. **expands** (Zero Conditional: Scientific fact)
98. **won** (Conditional Type 2: would you do $\rightarrow$ $V_2$ in if clause)
99. **does not hurry** (Conditional Type 1 negative)
100. **would have passed** (Inversion of Conditional Type 3: Had you worked $\rightarrow$ would have + $V_3$)
101. **is covering** (*Look!* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
102. **had recovered** (पहले की घटना पर जोर: Past Perfect)
103. **wears, is wearing** (Usually = Present Simple; Today = Temporary action / Present Continuous)
104. **will have been working** (*By next December + for 25 years* $\rightarrow$ Fut. Perf. Cont.)
105. **entered** (While clause had past continuous, interrupted by $V_2$)
106. **flows** (Geographical/General fact $\rightarrow$ Present Simple)
107. **travels** (Scientific law $\rightarrow$ Present Simple)
108. **have known** (*since childhood* + stative verb *know* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect)
109. **had already closed** (Past Perfect for prior completion)
110. **pay** (Plural subject *Those pupils* + never $\rightarrow$ $V_1$)
111. **is wailing** (*Listen!* $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous)
112. **will have delivered** (*By tomorrow noon* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
113. **was climbing** (While clause $\rightarrow$ Past Continuous)
114. **will break** (Conditional Type 1)
115. **has not risen** (*not yet* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect negative)
116. **visited** (Past routine/habit $\rightarrow$ Past Simple $V_2$)
117. **shall have submitted / will have submitted** (*By next Monday* $\rightarrow$ Future Perfect)
118. **started** (Standard *It is time we started* pattern; this past form refers to the present need to act. A different structure is *It is time to start*.)
119. **were** (As if + Unreal hypothetical state $\rightarrow$ 'were')
120. **has finished** (Formal school grammar normally uses singular agreement with *neither of*; plural agreement also occurs informally. Here singular subject agreement + *yet* $\rightarrow$ Present Perfect singular *has finished*)

---
⚡ 8. Pre-Exam 2-Minute Rapid Revision Cheat Sheet

परीक्षा भवन में प्रवेश करने से ठीक पहले इस तालिका को 60 सेकंड में दोहरा लें:

```
[Clue Word / Pattern] ──────────────────────────► [Possible Verb Form; Check Context]
1. daily / usually / always / every... ────────► often V1 / (V1 + s/es)
2. Universal / Scientific Truth ───────────────► V1 / (V1 + s/es)
3. Look! / Listen! / now / at present ─────────► often is / am / are + V4 (ing)
4. already / just / yet ───────────────────────► may pair with has / have + V3
5. since / for + time ────────────────────────► choose tense by meaning; stative verbs may use have/has + V3
6. yesterday / ago / last... / in 1947 ────────► V2 (did not + V1)
7. While ... / When ... (interrupted) ─────────► was / were + V4 (ing) vs V2
8. ... BEFORE ... ─────────────────────────────► had + V3 [BEFORE] V2
9. ... AFTER ... ──────────────────────────────► V2 [AFTER] had + V3
10. tomorrow / next... / soon ─────────────────► will / shall + V1
11. at this time tomorrow ─────────────────────► will be / shall be + V4
12. BY + future time (by next year) ───────────► will have / shall have + V3
13. If + V1 (Simple Present) ──────────────────► will + V1
14. If + V2 (Simple Past / were) ──────────────► would + V1
15. If + had + V3 (Past Perfect) ──────────────► would have + V3
```

---
📝 9. Final Practice Test: 10 points (not an RBSE exam simulation)

**अभ्यास समय:** 15 मिनट | **स्व-मूल्यांकन:** 10 practice points (1 point each)  
*निर्देश: Fill in the blanks with the correct form of the verbs given in brackets.*

1. Look! Smoke ______ (come) out of that abandoned house.
2. The earth ______ (revolve) around the sun.
3. My father ______ (buy) this watch last year.
4. She ______ (already cook) the dinner before the guests arrived.
5. We ______ (play) tennis since 4 o'clock.
6. By next Friday, the carpenter ______ (make) all the chairs.
7. While the boys were playing cricket, it ______ (start) raining.
8. If he ______ (run) fast, he will win the race.
9. If they had worked honestly, they ______ (not fail).
10. The doctor arrived after the patient ______ (examine) by the nurse.

---

### 📋 Suggested answer key:
1. **is coming** [1 point] — *Look!* plus the context shows an action in progress.
2. **revolves** [1 point] — Universal astronomical truth indicates Present Simple ($V_1 + s$).
3. **bought** [1 point] — *last year* indicates Past Simple ($V_2$ of buy).
4. **had already cooked** [1 point] — Before-pattern past action completed first indicates Past Perfect ($\text{had} + V_3$).
5. **have been playing** [1 point] — *since 4 o'clock* without past context indicates Present Perfect Continuous.
6. **will have made** [1 point] — *By next Friday* indicates Future Perfect ($\text{will have} + V_3$).
7. **started** [1 point] — Interrupted action in past with while clause takes Past Simple ($V_2$).
8. **runs** [1 point] — Conditional Type 1 if-clause takes Present Simple ($V_1 + s$).
9. **would not have failed** [1 point] — Conditional Type 3 (had + $V_3$ $\rightarrow$ would not have + $V_3$).
10. **had been examined** [1 point] — Passive construction: the patient receives the action. The nurse is the agent; in active voice the clause would be *after the nurse had examined the patient*.

content.value: माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर (कक्षा 10वीं — अंग्रेजी अनिवार्य)

### 🎯 पाठ्यक्रम स्थिति: Subject–Verb Concord के लिए 2 अंक (2026–27 Madhyamik syllabus)

---
🧭 1. Subject–Verb Concord: scope and core idea

Subject-Verb Concord (कर्ता-क्रिया अन्वय) का सीधा अर्थ है: **"किसी वाक्य में Subject (कर्ता) के Number (वचन) और Person (पुरुष) के अनुसार ही उसकी Verb (क्रिया) का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।"**

### 📐 मूलभूत नियम (The Cardinal Law):
$$\mathbf{\text{Singular Subject} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{Singular Verb}}$$
$$\mathbf{\text{Plural Subject} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{Plural Verb}}$$

- **Singular Verbs:** `is, was, has, does, V1 + s/es` (जैसे: *writes, plays, goes*)
- **Plural Verbs:** `are, were, have, do, V1` (जैसे: *write, play, go*)
- **अभ्यास का स्वरूप:** रिक्त स्थान, विकल्प-चयन और वाक्य-संपादन से agreement का अभ्यास किया जा सकता है। ये किसी एकमात्र RBSE प्रश्न-रूप का दावा नहीं हैं।
- **पाठ्यक्रम भार:** 2026–27 RBSE syllabus में Subject–Verb Concord के लिए 2 अंक निर्धारित है। सटीक प्रश्न-संख्या/रूप तय नहीं है; grammar का कुल भाग 8 अंक का है.
