🔍 3. In-Depth Rule Explanations & Step-by-Step Practical Insights

### 📘 Rule 1: 'And' से जुड़े दो कर्ता एवं इसके अपवाद
- **सामान्य नियम:** यदि दो एकवचन संज्ञाएं 'and' से जुड़ी हों, तो बहुवचन क्रिया का प्रयोग होता है:
  * *Example:* Ram and Shyam **are** playing cricket. (Plural)
  * *Example:* Fire and water **do** not agree. (Plural)
- **अपवाद A: संयुक्त विचार अथवा भोजन की वस्तुएं (Single Compound Idea / Dish / Profession):**
  * जब 'and' से जुड़ी दो संज्ञाएं मिलकर एक ही विचार, भाव, भोजन या पहचान व्यक्त करें, तो क्रिया **Singular** होगी:
  * *Bread and butter* **is** my favourite breakfast. (एक संपूर्ण नाश्ता)
  * *Rice and curry* **is** a popular dish.
  * *Slow and steady* **wins** the race. (कहावत)
  * *Horse and carriage* **is** at the gate. (एक पूरी बग्घी)
  * *Truth and honesty* **is** the best policy.
- **अपवाद B: एक ही व्यक्ति के दो पद (The Single Article Rule):**
  * यदि प्रथम संज्ञा से पहले Article (*the/a/an*) या Possessive (*my/his*) हो और दूसरी संज्ञा से पहले न हो, तो इसका अर्थ है कि **व्यक्ति एक ही है** $\rightarrow$ **Singular Verb**!
  * *Example:* **The** poet and philosopher **is** dead. (एक ही व्यक्ति जो कवि भी था और दार्शनिक भी)
  * *Example:* **My** friend and guide **has** come. (एक ही व्यक्ति)
  * परन्तु यदि दोनों संज्ञाओं से पहले Article या Possessive लगा हो, तो **दो अलग-अलग व्यक्ति** होते हैं $\rightarrow$ **Plural Verb**!
  * *Example:* **The** poet and **the** philosopher **are** dead. (दो अलग-अलग व्यक्ति)
  * *Example:* **The** Headmaster and **the** Secretary **were** present. (दो अलग व्यक्ति)

---

### 📗 Rule 2: प्रथम कर्ता का प्रभुत्व (First Subject Dominance)
जब दो कर्ता निम्नलिखित संयोजकों (Connectors) से जुड़े हों:
$$\mathbf{\text{as well as, along with, together with, with, accompanied by, in addition to, besides, rather than, like, unlike, including, excluding}}$$
तो आने वाली क्रिया **प्रथम कर्ता (First Subject)** के Number और Person के अनुसार ही लगेगी। दूसरे कर्ता को पूरी तरह अनदेखा (ignore) कर दें!

- *Example 1:* The Captain, **along with** all his soldiers, **was** (was/were) killed in action.
  * *स्पष्टीकरण:* मुख्य कर्ता *The Captain* (Singular) है, अतः क्रिया *was* आएगी; *soldiers* (Plural) को नहीं देखना है।
- *Example 2:* The students, **as well as** their teacher, **are** (is/are) going on a tour.
  * *स्पष्टीकरण:* प्रथम कर्ता *The students* (Plural) है, अतः *are* आएगा।
- *Example 3:* She, **accompanied by** her parents, **has** (has/have) arrived.
  * *स्पष्टीकरण:* प्रथम कर्ता *She* (Singular) है, अतः *has* आएगा।
- *Example 4:* He, and not his brothers, **is** (is/are) guilty.

---

### 📙 Rule 3: निकटतम कर्ता का नियम (The Proximity Rule)
जब दो कर्ता निम्नलिखित जोड़ों (Correlative Conjunctions) से जुड़े हों:
$$\mathbf{\text{Neither ... nor, \quad Either ... or, \quad Not only ... but also, \quad Or, \quad Nor}}$$
तो क्रिया अपने **सबसे निकट वाले कर्ता (Nearest Subject / Second Subject)** के अनुसार लगती है!

- *Example 1:* Neither the principal nor the teachers **were** (was/were) present.
  * *स्पष्टीकरण:* क्रिया के सबसे निकट *the teachers* (Plural) है, अतः *were* आया।
- *Example 2:* Neither the teachers nor the principal **was** (was/were) present.
  * *स्पष्टीकरण:* क्रिया के सबसे निकट *the principal* (Singular) है, अतः *was* आया।
- *Example 3:* Either he or I **am** (is/am/are) to blame.
  * *स्पष्टीकरण:* क्रिया के सबसे निकट *I* है, अतः *am* आया।
- *Example 4:* Not only the father but also his sons **have** (has/have) attended the meeting.
  * *स्पष्टीकरण:* क्रिया के सबसे निकट *his sons* (Plural) है, अतः *have* आया।
- *Example 5:* Is either he or you **ready**? $\rightarrow$ Is either you or he ready? (क्रिया के निकट singular *he* है।)

---

### 📕 Rule 4: 'Each, Every, Either, Neither, One' एवं Indefinite Pronouns
निम्नलिखित शब्द सामान्यतः **Singular Verb** लेते हैं; *neither of* जैसे प्रयोगों में formal और informal usage अलग हो सकता है:
$$\mathbf{\text{Each, Every, Either, Neither, Everyone, Everybody, Someone, Somebody, No one, Nobody, Anyone, Anybody, Everything, Something, Nothing, Anything}}$$

- **Each of / Either of / Neither of + Plural Noun:**
  * यहाँ छात्र सबसे बड़ी गलती करते हैं। वे Plural Noun देखकर Plural Verb लगा देते हैं, जबकि वास्तविक कर्ता *Each / Either / Neither* (Singular) होता है!
  * *Example 1:* Each of the girls **has** (has/have) a pen. (✔️ 'has', क्योंकि प्रत्येक एक-एक लड़की की बात हो रही है)
  * *Example 2:* Neither of the two brothers **is** (is/are) honest.
  * *Example 3:* Either of these two roads **leads** (leads/lead) to the station.
  * *Example 4:* Everyone of the students **was** (was/were) given a medal.
  * *Example 5:* Someone **has** (has/have) stolen my pen.
  * *Example 6:* Everything **is** (is/are) fine.

---

### 📓 Rule 5: 'A number of' बनाम 'The number of' (Super-High Yield Trap!)
RBSE बोर्ड में यह नियम बार-बार पूछा जाता है। इसे कंठस्थ कर लें:

$$\mathbf{\text{A number of} + \text{Plural Noun} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{PLURAL VERB} \quad (\text{'कई' या 'अनेक' का भाव})}$$
$$\mathbf{\text{The number of} + \text{Plural Noun} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{SINGULAR VERB} \quad (\text{'निश्चित संख्या' का भाव})}$$

- *Example 1:* **A number of** students **were** (was/were) waiting outside the hall.
- *Example 2:* **The number of** students in this class **is** (is/are) fifty.
- *Example 3:* **A large number of** people **have** (has/have) applied for the post.
- *Example 4:* **The number of** road accidents **has** (has/have) decreased this year.

---

### 📒 Rule 6: समूहवाचक संज्ञाएं (Collective Nouns)
जैसे: *Jury, Committee, Team, Family, Crowd, Council, Army, Audience, Parliament, Government, Board*.
- **स्थिति 1 (Unanimous / Single Unit):** जब पूरा समूह एकमत होकर एक इकाई (Single entity) के रूप में कार्य करे $\rightarrow$ **Singular Verb**।
  * *Example:* The jury **has** given its verdict. (निर्णय सर्वसम्मति से आया)
  * *Example:* The committee **has** elected its chairman.
  * *Example:* The Indian cricket team **is** very strong.
- **स्थिति 2 (Divided / Individual Members):** जब समूह के सदस्यों में मतभेद हो, वे अलग-अलग विचार रखें या अलग-अलग कार्य करें $\rightarrow$ **Plural Verb** (साथ ही pronoun भी *their* आता है)।
  * *Example:* The jury **were** divided in their opinions. (जजों के बीच मतभेद हो गया)
  * *Example:* The committee **have** taken their seats. (सदस्य अपनी-अपनी कुर्सियों पर बैठ रहे हैं)
  * *Example:* The family **are** fighting over property.

---

### 📘 Rule 7: माप, भार, दूरी एवं निश्चित धनराशि (Quantity, Distance & Amount)
जब कोई बहुवचन संज्ञा किसी **निश्चित दूरी (distance), निश्चित भार (weight), निश्चित समयावधि (period of time) या निश्चित धनराशि (sum of money)** को एकमुश्त (single unit / whole lump sum) के रूप में व्यक्त करे, तो क्रिया **Singular** होती है!

- *Example 1:* Ten miles **is** (is/are) a long distance to walk.
- *Example 2:* Fifty thousand rupees **was** (was/were) spent on the project.
- *Example 3:* Five hundred kilometers **is** (is/are) not a big deal for airplanes.
- *Example 4:* Two hours **is** (is/are) enough to complete this test.
- *Example 5:* Six months **is** (is/are) a sufficient time for preparation.
- **अपवाद:** यदि धनराशि को अलग-अलग खर्च करने या अलग-अलग व्यक्तियों में बांटने के रूप में दिखाया जाए, तो Plural Verb आती है:
  * *Example:* Fifty thousand rupees **were** distributed among the victims.

---

### 📗 Rule 8: दिखने में बहुवचन, अर्थ में एकवचन (Plural in Form, Singular in Meaning)
कुछ संज्ञाएँ रूप में बहुवचन जैसी दिखती हैं, पर किसी विषय/एकल विचार के अर्थ में सामान्यतः singular verb लेती हैं:
1. **विषयों के नाम (Subjects):** *mathematics, physics, economics, civics, statistics,* और *phonetics* अकादमिक विषय के अर्थ में सामान्यतः singular हैं। *Politics* अर्थानुसार बदल सकता है।
   * *Example:* Mathematics **is** a scoring subject.
   * *Example:* Physics **requires** conceptual clarity.
   * *⚠️ Special Exception:* यदि इनके पूर्व Possessive Adjective (*my, his, their*) या 'The' लगा हो, तो इनका अर्थ 'गणना' या 'विचार' हो जाता है और Plural Verb आती है:
     * *His mathematics* **are** very weak. (यहाँ गणित विषय नहीं, बल्कि गणना क्षमता है)
2. **बीमारियों के नाम (Diseases):** *Measles, Mumps, Rickets, Shingles*.
   * *Example:* Measles **is** an infectious disease.
3. **खेलों के नाम (Games):** *Billiards, Darts, Dominoes, Bowls*.
   * *Example:* Billiards **is** played across the world.
4. **अन्य संज्ञाएं:** *News, Innings, Gallows*.
   * *Example:* The news **is** true.
   * *Example:* The first innings **was** completed today.

---

### 📙 Rule 9: दो भागों वाले वस्त्र एवं उपकरण (Two-Part Tools & Clothes)
जैसे: *Scissors, Trousers, Spectacles, Glasses, Pliers, Tongs, Binoculars, Pants, Jeans, Shorts*.
- यदि ये अकेले आएं, तो इनके साथ **Plural Verb** का प्रयोग होता है:
  * *Example:* My spectacles **are** broken.
  * *Example:* The scissors **are** blunt.
  * *Example:* His jeans **look** trendy.
- परन्तु यदि इनके पूर्व **'A pair of'** (एक जोड़ी) लग जाए, तो क्रिया **Singular Verb** हो जाएगी!
  * *Example:* **A pair of** scissors **was** purchased yesterday.
  * *Example:* **A pair of** trousers **is** lying on the bed.

---

### 📕 Rule 10: 'One of the' के दो रूप (Board's Most Sophisticated Trap)
1. **साधारण वाक्य (Simple Sentence):**
   $$\mathbf{\text{One of the} + \text{Plural Noun} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{SINGULAR VERB}}$$
   * *Example:* One of my best friends **is** (is/are) an engineer.
   * *Example:* One of the rooms **was** (was/were) locked.
2. **Relative Pronoun वाला वाक्य (With who / which / that):**
   $$\mathbf{\text{One of the} + \text{Plural Noun} + \text{who / which / that} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{PLURAL VERB}}$$
   यहाँ Relative Pronoun (*who/that*) अपने पूर्ववर्ती Plural Noun (Antecedent) को संदर्भित करता है:
   * *Example:* He is one of the players who **have** (has/have) performed brilliantly.
3. **The ONLY one of the (अपवाद का भी अपवाद):**
   यदि 'the only' लग जाए, तो पुनः **Singular Verb** आएगी:
   * *Example:* She is **the only one of** the girls who **has** (has/have) passed the examination.

---

### 📓 Rule 11: 'Many', 'A great many', 'Many a'
- **Many / A great many / Several / Few / Both:** इनके साथ Plural Noun और **Plural Verb** आती है:
  * *Example:* Many students **have** registered for the competition.
  * *Example:* Both the sisters **are** talented.
- **Many a + Singular Noun:** formal written usage में इसके साथ सामान्यतः **Singular Verb** आती है।
  * *Example:* **Many a** man **has** (has/have) succumbed to temptation.
  * *Example:* **Many a** flower **fades** (fade/fades) unobserved.

---

### 📒 Rule 12: 'There' वाले वाक्यों में Concord
'There' स्वयं कोई वास्तविक कर्ता नहीं होता। 'There' वाले वाक्य में क्रिया उसके बाद आने वाले **वास्तविक संज्ञा (Real Noun)** के अनुसार तय होती है:
$$\mathbf{\text{There} + \text{Verb} + \text{Noun (Real Subject)}}$$
- *Example 1:* There **is** a big banyan tree near the temple. (एकवचन: *a big banyan tree*)
- *Example 2:* There **are** fifty rooms in our school building. (बहुवचन: *fifty rooms*)
- *Example 3:* There **was** an apple and two oranges on the plate. (निकटतम संज्ञा *an apple* के अनुसार)

---
🚫 4. Mistake Busters: शीर्ष 7 भ्रम और उनका निवारण

| क्र. सं. | सामान्य छात्र भ्रम (Common Student Error) | सही रूप (Correct Form) | कारण एवं नियम (Rule Explanation) | |:---:|---|---|---| | **1** | In formal writing, Neither of the boys **were** present. | Neither of the boys **was** present. ✔️ | *Neither of* सामान्यतः formal writing में singular लेता है; informal usage में plural भी मिलता है। | | **2** | The teacher with all his pupils **are** coming. ❌ | The teacher with all his pupils **is** coming. ✔️ | 'With' से जुड़ने पर क्रिया प्रथम कर्ता (*The teacher* - Singular) के अनुसार लगेगी। | | **3** | Bread and butter **are** sold here / **are** my breakfast. | Bread and butter **is** my breakfast. ✔️ (भोजन)
Bread and butter **are** sold here. ✔️ (सामान) | जब एक भोजन डिश हो तो Singular; जब अलग-अलग बेची जाने वाली वस्तुएं हों तो Plural! | | **4** | Mathematics **are** a difficult subject. ❌ | Mathematics **is** a difficult subject. ✔️ | विषय के नाम के रूप में *mathematics* सामान्यतः singular है। | | **5** | The number of boys **are** thirty. ❌ | The number of boys **is** thirty. ✔️ | 'The number of' हमेशा निश्चित संख्या $\rightarrow$ Singular Verb! | | **6** | Ten thousand rupees **were** a big amount. ❌ | Ten thousand rupees **was** a big amount. ✔️ | धनराशि एकमुश्त राशि (single lump sum) दर्शाती है $\rightarrow$ Singular! | | **7** | She is one of those women who **is** generous. ❌ | She is one of those women who **are** generous. ✔️ | 'who' से पहले 'women' (Plural) है, अतः क्रिया Plural आएगी! | ---
🏛️ 5. Practice bank (not authenticated past-paper questions)

नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न agreement अभ्यास के लिए हैं; इन्हें 2014–2024 के RBSE प्रश्नपत्रों से प्रमाणित प्रश्न न समझें:

1. **Practice set:** Neither he nor his sisters ______ (was/were) invited.
   * **Answer:** **were**
   * *कारण:* Neither...nor में क्रिया निकटतम कर्ता (*his sisters* - Plural) के अनुसार लगती है।
2. **Practice set:** The poet and singer ______ (has/have) died.
   * **Answer:** **has**
   * *कारण:* केवल प्रथम शब्द से पहले 'The' है, अतः व्यक्ति एक ही है $\rightarrow$ Singular।
3. **Practice set:** Each of the players ______ (was/were) rewarded.
   * **Answer:** **was**
   * *कारण:* 'Each of' के साथ सदैव Singular Verb आती है।
4. **Practice set:** Bread and butter ______ (is/are) his only food.
   * **Answer:** **is**
   * *कारण:* 'Bread and butter' एक संयुक्त भोजन (single dish) दर्शाता है $\rightarrow$ Singular।
5. **Practice set:** The teacher, along with his students, ______ (has/have) gone on a picnic.
   * **Answer:** **has**
   * *कारण:* 'along with' से जुड़ने पर क्रिया प्रथम कर्ता (*The teacher* - Singular) के अनुसार लगेगी।
6. **Practice set:** Mathematics ______ (is/are) an interesting subject.
   * **Answer:** **is**
   * *कारण:* विषय का नाम सदा Singular होता है।
7. **Practice set:** A large number of students ______ (is/are) absent today.
   * **Answer:** **are**
   * *कारण:* 'A number of' के साथ Plural Verb आती है।
8. **Practice set:** Either you or Mohan ______ (has/have) stolen the watch.
   * **Answer:** **has**
   * *कारण:* Either...or में निकटतम कर्ता (*Mohan* - Singular) के अनुसार क्रिया आती है।
9. **Practice set:** The quality of these mangoes ______ (is/are) not good.
   * **Answer:** **is**
   * *कारण:* मुख्य कर्ता *The quality* (भाववाचक संज्ञा - Singular) है, *mangoes* नहीं!
10. **Practice set:** Not only the officer but also the soldiers ______ (was/were) killed.
    * **Answer:** **were**
    * *कारण:* Not only...but also में निकटतम कर्ता (*the soldiers* - Plural) के अनुसार क्रिया।
11. **Practice set:** Slow and steady ______ (win/wins) the race.
    * **Answer:** **wins**
    * *कारण:* एक ही विचार व्यक्त करने वाला युग्म शब्द $\rightarrow$ Singular Verb ($V_1 + s$).
12. **Practice set:** A pair of shoes ______ (was/were) kept in the corner.
    * **Answer:** **was**
    * *कारण:* 'A pair of' लगने के कारण क्रिया Singular होगी।
13. **Practice set:** Ten kilometers ______ (is/are) a long walk.
    * **Answer:** **is**
    * *कारण:* निश्चित दूरी एकमुश्त इकाई (single unit) है $\rightarrow$ Singular।
14. **Practice set:** The jury ______ (was/were) divided in their opinion.
    * **Answer:** **were**
    * *कारण:* मतभेद होने पर Collective Noun के साथ Plural Verb आती है।
15. **Practice set:** No news ______ (is/are) good news.
    * **Answer:** **is**
     * *कारण:* *News* सामान्यतः singular noun है।
16. **Practice set:** Mohan as well as his parents ______ (was/were) present at the function.
    * **Answer:** **was**
    * *कारण:* 'as well as' में क्रिया प्रथम कर्ता (*Mohan* - Singular) के अनुसार लगती है।
17. **Practice set:** One of my cousins ______ (lives/live) in Canada.
    * **Answer:** **lives**
    * *कारण:* 'One of the' के साथ क्रिया सदा Singular होती है।
18. **Practice set:** The committee ______ (has/have) issued its report.
    * **Answer:** **has**
    * *कारण:* समिति ने एकमत होकर रिपोर्ट दी (*its report*) $\rightarrow$ Singular।
19. **Practice set:** Two and two ______ (makes/make) four.
    * **Answer:** **make / makes** (RBSE बोर्ड में दोनों मान्य, परन्तु 'make' व्याकरणिक रूप से अधिक प्रामाणिक)।
20. **Practice set:** The leader accompanied by his followers ______ (has/have) arrived.
    * **Answer:** **has**
    * *कारण:* 'accompanied by' में क्रिया प्रथम कर्ता (*The leader*) के अनुसार आती है।

---
🏋️ 6. 60 Board-Style High-Yield Practice Exercises (Complete Bank)

नीचे दिए गए 60 प्रश्नों में रिक्त स्थान की पूर्ति कोष्ठक में दिए गए सही विकल्प से करें:

### Set A: Foundations & Pair Words (Q1 – Q20)
1. Slow and steady ______ (win / wins) the race.
2. Time and tide ______ (wait / waits) for none.
3. The horse and carriage ______ (is / are) standing at the door.
4. Rice and curry ______ (is / are) his staple diet.
5. The District Magistrate and Collector ______ (has / have) visited the flood area.
6. The Director and the Manager ______ (has / have) signed the agreement.
7. My uncle and benefactor ______ (has / have) passed away.
8. Fire and water ______ (do / does) not agree.
9. Age and experience ______ (bring / brings) wisdom to man.
10. The teacher and the student ______ (is / are) working on the project.
11. Bread and butter ______ (is / are) essential for breakfast.
12. Truth and non-violence ______ (was / were) Gandhiji's principles.
13. Gold and silver ______ (is / are) precious metals.
14. The orator and statesman ______ (has / have) arrived.
15. Early to bed and early to rise ______ (make / makes) a man healthy.
16. Oil and water ______ (do / does) not mix.
17. The novelist and poet ______ (is / are) being honoured today.
18. Crown and glory ______ (is / are) the reward of hard work.
19. Pen and ink ______ (is / are) required for the examination.
20. Ram, Shyam and Mohan ______ (is / are) brothers.

### Set B: Connectors, Connectives & Proximity Rules (Q21 – Q40)
21. The captain, as well as the crew members, ______ (was / were) drowned.
22. Neither praise nor blame ______ (affect / affects) a truly noble soul.
23. Either Sita or her friends ______ (has / have) organized the party.
24. Not only the principal but also the teachers ______ (was / were) present.
25. The king, accompanied by his courtiers, ______ (has / have) entered the court.
26. You as well as he ______ (is / are / am) guilty.
27. Neither the father nor the sons ______ (was / were) ready to sell the land.
28. Either he or you ______ (is / are) mistaken.
29. The commander, with his battalion, ______ (has / have) taken position.
30. Not only the students but also their guide ______ (was / were) delighted.
31. The house, in addition to the furniture, ______ (was / were) sold.
32. Neither food nor water ______ (was / were) available in the desert.
33. She, rather than her classmates, ______ (deserves / deserve) the award.
34. The mother, together with her daughters, ______ (bakes / bake) delicious cakes.
35. No nook or corner ______ (was / were) left unchecked.
36. The players, along with their coach, ______ (is / are) arriving today.
37. He and not I ______ (has / have) broken the mirror.
38. Neither the doctor nor the nurses ______ (was / were) in the ward.
39. The boy, like his father, ______ (possesses / possess) great courage.
40. Either the manager or the assistants ______ (has / have) misplaced the file.

### Set C: Indefinite Pronouns, Special Nouns & Number Units (Q41 – Q60)
41. Each of the participants ______ (was / were) given a certificate.
42. Neither of these two books ______ (is / are) useful for the exam.
43. Everyone ______ (wants / want) to succeed in life.
44. A number of migratory birds ______ (has / have) arrived at the lake.
45. The number of accidents on this highway ______ (is / are) alarming.
46. Ten thousand rupees ______ (is / are) a handsome amount.
47. Five kilometers ______ (is / are) not a great distance for a cyclist.
48. Mathematics ______ (is / are) considered a tough subject by some.
49. The news of his sudden demise ______ (has / have) shocked everyone.
50. My scissors ______ (needs / need) sharpening.
51. A pair of spectacles ______ (was / were) found on the bench.
52. One of the windows ______ (was / were) broken by the storm.
53. He is one of the politicians who ______ (is / are) genuinely honest.
54. She is the only one of the students who ______ (has / have) scored 100%.
55. Many a soldier ______ (has / have) laid down his life for the motherland.
56. The jury ______ (has / have) announced its unanimous decision.
57. The committee ______ (was / were) divided on the proposal.
58. There ______ (is / are) a library and four laboratories in our school.
59. More than one candidate ______ (was / were) selected for the interview.
60. Two-thirds of the book ______ (has / have) been read by me.

---
🔑 Complete Answer Key with Detailed Explanations (Q1 – Q60)

### Set A Explanations:
1. **wins** — Compound idea representing a single proverb $\rightarrow$ Singular.
2. **wait** — Time and tide are two distinct forces of nature $\rightarrow$ Plural.
3. **is** — Pair word referring to a single conveyance carriage $\rightarrow$ Singular.
4. **is** — Single food item $\rightarrow$ Singular.
5. **has** — One article 'The' denotes a single person holding both titles $\rightarrow$ Singular.
6. **have** — Two separate articles 'The... and the...' denote two distinct individuals $\rightarrow$ Plural.
7. **has** — Single possessive 'My' denotes one single person $\rightarrow$ Singular.
8. **do** — Two contrary elements $\rightarrow$ Plural.
9. **brings** — Combined quality / experience $\rightarrow$ Singular.
10. **are** — Two separate entities $\rightarrow$ Plural.
11. **is** — Combined food unit $\rightarrow$ Singular.
12. **were** — Two separate ideals of Gandhiji $\rightarrow$ Plural.
13. **are** — Two different precious metals $\rightarrow$ Plural.
14. **has** — Single article denotes one person who is both orator and statesman $\rightarrow$ Singular.
15. **makes** — Proverb expressing a single habit/lifestyle $\rightarrow$ Singular.
16. **do** — Distinct liquids $\rightarrow$ Plural.
17. **is** — One person (single article) $\rightarrow$ Singular.
18. **is** — Single reward/glory $\rightarrow$ Singular.
19. **is** — Single requirement unit $\rightarrow$ Singular.
20. **are** — Three separate persons $\rightarrow$ Plural.

### Set B Explanations:
21. **was** — 'as well as' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *The captain* (Singular).
22. **affects** — Neither...nor $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *blame* (Singular).
23. **have** — Either...or $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *her friends* (Plural).
24. **were** — Not only...but also $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *the teachers* (Plural).
25. **has** — 'accompanied by' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *The king* (Singular).
26. **are** — 'as well as' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *You* (Plural: *You are*).
27. **were** — Neither...nor $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *the sons* (Plural).
28. **are** — Either...or $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *you* (*you are*).
29. **has** — 'with' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *The commander* (Singular).
30. **was** — Not only...but also $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *their guide* (Singular).
31. **was** — 'in addition to' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *The house* (Singular).
32. **was** — Neither...nor $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *water* (Uncountable/Singular).
33. **deserves** — 'rather than' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *She* (Singular).
34. **bakes** — 'together with' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *The mother* (Singular).
35. **was** — 'No...or...' $\rightarrow$ Singular.
36. **are** — 'along with' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *The players* (Plural).
37. **has** — 'and not' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *He* (Singular).
38. **were** — Neither...nor $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *the nurses* (Plural).
39. **possesses** — 'like' $\rightarrow$ follows first subject *The boy* (Singular).
40. **have** — Either...or $\rightarrow$ follows nearest subject *the assistants* (Plural).

### Set C Explanations:
41. **was** — 'Each of' $\rightarrow$ always takes Singular Verb.
42. **is** — 'Neither of' $\rightarrow$ Singular.
43. **wants** — 'Everyone' $\rightarrow$ Indefinite pronoun always takes Singular Verb.
44. **have** — 'A number of' $\rightarrow$ Plural Verb.
45. **is** — 'The number of' $\rightarrow$ Singular Verb.
46. **is** — Specific sum of money considered as one whole $\rightarrow$ Singular.
47. **is** — Specific distance considered as a single unit $\rightarrow$ Singular.
48. **is** — Name of an academic subject $\rightarrow$ Singular.
49. **has** — 'News' is singular in meaning $\rightarrow$ Singular.
50. **need** — 'Scissors' without 'a pair of' takes Plural Verb ($V_1$).
51. **was** — 'A pair of' $\rightarrow$ Singular Verb.
52. **was** — 'One of the' $\rightarrow$ Singular Verb.
53. **are** — Relative pronoun 'who' refers to plural antecedent *politicians* $\rightarrow$ Plural.
54. **has** — 'The only one of...' exception $\rightarrow$ Singular.
55. **has** — 'Many a + Singular Noun' $\rightarrow$ Singular Verb.
56. **has** — Collective noun acting with unanimous consensus (*its decision*) $\rightarrow$ Singular.
57. **were** — Collective noun divided in opinion $\rightarrow$ Plural.
58. **is** — 'There' followed immediately by singular *a library* $\rightarrow$ Singular.
59. **was** — 'More than one + Singular Noun' $\rightarrow$ Singular Verb.
60. **has** — Fraction of a single uncountable or single whole unit (*the book*) $\rightarrow$ Singular.

---
⚡ 7. Pre-Exam 2-Minute Rapid Revision Cheat Sheet

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┐
│ If the Sentence Contains:                              │ Choose This Verb:           │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────┤
│ 1. as well as / along with / together with / with      │ 1st Subject के अनुसार      │
│ 2. Neither...nor / Either...or / Not only...but also   │ Nearest Subject के अनुसार   │
│ 3. Each of / Either of / Neither of / One of the       │ SINGULAR (is / was / has)   │
│ 4. A number of + Plural Noun                           │ PLURAL (are / were / have)  │
│ 5. The number of + Plural Noun                         │ SINGULAR (is / was / has)   │
│ 6. Distance / Weight / Money as a lump sum unit        │ SINGULAR (is / was)         │
│ 7. Subjects: Mathematics, Physics, Politics, News      │ SINGULAR (is / was)         │
│ 8. Scissors, Trousers, Spectacles (without 'a pair')   │ PLURAL (are / were)         │
│ 9. A pair of scissors / trousers                       │ SINGULAR (is / was)         │
│ 10. Many a + Singular Noun                             │ SINGULAR (has / was / V1+s) │
│ 11. Collective Noun (United)                           │ SINGULAR (its report)       │
│ 12. Collective Noun (Divided)                          │ PLURAL (their opinions)     │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┘
```

---
📝 8. Final practice test: 10 points (not an RBSE exam simulation)

**अभ्यास समय:** 15 मिनट | **स्व-मूल्यांकन:** 10 practice points (1 point each)  
*निर्देश: Fill in the blanks with the correct form of the verbs given in brackets.*

1. Neither of the two sisters ______ (has / have) qualified the test.
2. The teacher, along with all the students, ______ (was / were) felicitated by the Collector.
3. Bread and butter ______ (is / are) his daily diet.
4. Either the peon or the clerks ______ (has / have) opened the main gate.
5. The number of books in our library ______ (is / are) increasing rapidly.
6. A large number of migratory birds ______ (has / have) arrived at Keoladeo Sanctuary.
7. Mathematics ______ (is / are) considered difficult by weak students.
8. A pair of new trousers ______ (was / were) purchased by Rohit yesterday.
9. She is one of the noble women who ______ (inspires / inspire) the whole village.
10. Twenty thousand rupees ______ (was / were) spent on the annual day celebration.

---

### 📋 Suggested answer key:
1. **has** [1 point] — formal school-grammar agreement uses singular after *neither of*; informal usage may vary.
2. **was** [1 point] — *Along with* does not change the number of the main subject (*the teacher*).
3. **is** [1 point] — *Bread and butter* denotes one meal here.
4. **have** [1 point] — In this either-or sentence, agreement follows the nearer subject (*the clerks*).
5. **is** [1 point] — *The number of* is singular.
6. **have** [1 point] — *A large number of* takes plural agreement in this construction.
7. **is** [1 point] — *Mathematics* is singular when naming the academic subject.
8. **was** [1 point] — The head noun is singular *pair*.
9. **inspire** [1 point] — *Who* refers to plural *noble women*.
10. **was** [1 point] — The amount is treated as one sum here.

---

### Sources and scope

- [RBSE Class X syllabus 2026–27](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf): Subject–Verb Concord is allocated 2 marks within the 8-mark grammar section.
- [Cambridge English Grammar Today: Subject–verb agreement](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/subject-verb-agreement)
- [Cambridge English Grammar Today: Neither and neither … nor](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/grammar/british-grammar/neither-neither-nor-and-not-either) — notes formal singular and informal plural variation with *neither of*.
- This pass reviewed syllabus framing and selected rules/examples, including one incorrect proximity-rule example. The large practice-bank answer keys remain unchecked individually.

**Syllabus source correction, 13 October 2026:** Scope/marks above use the [Madhyamik Class 10 syllabus, PDF pp. 3–5](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf), not the separate Praveshika scheme. This correction does not certify the remaining exercise keys.

chapters.title: RBSE Class 10 English Grammar: Unit 3 — Active and Passive Voice

content.value: माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर (कक्षा 10वीं — अंग्रेजी अनिवार्य)

### 🎯 पाठ्यक्रम स्थिति: Active/Passive Voice current RBSE 2026–27 grammar list में नहीं; यह enrichment practice है

---
🧭 1. Voice: supplementary grammar practice

Active/Passive Voice उपयोगी अतिरिक्त grammar practice है, पर इसे current RBSE board requirement या 2-mark unit न समझें। RBSE 2026–27 English grammar में कुल 8 marks हैं; इस विषय के लिए कोई अलग mark allocation सूचीबद्ध नहीं है।

### 📌 परीक्षा का स्वरूप:
- प्रश्नपत्र में वाक्य Active Voice में दिया जाता है, और छात्र को उसे Passive Voice में बदलना होता है। प्रायः Passive Voice का प्रारम्भिक कर्ता (Object shifted to Subject) प्रश्नपत्र में पहले से मुद्रित होता है, जिससे छात्र को वाक्य को सही व्याकरणिक संरचना में पूरा करना होता है।
- **उदा. बोर्ड प्रारूप:**
  * Active: *The police caught the thief.*
  * Passive: *The thief ___________________________ .*

### 💡 Active बनाम Passive का मूल अंतर:
- **Active Voice (कर्तृवाच्य):** जब वाक्य का Subject (कर्ता) स्वयं कार्य करता है और कर्ता को प्रमुखता दी जाती है।
  * $\text{Structure: } \mathbf{\text{Subject} + \text{Verb} + \text{Object}}$
  * *Example:* Ram killed Ravana. (राम ने रावण को मारा)
- **Passive Voice (कर्मवाच्य):** जब वाक्य के Object (कर्म) को प्रमुखता दी जाती है और कर्ता द्वारा किए गए कार्य का प्रभाव कर्म पर दिखाया जाता है।
  * $\text{Structure: } \mathbf{\text{Object (as Subject)} + \text{Helping Verb (Be-form)} + V_3 + \text{by} + \text{Subject (as Object)}}$
  * *Example:* Ravana was killed by Ram. (रावण राम के द्वारा मारा गया)

---
⚡ 2. The 5 Universal Golden Rules of Voice Transformation

किसी भी Active वाक्य को Passive Voice में बदलते समय निम्नलिखित **5 अपरिवर्तनीय चरणों (Five Invariable Steps)** का पालन किया जाता है:

```
Step 1: Active के Object (कर्म) को Passive का Subject (कर्ता) बनाएं।
                          ▼
Step 2: Tense के अनुसार उपयुक्त सहायक क्रिया (Helping Verb / Form of 'BE') लगाएं।
                          ▼
Step 3: Main Verb का सदैव तृतीय रूप (Past Participle - V3) ही प्रयोग करें।
                          ▼
Step 4: नए Object से पहले उपयुक्त Preposition (प्रायः 'by', विशेष मामलों में to, at, with, in) लगाएं।
                          ▼
Step 5: Active के Subject को Object (कर्म कारक) बनाकर वाक्य के अंत में रखें।
```

🔍 4. Specialized Board Transformation Patterns (विशिष्ट परीक्षा संरचनाएं)

### 📘 Pattern 4.1: Modal Auxiliaries (मॉडल्स वाले वाक्य) - **Modals:** *can, could, may, might, must, should, would, ought to, need not, dare not, used to*. - **Present / Future Modal Formula:** $$\mathbf{\text{Active: } \text{Subject} + \text{Modal} + V_1 + \text{Object}}$$ $$\mathbf{\text{Passive: } \text{Object} + \text{Modal} + \mathbf{be} + V_3 + \text{by} + \text{Subject}}$$ * *Example 1:* You can lift this heavy box. $\rightarrow$ **This heavy box can be lifted by you.** * *Example 2:* We should respect our elders. $\rightarrow$ **Our elders should be respected by us.** * *Example 3:* One must keep one's promises. $\rightarrow$ **Promises must be kept.** (यहाँ 'one' लोप हो गया) - **Past Modal Formula (Modal + have + $V_3$):** $$\mathbf{\text{Active: } \text{Subject} + \text{Modal} + \text{have} + V_3 + \text{Object}}$$ $$\mathbf{\text{Passive: } \text{Object} + \text{Modal} + \text{have been} + V_3 + \text{by} + \text{Subject}}$$ * *Example:* You should have helped the poor boy. $\rightarrow$ **The poor boy should have been helped by you.** --- ### 📗 Pattern 4.2: Sentences with Two Objects (द्वि-कर्मक वाक्य — Direct & Indirect Object) जब Active वाक्य में दो Objects दिए हों: 1. **Indirect Object (अप्रत्यक्ष कर्म):** सजीव व्यक्ति (Person) $\rightarrow$ *me, him, her, us, them, you, Ramesh*. 2. **Direct Object (प्रत्यक्ष कर्म):** निर्जीव वस्तु (Thing) $\rightarrow$ *a book, a pen, money, a letter*. *Active Example:* **Mr. Sharma teaches us English.** - यहाँ *us* = Indirect Object (Person), *English* = Direct Object (Thing). - ऐसे वाक्यों को Passive में बदलने की **दो विधियां** हैं: #### 🌟 Method 1 (Indirect Object को कर्ता बनाकर — Recommended & Preferred in RBSE Board): $$\mathbf{\text{Indirect Object} + \text{Helping Verb} + V_3 + \text{Direct Object} + \text{by} + \text{Subject}}$$ * *Passive 1:* **We are taught English by Mr. Sharma.** (सबसे सरल और सर्वाधिक प्रामाणिक) #### 🌟 Method 2 (Direct Object को कर्ता बनाकर): जब निर्जीव वस्तु को कर्ता बनाया जाता है, तो सजीव व्यक्ति से पूर्व **'to'** (या कभी-कभी 'for') लगाना अनिवार्य होता है: $$\mathbf{\text{Direct Object} + \text{Helping Verb} + V_3 + \mathbf{to} + \text{Indirect Object} + \text{by} + \text{Subject}}$$ * *Passive 2:* **English is taught to us by Mr. Sharma.** #### अधिक उदाहरण: - *Active:* My father gave me a watch. * *Passive A:* **I was given a watch by my father.** (Method 1) * *Passive B:* **A watch was given to me by my father.** (Method 2) - *Active:* He told us an interesting story. * *Passive A:* **We were told an interesting story by him.** * *Passive B:* **An interesting story was told to us by him.** --- ### 📙 Pattern 4.3: Imperative Sentences (आज्ञा, प्रार्थना एवं परामर्श वाले वाक्य) आज्ञावाचक वाक्यों में Subject (you) छिपा रहता है और वाक्य सीधे $V_1$ से प्रारम्भ होता है। #### 1. Orders / Commands (आज्ञा या निर्देश): - **Formula:** $\mathbf{\text{Let} + \text{Object} + \mathbf{be} + V_3}$ * *Active:* Shut the door. $\rightarrow$ **Let the door be shut.** * *Active:* Open the window. $\rightarrow$ **Let the window be opened.** * *Active:* Post this letter. $\rightarrow$ **Let this letter be posted.** * *Alternative Structure:* **You are ordered / commanded to + $V_1$ + Object.** * *Active:* Stand up on the bench. $\rightarrow$ **You are ordered to stand up on the bench.** #### 2. Requests (प्रार्थना — Please / Kindly वाले वाक्य): 'Please' या 'Kindly' को पूरी तरह हटा दें और वाक्य के प्रारम्भ में **"You are requested to"** जोड़ दें: - **Formula:** $\mathbf{\text{You are requested to} + V_1 + \text{Rest of Sentence}}$ * *Active:* Please help me. $\rightarrow$ **You are requested to help me.** * *Active:* Kindly grant me leave for two days. $\rightarrow$ **You are requested to grant me leave for two days.** * *Active:* Please do not smoke here. $\rightarrow$ **You are requested not to smoke here.** #### 3. Moral Advice / Suggestions (सलाह / परामर्श / नैतिक कर्तव्य): - **Formula:** $\mathbf{\text{Object} + \mathbf{should be} + V_3}$ * *Active:* Help the poor. $\rightarrow$ **The poor should be helped.** * *Active:* Respect your teachers. $\rightarrow$ **Your teachers should be respected.** * *Active:* Obey traffic rules. $\rightarrow$ **Traffic rules should be obeyed.** * *Alternative:* **You are advised to + $V_1$ + Object.** * *Active:* Work hard. $\rightarrow$ **You are advised to work hard.** #### 4. Negative Imperative Sentences (Don't वाले वाक्य): - **Formula A:** $\mathbf{\text{Let} + \text{Object} + \mathbf{not be} + V_3}$ * *Active:* Don't pluck flowers. $\rightarrow$ **Let flowers not be plucked.** - **Formula B:** $\mathbf{\text{You are forbidden to} + V_1 + \text{Object}}$ (सावधान: 'forbidden' के साथ 'not' नहीं लगता!) * *Active:* Don't touch the live wire. $\rightarrow$ **You are forbidden to touch the live wire.** --- ### 📕 Pattern 4.4: Omission of Unimportant Agents (अनावश्यक कर्ता का लोप) जब Active Voice का Subject कोई **अस्पष्ट, अज्ञात, सर्वविदित या महत्वहीन** शब्द हो, तो Passive Voice में **'by + Subject'** को नहीं लिखा जाता: $$\mathbf{\text{Unimportant Agents: someone, somebody, anyone, anybody, people, they, we, one, all, nobody, no one}}$$ - *Example 1:* Someone has stolen my purse. $\rightarrow$ **My purse has been stolen.** (by someone नहीं लिखा जाता) - *Example 2:* People speak English all over the world. $\rightarrow$ **English is spoken all over the world.** - *Example 3:* The police arrested the burglar. $\rightarrow$ **The burglar was arrested.** (चोर को गिरफ्तार केवल पुलिस ही करती है, अतः *by the police* अनावश्यक है) - *Example 4:* Doctors treat patients. $\rightarrow$ **Patients are treated.** #### ⚠️ 'Nobody / No one' का विशेष नियम (Negative Transfer): चूंकि 'Nobody' और 'No one' नकारात्मक होते हैं, इसलिए जब इन्हें हटाया जाता है, तो Passive Voice में **'not'** जोड़ना अनिवार्य होता है: - *Active:* Nobody answered my question. $\rightarrow$ **My question was not answered.** (❌ was answered by nobody गलत है!) - *Active:* No one can climb this steep hill. $\rightarrow$ **This steep hill cannot be climbed.** --- ### 📓 Pattern 4.5: Verbs Taking Prepositions Other Than 'BY' (विशिष्ट Preposition नियम) कुछ विशिष्ट क्रियाओं के बाद Passive Voice में 'by' के स्थान पर निश्चित Prepositions (*to, at, with, in*) का प्रयोग होता है। RBSE बोर्ड इन पर प्रश्न पूछकर छात्रों को परखता है: | क्रिया (Verb) | आवश्यक Preposition | आदर्श उदाहरण (Active $\rightarrow$ Passive) | |---|:---:|---| | **know, marry** | **to** | A: I know him. $\rightarrow$ P: **He is known to me.** (by me नहीं!)
A: Ram married Sita. $\rightarrow$ P: **Sita was married to Ram.** | | **surprise, shock, astonish, amaze, alarm, distress** | **at** | A: His sudden failure surprised me. $\rightarrow$ P: **I was surprised at his sudden failure.**
A: The news shocked us. $\rightarrow$ P: **We were shocked at the news.** | | **please, satisfy, disgust, line, fill** | **with** | A: His performance pleased the teacher. $\rightarrow$ P: **The teacher was pleased with his performance.**
A: Smoke filled the room. $\rightarrow$ P: **The room was filled with smoke.** | | **contain, interest, embody** | **in** | A: This jug contains milk. $\rightarrow$ P: **Milk is contained in this jug.**
A: This book interests me. $\rightarrow$ P: **I am interested in this book.** | --- ### 📒 Pattern 4.6: Interrogative Sentences (प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य) प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य का Passive रूप भी सदैव **प्रश्नवाचक ही रहता है** (प्रारम्भ में Helping Verb तथा अंत में '?' बना रहेगा)। #### 1. Yes/No Type (Helping Verb से प्रारम्भ होने वाले): - Active: $\text{Do / Does} + \text{Sub} + V_1 + \text{Obj}?$ $\rightarrow$ Passive: $\mathbf{\text{Is / Am / Are} + \text{Obj} + V_3 + \text{by} + \text{Sub}?}$ * *Active:* Do you play cricket? $\rightarrow$ **Is cricket played by you?** * *Active:* Does she write letters? $\rightarrow$ **Are letters written by her?** - Active: $\text{Did} + \text{Sub} + V_1 + \text{Obj}?$ $\rightarrow$ Passive: $\mathbf{\text{Was / Were} + \text{Obj} + V_3 + \text{by} + \text{Sub}?}$ * *Active:* Did you break this glass? $\rightarrow$ **Was this glass broken by you?** - Active: $\text{Has / Have / Had} + \text{Sub} + V_3 + \text{Obj}?$ $\rightarrow$ Passive: $\mathbf{\text{Has / Have / Had} + \text{Obj} + \mathbf{been} + V_3 + \text{by} + \text{Sub}?}$ * *Active:* Have you completed the project? $\rightarrow$ **Has the project been completed by you?** #### 2. Wh- Type Questions: Wh- शब्द (जैसे *Why, When, Where, How, What*) अपने स्थान पर यथावत रहेगा: $$\mathbf{\text{Wh-word} + \text{Helping Verb} + \text{Object} + V_3 + \text{by} + \text{Subject}?}$$ - *Active:* Why did you punish him? $\rightarrow$ **Why was he punished by you?** - *Active:* When will you return my camera? $\rightarrow$ **When will my camera be returned by you?** #### 3. 'Who' एवं 'Whom' वाले प्रश्न (Super-Important Rule!): - **Who $\rightarrow$ By whom + Helping Verb + Object + $V_3$?** * *Active:* Who wrote the Ramayana? $\rightarrow$ **By whom was the Ramayana written?** * *Active:* Who has broken this mirror? $\rightarrow$ **By whom has this mirror been broken?** - **Whom $\rightarrow$ Who + Helping Verb + $V_3$ + by + Subject?** * *Active:* Whom did you invite? $\rightarrow$ **Who was invited by you?** --- ### 📘 Pattern 4.7: Infinitive Structures ('to + $V_1$') & Going to - **Formula:** $\mathbf{\text{to} + V_1 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{to} + \mathbf{be} + V_3}$ * *Active:* I have to do this work. $\rightarrow$ **This work has to be done by me.** * *Active:* She has to write two essays. $\rightarrow$ **Two essays have to be written by her.** * *Active:* It is time to close the shop. $\rightarrow$ **It is time for the shop to be closed.** * *Active:* There is no money to spend. $\rightarrow$ **There is no money to be spent.** - **'Going to' Construction:** $$\mathbf{\text{Subject} + \text{be} + \text{going to} + V_1 + \text{Object} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{Object} + \text{be} + \text{going to} + \mathbf{be} + V_3 + \text{by} + \text{Sub}}$$ * *Active:* He is going to buy a new bicycle. $\rightarrow$ **A new bicycle is going to be bought by him.** * *Active:* They are going to build a hospital. $\rightarrow$ **A hospital is going to be built by them.** * *Active:* The teacher is going to ask questions. $\rightarrow$ **Questions are going to be asked by the teacher.** --- ### 📙 Pattern 4.8: Complex Sentences & "People say that..." Clauses (जटिल उपवाक्यों का वाच्य) जब Active वाक्य का ढांचा **"People say that...", "They believe that...", "We know that...", "Everyone considers that..."** जैसा हो, तो इसे Passive में बदलने की दो विधियां हैं: #### Method 1: "It is said that..." (सबसे लोकप्रिय एवं सरल तरीका): - **Active:** People say that honesty is the best policy. $\rightarrow$ **It is said that honesty is the best policy.** - **Active:** They believe that the ghost haunts the old palace. $\rightarrow$ **It is believed that the ghost haunts the old palace.** - **Active:** We know that hard work leads to success. $\rightarrow$ **It is known that hard work leads to success.** - **Active:** People expect that the prices will come down soon. $\rightarrow$ **It is expected that the prices will come down soon.** #### Method 2: Infinitive Construction (Subject-to-Subject Shift): $$\mathbf{\text{Subordinate Subject} + \text{is/are said to be} + \dots}$$ - **Active:** People say that he is a spy. $\rightarrow$ **He is said to be a spy.** - **Active:** People consider that the king was generous. $\rightarrow$ **The king is considered to have been generous.** --- ### 📕 Pattern 4.9: Prepositional Verbs / Phrasal Verbs (पूर्वसर्ग युक्त क्रियाएं) यदि Active वाक्य की क्रिया के साथ कोई Preposition या Adverb Particle स्थायी रूप से जुड़ा हो (जैसे: *look after, laugh at, look down upon, care for, break into, send for*), तो Passive Voice बनाते समय उस Preposition को **क्रिया के तुरंत बाद बनाए रखना अनिवार्य है**, और उसके बाद 'by' भी लगेगा: - *Active:* The girl laughed at the beggar. $\rightarrow$ **The beggar was laughed at by the girl.** (❌ *was laughed by the girl* लिखना बहुत बड़ी गलती है!) - *Active:* We must look after our elderly parents. $\rightarrow$ **Our elderly parents must be looked after by us.** - *Active:* The doctor sent for the compounder. $\rightarrow$ **The compounder was sent for by the doctor.** - *Active:* The police broke into the locked room. $\rightarrow$ **The locked room was broken into by the police.** - *Active:* You should not look down upon the poor. $\rightarrow$ **The poor should not be looked down upon by you.** --- ### 📓 Pattern 4.10: Contextual Board Dialogues & Passage-Based Voice (संवाद आधारित वाच्य रूपान्तरण) नवीनतम RBSE प्रश्नपत्रों में कभी-कभी दो व्यक्तियों के बीच संवाद (Dialogue) देकर रिक्त स्थान में Passive Voice भरने को कहा जाता है: #### संवाद मॉडल 1: - **Teacher:** Have you submitted the application form? - **Student:** Yes sir, the application form ______________________ (submit) by me yesterday. * **Answer:** **was submitted** (चूंकि 'yesterday' दिया गया है, अतः Past Simple Passive का प्रयोग हुआ)। #### संवाद मॉडल 2: - **Mother:** Why is there so much noise in the kitchen? - **Son:** Don't worry mother, tea ______________________ (prepare) by sister. * **Answer:** **is being prepared** (वर्तमान में कार्य चल रहा है $\rightarrow$ Present Continuous Passive)। #### संवाद मॉडल 3: - **Shopkeeper:** Can you pay the bill now? - **Customer:** The bill ______________________ (already pay) through UPI by my brother. * **Answer:** **has already been paid** (Present Perfect Passive)। --- ---
🚫 5. Mistake Busters: शीर्ष 6 गलतियां जिनसे छात्र अंक गंवाते हैं

1. **Mistake 1:** Tense बदल देना!
   * याद रखें: **Voice में Tense कभी नहीं बदलता!** (Present tense Present ही रहेगा, Past Past ही रहेगा)। छात्र Direct/Indirect Speech के भ्रम में Present को Past में बदल देते हैं, जो कि 100% गलत है।
   * ❌ *Wrong:* He writes a letter. $\rightarrow$ A letter was written by him.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* A letter **is written** by him.
2. **Mistake 2:** Continuous Tenses में 'being' भूल जाना!
   * Continuous Tense की Passive में **is/am/are/was/were के बाद 'being'** लगाना अनिवार्य है:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* She is singing a song. $\rightarrow$ A song is sung by her.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* A song **is being sung** by her.
3. **Mistake 3:** 'Please' वाले वाक्यों में 'Please' को यथावत छोड़ देना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* You are requested to please help me.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* You are requested to **help** me.
4. **Mistake 4:** 'Known' के साथ 'by' लगाना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* He is known by me.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* He is **known to** me.
5. **Mistake 5:** Interrogative Passive में Helping Verb को Subject के बाद लगा देना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* Was the glass broken by you? $\rightarrow$ Why the glass was broken by you?
   * ✔️ *Correct:* Why **was** the glass broken by you?
6. **Mistake 6:** 'Let' वाले वाक्यों में 'be' छोड़ देना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* Let the door closed.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* Let the door **be closed**.

14. They have renovated the old building.
15. The dog was chasing a rabbit.
16. We should obey our parents.
17. He will teach us mathematics.
18. Nobody can lift this heavy stone.
19. You ought to respect your teachers.
20. The doctor examined the patient carefully.
21. Farmers grow wheat in this field.
22. The hunter had shot a deer.
23. The mechanic is repairing the car.
24. Science has changed our lives completely.
25. We could hear their voices clearly.

### Set B: Two Objects & Imperative Sentences (Q26 – Q50)
26. Mr. Sharma gave me a watch.
27. The principal granted him a scholarship.
28. She teaches us Hindi every morning.
29. My uncle sent me a birthday gift.
30. The manager promised the workers a bonus.
31. Post this letter immediately.
32. Please help the blind man cross the street.
33. Do not make a noise in the library.
34. Obey your elders.
35. Kindly grant me leave for three days.
36. Switch off the lights before leaving.
37. Don't touch the live electric wire.
38. Help the needy.
39. Bring a glass of fresh water.
40. Please lend me your camera for a day.
41. Take this medicine twice a day.
42. Never tell a lie.
43. Inform the police of the accident.
44. Please sit down and wait for your turn.
45. Do not insult the poor.
46. Call the ambulance immediately.
47. Listen to your parents' advice.
48. Kindly check my answer sheet.
49. Do not cross the railway track.
50. Keep your promise.

### Set C: Interrogatives, Prepositions & Advanced Patterns (Q51 – Q70)
51. Do you know him?
52. Did she write this essay?
53. Have you finished the assignment?
54. Who taught you French?
55. Who broke the window pane?
56. Whom did you invite to the party?
57. Why did the teacher punish the boy?
58. When will they declare the result?
59. His sudden success surprised everyone.
60. This bottle contains pure honey.
61. The news shocked the whole village.
62. Her sweet voice pleased the audience.
63. I know Mr. Gupta very well.
64. Someone has picked my pocket.
65. People speak Spanish in South America.
66. They are going to inaugurate the new library tomorrow.
67. I have to finish this task today.
68. It is time to say prayers.
69. Smoke filled the cinema hall.
70. Rose smells sweet.

---
🔑 Complete Answer Key & Explanatory Notes (Q1 – Q70)

### Set A Solutions:
1. **The room is cleaned by her every day.** (Present Simple $\rightarrow$ is + $V_3$)
2. **The wall is being built by the mason.** (Present Continuous $\rightarrow$ is being + $V_3$)
3. **The letters have been delivered by the postman.** (Present Perfect $\rightarrow$ have been + $V_3$)
4. **A mouse was killed by the cat.** (Past Simple $\rightarrow$ was + $V_3$)
5. **A horror movie was being watched by them.** (Past Continuous $\rightarrow$ was being + $V_3$)
6. **Their homework had been completed by the students.** (Past Perfect $\rightarrow$ had been + $V_3$)
7. **All our friends will be invited by us.** (Future Simple $\rightarrow$ will be + $V_3$)
8. **By next year, the project will have been completed by them.** (Future Perfect $\rightarrow$ will have been + $V_3$)
9. **The safety rules must be followed by you.** (Modal must $\rightarrow$ must be + $V_3$)
10. **This difficult problem can be solved by the teacher.** (Modal can $\rightarrow$ can be + $V_3$)
11. **Animals are loved by children.**
12. **The thief was not caught by the police.** (Past Simple negative $\rightarrow$ was not + $V_3$)
13. **An interesting story is being written by her.**
14. **The old building has been renovated by them.**
15. **A rabbit was being chased by the dog.**
16. **Our parents should be obeyed by us.**
17. **We will be taught mathematics by him.** / **Mathematics will be taught to us by him.**
18. **This heavy stone cannot be lifted.** (*Nobody* converted to negative modal)
19. **Your teachers ought to be respected by you.**
20. **The patient was examined carefully by the doctor.**
21. **Wheat is grown in this field by farmers.**
22. **A deer had been shot by the hunter.**
23. **The car is being repaired by the mechanic.**
24. **Our lives have been changed completely by science.**
25. **Their voices could be heard clearly by us.**

### Set B Solutions:
26. **I was given a watch by Mr. Sharma.** (or: *A watch was given to me by Mr. Sharma.*)
27. **He was granted a scholarship by the principal.**
28. **We are taught Hindi by her every morning.** (or: *Hindi is taught to us by her...*)
29. **I was sent a birthday gift by my uncle.**
30. **The workers were promised a bonus by the manager.**
31. **Let this letter be posted immediately.**
32. **You are requested to help the blind man cross the street.**
33. **You are requested not to make a noise in the library.** / **Let a noise not be made in the library.**
34. **Your elders should be obeyed.**
35. **You are requested to grant me leave for three days.**
36. **Let the lights be switched off before leaving.**
37. **You are forbidden to touch the live electric wire.** / **Let the live electric wire not be touched.**
38. **The needy should be helped.**
39. **Let a glass of fresh water be brought.**
40. **You are requested to lend me your camera for a day.**
41. **You are advised to take this medicine twice a day.**
42. **A lie should never be told.** / **Let a lie never be told.**
43. **Let the police be informed of the accident.**
44. **You are requested to sit down and wait for your turn.**
45. **The poor should not be insulted.** / **Let the poor not be insulted.**
46. **Let the ambulance be called immediately.**
47. **Your parents' advice should be listened to.**
48. **You are requested to check my answer sheet.**
49. **You are forbidden to cross the railway track.**
50. **Promises should be kept.** / **Let your promise be kept.**

### Set C Solutions:
51. **Is he known to you?** (Do $\rightarrow$ Is; *known to*, not *by*)
52. **Was this essay written by her?** (Did $\rightarrow$ Was)
53. **Has the assignment been finished by you?** (Have $\rightarrow$ Has ... been)
54. **By whom were you taught French?** / **Who were you taught French by?**
55. **By whom was the window pane broken?**
56. **Who was invited to the party by you?** (Whom $\rightarrow$ Who)
57. **Why was the boy punished by the teacher?**
58. **When will the result be declared by them?**
59. **Everyone was surprised at his sudden success.** (*surprised at*, not *by*)
60. **Pure honey is contained in this bottle.** (*contained in*, not *by*)
61. **The whole village was shocked at the news.** (*shocked at*, not *by*)
62. **The audience was pleased with her sweet voice.** (*pleased with*, not *by*)
63. **Mr. Gupta is well known to me.** (*known to*)
64. **My pocket has been picked.** (*someone* omitted)
65. **Spanish is spoken in South America.** (*people* omitted)
66. **The new library is going to be inaugurated tomorrow.** (*they* omitted)
67. **This task has to be finished by me today.**
68. **It is time for prayers to be said.**
69. **The cinema hall was filled with smoke.** (*filled with*)
70. **Rose is sweet when it is smelt.** (Quasi-passive / Middle voice)

---
⚡ 8. Pre-Exam 2-Minute Rapid Revision Cheat Sheet

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Active Structure                                       │ Passive Verb Formula                     │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Present Simple: V1 / does / do                         │ is / am / are + V3                       │
│ Present Continuous: is/am/are + V4                     │ is / am / are + BEING + V3               │
│ Present Perfect: has / have + V3                       │ has / have + BEEN + V3                   │
│ Past Simple: V2 / did + not                            │ was / were + V3                          │
│ Past Continuous: was / were + V4                       │ was / were + BEING + V3                  │
│ Past Perfect: had + V3                                 │ had + BEEN + V3                          │
│ Future Simple: will / shall + V1                       │ will / shall + BE + V3                   │
│ Modals: can / may / must / should + V1                 │ modal + BE + V3                          │
│ Imperative: Order / Command                            │ Let + Obj + BE + V3                      │
│ Imperative: Request (Please / Kindly)                  │ You are requested to + V1                │
│ Imperative: Advice / Moral Duty                        │ Obj + SHOULD BE + V3                     │
│ Known / Married                                        │ to (He is known TO me)                   │
│ Surprised / Shocked / Astonished                       │ at (I was surprised AT...)               │
│ Pleased / Satisfied / Filled                           │ with (Pleased WITH...)                   │
│ Contained / Interested                                 │ in (Contained IN...)                     │
│ Who wrote ...?                                         │ By whom was ... written?                 │
│ Unimportant Agents (someone, people, they, nobody)    │ Omit agent (Nobody -> add 'not')         │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---
📝 9. Final practice test: 10 points (not an RBSE exam simulation)

**समय:** 15 मिनट | **पूर्णांक:** 10 अंक (1 Mark each)  
*निर्देश: Change the following sentences into Passive Voice.*

1. The police arrested two notorious thieves yesterday.
2. Please don't disturb me right now.
3. She gave him a useful dictionary on his birthday.
4. Who broke this antique flowerpot?
5. The mechanic has repaired our motorcycle.
6. We should protect the wild animals.
7. Shut all the classroom windows immediately.
8. His arrogant behaviour shocked the headmaster.
9. They are laying the foundation stone tomorrow.
10. Can you solve this puzzle?

---

### 📋 Test Marking Scheme & Solutions:
1. **Two notorious thieves were arrested yesterday.** [1 Mark] — Past Simple ($V_2$) $\rightarrow$ were + $V_3$; agent *by the police* omitted.
2. **You are requested not to disturb me right now.** [1 Mark] — Please imperative negative transformation.
3. **He was given a useful dictionary on his birthday by her.** [1 Mark] — (or: *A useful dictionary was given to him on his birthday by her.*)
4. **By whom was this antique flowerpot broken?** [1 Mark] — Who $\rightarrow$ By whom + was + Object + $V_3$?
5. **Our motorcycle has been repaired by the mechanic.** [1 Mark] — Present Perfect $\rightarrow$ has been + $V_3$.
6. **The wild animals should be protected by us.** [1 Mark] — Modal should $\rightarrow$ should be + $V_3$.
7. **Let all the classroom windows be shut immediately.** [1 Mark] — Imperative order $\rightarrow$ Let + Obj + be + $V_3$.
8. **The headmaster was shocked at his arrogant behaviour.** [1 Mark] — Shocked takes preposition *at*, not *by*.
9. **The foundation stone is being laid tomorrow.** [1 Mark] — Present Continuous $\rightarrow$ is being + $V_3$; agent *they* omitted.
10. **Can this puzzle be solved by you?** [1 Mark] — Interrogative modal $\rightarrow$ Can + Obj + be + $V_3$ + by + you?

chapters.title: RBSE Class 10 English Grammar: Unit 4 — Direct and Indirect Speech (Reported Speech)

content.value: माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर (कक्षा 10वीं — अंग्रेजी अनिवार्य)

### 🎯 पाठ्यक्रम भार: Reported Speech के लिए 2 अंक (2026–27 RBSE syllabus)

---
🧭 1. Reported Speech: scope and practice guidance

RBSE 2026–27 English syllabus में Reported Speech के लिए 2 अंक निर्धारित है। Grammar का कुल आवंटन 8 अंक है। Syllabus में statements, questions, commands और requests का scope है; प्रश्न का exact format निश्चित नहीं है। नीचे के रूपांतरण अभ्यास हैं।
- **अभ्यास का स्वरूप:** Direct/Indirect Speech और संवाद-रूपांतरण से अभ्यास करें; प्रश्न में जो निर्देश हों, उनका पालन करें।
- **Direct Speech (प्रत्यक्ष कथन):** जब वक्ता (Speaker) के कहे हुए शब्दों को बिना किसी परिवर्तन के ज्यों-का-त्यों उद्धरण चिह्नों (Inverted Commas `“ ”`) के भीतर लिखा जाता है:
  * *Example:* Ram said to Mohan, "I am going to Jaipur today."
  * यहाँ `Ram` = Speaker (Reporting Subject)
  * `said to` = Reporting Verb (RV)
  * `Mohan` = Listener (Reporting Object)
  * `"I am going to Jaipur today."` = Reported Speech (RS)
- **Indirect Speech (अप्रत्यक्ष कथन):** जब वक्ता के कहे हुए शब्दों को Inverted Commas हटाकर, अपने शब्दों में, आवश्यक काल (Tense), सर्वनाम (Pronoun) और निकटता-सूचक शब्दों में परिवर्तन करके प्रस्तुत किया जाता है:
  * *Example:* Ram told Mohan that he was going to Jaipur that day.

---
⚡ 2. The 5 Universal Golden Rules of Indirect Speech Transformation

Direct Speech से Indirect Speech बनाते समय निम्नलिखित 5 बुनियादी नियमों का क्रमवार पालन किया जाता है:

```
[चरण 1] Reporting Verb (RV) में परिवर्तन (वाक्य के प्रकार के अनुसार: told, asked, ordered, आदि)।
                                    ▼
[चरण 2] Comma (,) और Inverted Commas (" ") को हटाकर उपयुक्त Conjunction (that, if/whether, to, Wh-word) लगाना।
                                    ▼
[चरण 3] सर्वनाम (Pronouns) में परिवर्तन (SON फॉर्मूला के अनुसार)।
                                    ▼
[चरण 4] Tense (काल) में परिवर्तन (यदि RV Past Tense में हो और कोई अपवाद न हो)।
                                    ▼
[चरण 5] निकटता-सूचक शब्दों (Time & Distance words) को दूरी-सूचक शब्दों में बदलना।
```

---
🔄 3. Pronoun Change: The Revolutionary "SON" Formula

सर्वनामों का परिवर्तन Reported Speech के वक्ता और श्रोता के संबंध को स्पष्ट करता है। इसे **SON / 123 फॉर्मूला** द्वारा सरलता से याद रखा जा सकता है: $$\mathbf{\frac{S \quad O \quad N}{1 \quad 2 \quad 3}}$$ - **1 (First Person: I, me, my, mine, we, us, our, ours):** * Reporting Verb के **Subject (S)** के अनुसार बदलता है। * *Example:* **He** said, "I like apples." $\rightarrow$ He said that **he** liked apples. - **2 (Second Person: You, you, your, yours):** * Reporting Verb के **Object (O)** के अनुसार बदलता है। * *Example:* Ram said to **me**, "You are my friend." $\rightarrow$ Ram told me that **I** was his friend. * *⚠️ Note:* यदि Reporting Verb में कोई Object न दिया हो और RS में 2nd Person (*you*) आए, तो आवश्यकतानुसार 1st Person (*me*) या 3rd Person (*him/her*) को काल्पनिक Object मान लिया जाता है। - **3 (Third Person: He, him, his, She, her, It, its, They, them, their, Any Name):** * इसमें कोई परिवर्तन नहीं होता (**N = No Change**)। * *Example:* Mohan said, "**She** is dancing." $\rightarrow$ Mohan said that **she** was dancing. ### 📋 Complete Pronoun Paradigm Table: | Person | Nominative (Subject) | Objective (Object) | Possessive Adjective | Possessive Pronoun | Reflexive Pronoun | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | **1st Person** | I
We | me
us | my
our | mine
ours | myself
ourselves | | **2nd Person** | You | you | your | yours | yourself / yourselves | | **3rd Person** | He
She
It
They | him

it

hers
—
theirs | himself
herself

themselves | ---
🕰️ 4. Tense Backshifting Rules & Master Conversion Table

> 🛑 **The Master Condition:** Tense में परिवर्तन **केवल और केवल तभी** होता है जब Reporting Verb भूतकाल (**Past Tense — said / said to**) में हो! > यदि Reporting Verb **Present Tense (says, say, has said)** अथवा **Future Tense (will say, shall say)** में हो, तो Reported Speech का Tense **कभी नहीं बदलता!** ### 📊 Master Tense Backshift Matrix (जब RV Past Tense में हो): | Direct Speech Tense | Indirect Speech Tense | Active Form Change | |---|---|---| | **Present Simple** | **Past Simple** | $V_1 / (V_1+s/es) \longrightarrow V_2$
`do / does + not` $\longrightarrow$ `did + not + V1` | | **Present Continuous** | **Past Continuous** | `is / am / are` $\longrightarrow$ `was / were` | | **Present Perfect** | **Past Perfect** | `has / have` $\longrightarrow$ `had` | | **Present Perfect Continuous** | **Past Perfect Continuous** | `has been / have been` $\longrightarrow$ `had been` | | **Past Simple** | **Past Perfect** | $V_2 \longrightarrow \mathbf{had} + V_3$
`did + not + V1` $\longrightarrow$ `had + not + V3` | | **Past Continuous** | **Past Perfect Continuous** | `was / were` $\longrightarrow$ **had been** | | **Past Perfect** | **No Change** | `had + V3` $\longrightarrow$ `had + V3` (यथावत) | | **Past Perfect Continuous** | **No Change** | `had been + V4` $\longrightarrow$ `had been + V4` (यथावत) | ### 🛠️ Modal Auxiliaries Backshifting: - **will** $\longrightarrow$ **would** - **shall** $\longrightarrow$ **should / would** - **can** $\longrightarrow$ **could** - **may** $\longrightarrow$ **might** - **must** $\longrightarrow$ **had to / must** (नैतिक कर्तव्य में *must* ही रहता है; वर्तमान बाध्यता में *had to*) - *would, should, could, might, ought to, used to* $\longrightarrow$ **No Change** (यथावत रहते हैं) ---
🚫 5. Vital Exceptions to Tense Backshift (जब Tense बिल्कुल नहीं बदलता!)

चाहे Reporting Verb **Past Tense (said / said to)** में ही क्यों न हो, निम्नलिखित 5 स्थितियों में Reported Speech का Tense **यथावत (No Change)** रहता है:

### 1. सार्वभौमिक सत्य (Universal Truth / Astronomical Facts):
- *Direct:* The teacher said, "The sun rises in the east."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The teacher said that the sun **rises** in the east. (❌ rose नहीं होगा!)
- *Direct:* He said, "The earth revolves round the sun."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** He said that the earth **revolves** round the sun.

### 2. वैज्ञानिक तथ्य या शाश्वत नियम (Scientific Fact / Natural Law):
- *Direct:* The professor said, "Water boils at $100^\circ\text{C}$."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The professor said that water **boils** at $100^\circ\text{C}$.
- *Direct:* Father said, "Oil floats on water."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** Father said that oil **floats** on water.

### 3. आदतन क्रिया या स्थायी स्वभाव (Habitual Action / Routine):
- *Direct:* She said, "I take a bath in cold water daily."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** She said that she **takes** a bath in cold water daily.
- *Direct:* Mohan said, "Dogs bark at strangers."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** Mohan said that dogs **bark** at strangers.

### 4. ऐतिहासिक सत्य (Historical Truth / Event):
- *Direct:* The teacher said, "India became free on 15th August, 1947."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The teacher said that India **became** free on 15th August, 1947.
- *Direct:* He said, "Samudragupta is called the Napoleon of India."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** He said that Samudragupta **is called** the Napoleon of India.

### 5. लोकोक्तियाँ एवं मुहावरे (Proverbs / Idioms):
- *Direct:* My grandfather said, "Honesty is the best policy."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** My grandfather said that honesty **is** the best policy.
- *Direct:* The saint said, "Slow and steady wins the race."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The saint said that slow and steady **wins** the race.

### 6. RV Present या Future Tense में होना:
- *Direct:* Ram **says**, "I am unwell."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** Ram says that he **is** unwell. (❌ was नहीं होगा!)
- *Direct:* She **will say**, "I cannot attend the meeting."  
  $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** She will say that she **cannot** attend the meeting.

---
🗺️ 6. Changes in Words Expressing Nearness of Time & Place

Direct Speech में प्रयुक्त समय एवं दूरी के निकटता-सूचक शब्द Indirect Speech में दूरी-सूचक शब्दों में बदल जाते हैं:

| Direct Speech | Indirect Speech |
|:---:|:---:|
| **this** | **that** |
| **these** | **those** |
| **here** | **there** |
| **now** | **then** |
| **today** | **that day** |
| **yesterday** | **the previous day** / **the day before** |
| **tomorrow** | **the next day** / **the following day** |
| **last night / week / month** | **the previous night / week / month** |
| **next week / month / year** | **the following week / month / year** |
| **ago** | **before** |
| **thus** | **so** |
| **tonight** | **that night** |
| **come** (दिशा में परिवर्तन होने पर) | **go** |

---
🔍 7. Sentence-Type Comprehensive Breakdown & Golden Formulas

### 📘 Type 1: Assertive Sentences (साधारण एवं नकारात्मक कथन)
- **Reporting Verb Rules:**
  * `said` $\longrightarrow$ `said` (यथावत रहता है यदि कोई Object न हो)
  * `said to + Object` $\longrightarrow$ `told + Object` ('told' के बाद 'to' कभी नहीं लगता!)
  * `says to` $\longrightarrow$ `tells` | `say to` $\longrightarrow$ `tell`
- **Conjunction:** **that**
- **Examples:**
  * *Direct:* Ramesh said to Mohan, "I have finished my work today."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** Ramesh told Mohan **that** he had finished his work **that day**.
  * *Direct:* She said, "I do not like sweets."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** She said **that** she did not like sweets.
  * *Direct:* He said to me, "You wrote a good poem yesterday."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** He told me **that** I had written a good poem **the previous day**. ($V_2 \rightarrow \text{had} + V_3$)

---

### 📗 Type 2: Interrogative Sentences (प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य — अभ्यास प्रकार)
प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य दो प्रकार के होते हैं:

#### Pattern A: Helping Verb (Yes/No Questions) से प्रारम्भ होने वाले वाक्य:
- **Reporting Verb:** `said / said to` $\longrightarrow$ **asked** (अथवा *inquired of*)
- **Conjunction:** **if** अथवा **whether** (साधारणतः 'if' का प्रयोग करें)
- **The Golden Interrogative Rule (अति महत्वपूर्ण):**
  $$\mathbf{\text{Interrogative Form} \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \text{Assertive Form (Subject + Helping Verb)}}$$
  Indirect Speech में प्रश्न चिह्न (?) हटाकर **Full Stop (.)** लगाया जाता है!
  * *Direct:* He said to me, "Are you reading a novel?"  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** He asked me **if I was** reading a novel. (❌ *if was I* लिखना सबसे बड़ा ब्लंडर है!)
  * *Direct:* She said to him, "Did you attend the school yesterday?"  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** She asked him **if he had attended** the school the previous day. (Did $\rightarrow$ had + $V_3$)
  * *Direct:* Mother said to Rohit, "Do you want some milk?"  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** Mother asked Rohit **if he wanted** some milk. (Do + want $\rightarrow$ wanted)

#### Pattern B: Wh- Words (What, Where, When, Why, Who, Which, How) से प्रारम्भ होने वाले वाक्य:
- **Reporting Verb:** `said / said to` $\longrightarrow$ **asked**
- **Conjunction:** **कोई अतिरिक्त Conjunction ('that' या 'if') नहीं लगता!** वह Wh- शब्द स्वयं Conjunction का कार्य करता है।
- **Formula:** $\mathbf{\text{asked} + \text{Object} + \text{Wh-word} + \mathbf{Subject} + \mathbf{Verb} + \dots}$
  * *Direct:* The teacher said to Mohan, "Why are you late today?"  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The teacher asked Mohan **why he was** late that day.
  * *Direct:* I said to the stranger, "Where do you live?"  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** I asked the stranger **where he lived**.
  * *Direct:* He said to me, "What is your name?"  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** He asked me **what my name was**.

---

### 📙 Type 3: Imperative Sentences (आज्ञा, प्रार्थना, परामर्श एवं निषेध)
आज्ञावाचक वाक्यों में Subject 'you' छिपा रहता है और वाक्य क्रिया के प्रथम रूप ($V_1$) से शुरू होता है।
- **Reporting Verb (भाव के अनुसार):**
  * आज्ञा/आदेश $\longrightarrow$ **ordered / commanded**
  * प्रार्थना/निवेदन $\longrightarrow$ **requested** (Please/Kindly को हटा दें)
  * सलाह/परामर्श $\longrightarrow$ **advised / urged**
  * मनाही/निषेध $\longrightarrow$ **forbade** (सावधान: forbidden में 'not' नहीं आता)
- **Conjunction (Connector):**
  * Affirmative $\longrightarrow$ **to + $V_1$**
  * Negative (Don't) $\longrightarrow$ **not to + $V_1$** (अथवा *forbade + to + $V_1$*)
- **Examples:**
  * *Direct:* The teacher said to the boys, "Stand up on the bench."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The teacher **ordered** the boys **to stand up** on the bench.
  * *Direct:* The beggar said to me, "Please give me some food."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The beggar **requested** me **to give** him some food.
  * *Direct:* The doctor said to the patient, "Take this medicine regularly."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The doctor **advised** the patient **to take** that medicine regularly.
  * *Direct:* Father said to his son, "Do not waste your precious time."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect (Method 1):** Father **advised** his son **not to waste** his precious time.  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect (Method 2):** Father **forbade** his son **to waste** his precious time.

---

### 📕 Type 4: Sentences Beginning with "Let" (Let वाले विशेष वाक्य)

#### Case A: 'Let us' (Proposal / Suggestion — प्रस्ताव या सुझाव):
- Reporting Verb: `said to` $\longrightarrow$ **proposed to / suggested to** ('to' बना रहता है)
- Conjunction: **that**
- 'Let us' को बदलकर: **we should** (यदि वक्ता/श्रोता में 1st person हो) अथवा **they should** लिखें।
  * *Direct:* Mohan said to his friends, "Let us play a cricket match."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** Mohan **suggested to** his friends **that they should play** a cricket match.
  * *Direct:* I said to him, "Let us go for a walk."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** I **proposed to** him **that we should go** for a walk.

#### Case B: 'Let me / him / her' (Permission / Request / Order — अनुमति या प्रार्थना):
- Reporting Verb: **requested / ordered / told**
- Connector: **to let...** (अथवा *that he might be allowed to...*)
  * *Direct:* The peon said to the principal, "Let me go home early."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The peon **requested** the principal **to let him go** home early.

---

### 📓 Type 5: Exclamatory Sentences (विस्मयादिबोधक वाक्य)
हर्ष, शोक, आश्चर्य, प्रशंसा या घृणा व्यक्त करने वाले वाक्य जिनमें विस्मयादिबोधक चिह्न (!) लगा होता है।
- **Reporting Verb (भाव के अनुसार):**
  * 'Hurrah!' (हर्ष) $\longrightarrow$ **exclaimed with joy / delight**
  * 'Alas!' (शोक/दुःख) $\longrightarrow$ **exclaimed with sorrow / grief**
  * 'What / How' (आश्चर्य) $\longrightarrow$ **exclaimed with surprise / wonder**
  * 'Bravo!' (प्रशंसा) $\longrightarrow$ **applauded + Object + saying that...**
- **Conjunction:** **that**
- **Word Order:** विस्मयादिबोधक शब्दों (*Hurrah, Alas, Wow*) को हटाकर वाक्य को साधारण (Assertive) बनाया जाता है। 'What a / How' के स्थान पर **very / great** का प्रयोग होता है:
  * *Direct:* The captain said, "Hurrah! We have won the tournament."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The captain **exclaimed with joy that they had won** the tournament.
  * *Direct:* The poor woman said, "Alas! My only child is dead."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The poor woman **exclaimed with sorrow that her only child was dead**.
  * *Direct:* She said, "What a beautiful flower it is!"  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** She **exclaimed with surprise that it was a very beautiful flower**.
  * *Direct:* The teacher said to Rohit, "Bravo! You have scored full marks."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The teacher **applauded Rohit saying that he had scored** full marks.

---

### 📒 Type 6: Optative Sentences (इच्छा, प्रार्थना एवं शुभकामना)
- **Reporting Verb:** `wished / prayed / cursed`
- **Conjunction:** **that**
- **Formula:** $\mathbf{\text{Subject} + \mathbf{might} + V_1}$
  * *Direct:* The old hermit said, "May you live long!"  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** The old hermit **prayed that I might live long**.
  * *Direct:* They said to us, "Good morning! Have a nice day."  
    $\rightarrow$ **Indirect:** They **wished us a good morning** and wished that we might have a nice day.

🚫 8. Mistake Busters: शीर्ष 7 गंभीर गलतियां और उनका निवारण

1. **Mistake 1: Conjunction 'That' का अनावश्यक प्रयोग:**
   * Interrogative या Imperative वाक्यों में 'that' कभी नहीं लगता!
   * ❌ *Wrong:* He asked me that if I was ready.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* He asked me **if** I was ready.
   * ❌ *Wrong:* The doctor told that to take medicine.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* The doctor advised me **to take** medicine.
2. **Mistake 2: Interrogative क्रम को न बदलना (The Word Order Blunder):**
   * Indirect Speech में Wh- शब्द या 'if' के बाद हमेशा **पहले Subject** आता है, फिर Verb!
   * ❌ *Wrong:* She asked me what was my name.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* She asked me what **my name was**.
3. **Mistake 3: 'Told' के साथ 'to' लगाना:**
   * ❌ *Wrong:* Ram told to Mohan that he was ill.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* Ram **told Mohan** that he was ill.
4. **Mistake 4: Universal Truth में Tense बदल देना:**
   * ❌ *Wrong:* The teacher said that the earth was round.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* The teacher said that the earth **is** round.
5. **Mistake 5: 'Forbade' के साथ 'not' लगाना (Double Negative):**
   * ❌ *Wrong:* Father forbade me not to go there.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* Father **forbade me to go** there.
6. **Mistake 6: Inverted Commas और Question Mark को बनाए रखना:**
   * Indirect Speech में उद्धरण चिह्न (" ") और प्रश्न चिह्न (?) पूरी तरह हटा दिए जाते हैं और अंत में केवल **Full Stop (.)** आता है।
7. **Mistake 7: RV Present में होने पर भी Tense बदलना:**
   * ❌ *Wrong:* He says that he was honest.
   * ✔️ *Correct:* He **says that he is** honest.

2. **Practice set:** Ramesh said to me, "Why did you not attend my birthday party?"
   * **Indirect:** **Ramesh asked me why I had not attended his birthday party.**
   * *कारण:* Wh- question $\rightarrow$ asked + why + Subject (I) + had not attended ($V_2 \rightarrow \text{had} + V_3$).
3. **Practice set:** Rohit said to his friend, "Please lend me your bicycle for two days."
   * **Indirect:** **Rohit requested his friend to lend him his bicycle for two days.**
   * *कारण:* Please $\rightarrow$ requested + to lend; 'your' $\rightarrow$ 'his'.
4. **Practice set:** She said, "I have completed my science project."
   * **Indirect:** **She said that she had completed her science project.**
   * *कारण:* Present Perfect (have completed) $\rightarrow$ Past Perfect (had completed).
5. **Practice set:** The doctor said to the patient, "Take these tablets twice daily."
   * **Indirect:** **The doctor advised the patient to take those tablets twice daily.**
   * *कारण:* Imperative advice $\rightarrow$ advised + to take; 'these' $\rightarrow$ 'those'.
6. **Practice set:** Mohan said to me, "Do you know swimming?"
   * **Indirect:** **Mohan asked me if I knew swimming.**
   * *कारण:* Helping verb question $\rightarrow$ asked + if + I knew ($V_1 \rightarrow V_2$).
7. **Practice set:** The teacher said to Suresh, "Stand up on your bench."
   * **Indirect:** **The teacher ordered Suresh to stand up on his bench.**
8. **Practice set:** She said to me, "Where are you going right now?"
   * **Indirect:** **She asked me where I was going right then.**
   * *कारण:* where + I was going; 'now' $\rightarrow$ 'then'.
9. **Practice set:** Father said to Mohan, "Do not waste your time in idle gossip."
   * **Indirect:** **Father advised Mohan not to waste his time in idle gossip.** (अथवा: *Father forbade Mohan to waste his time...*)
10. **Practice set:** He said, "Alas! My best friend met with an accident."
    * **Indirect:** **He exclaimed with sorrow that his best friend had met with an accident.**

    * **Indirect:** **The principal ordered the peon to ring the bell immediately.**
12. **Practice set:** Sita said to Geeta, "Will you help me in my homework?"
    * **Indirect:** **Sita asked Geeta if she would help her in her homework.**
13. **Practice set:** He said to me, "I am writing an essay now."
    * **Indirect:** **He told me that he was writing an essay then.**
14. **Practice set:** The captain said, "Bravo! You played exceedingly well."
    * **Indirect:** **The captain applauded the team saying that they had played exceedingly well.**
15. **Practice set:** My friend said to me, "Have you ever visited the Taj Mahal?"
    * **Indirect:** **My friend asked me if I had ever visited the Taj Mahal.**
16. **Practice set:** The saint said, "Man proposes, God disposes."
    * **Indirect:** **The saint said that man proposes, God disposes.** (Proverb $\rightarrow$ No change).
17. **Practice set:** He said to his servant, "Bring a cup of hot tea."
    * **Indirect:** **He ordered his servant to bring a cup of hot tea.**
18. **Practice set:** Mother said to me, "Why are you crying?"
    * **Indirect:** **Mother asked me why I was crying.**
19. **Practice set:** The old man said to the boy, "May God bless you with a long life!"
    * **Indirect:** **The old man prayed that God might bless the boy with a long life.**
