### 📋 Test Marking Scheme & Solutions:
1. **The teacher told the students that the sun gives us light and energy.** [1 Mark] — Universal scientific fact; tense unchanged.
2. **He asked me if I had seen the match on television the previous day.** [1 Mark] — Yes/No interrogative; did $\rightarrow$ had seen; yesterday $\rightarrow$ the previous day.
3. **She requested her brother to give her his laptop for an hour.** [1 Mark] — Imperative request with please.
4. **The officer ordered the peon to bring that confidential file immediately.** [1 Mark] — Imperative order $\rightarrow$ ordered + to bring.
5. **Mohan asked Rohit why he was wasting his precious time.** [1 Mark] — Wh- question word order $\rightarrow$ why + he was wasting.
6. **The boys exclaimed with joy that the next day was a holiday.** [1 Mark] — Exclamatory with joy; tomorrow $\rightarrow$ the next day.
7. **The saint told the disciple that man is mortal.** [1 Mark] — Universal philosophical truth; tense unchanged.
8. **Father advised his son not to run in the scorching sun.** [1 Mark] — (or: *Father forbade his son to run...*).
9. **She told me that she had been waiting for me since 2 o'clock.** [1 Mark] — Present Perfect Continuous $\rightarrow$ Past Perfect Continuous.
10. **The doctor advised the patient to take complete rest for a week.** [1 Mark] — Imperative medical advice.

**Syllabus source correction, 13 October 2026:** Scope/marks above use the [Madhyamik Class 10 syllabus, PDF pp. 3–5](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf), not the separate Praveshika scheme. This correction does not certify the remaining exercise keys.

chapters.title: RBSE Class 10 English Grammar: Unit 5 — Clauses, Framing Questions & Question Tags

content.value: माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर (कक्षा 10वीं — अंग्रेजी अनिवार्य)

### 🎯 पाठ्यक्रम स्थिति: Clauses and Question Tags current RBSE grammar list में नहीं; यह enrichment practice है

---
🧭 1. Supplementary grammar practice

यह अतिरिक्त grammar practice तीन परस्पर संबद्ध घटकों को समझाती है:
1. **Relative Clauses (संबंधवाचक उपवाक्य):** दो clauses को उपयुक्त relative pronoun (*who, whom, whose, which, that*) अथवा relative adverb (*where, when, why*) से जोड़ना।
2. **Framing Questions (प्रश्न निर्माण):** दिए गए कथन/उत्तर से उपयुक्त प्रश्न बनाना।
3. **Question Tags (लघु पुछल्ले प्रश्न):** कथन के अंत में संक्षिप्त tag जोड़ना।

यह इकाई अतिरिक्त व्याकरण-अभ्यास देती है। Clauses और question tags वर्तमान RBSE 2026–27 grammar list में अलग से निर्दिष्ट नहीं हैं; इनसे किसी निश्चित अंक की उम्मीद न करें।

---
🔗 PART A: RELATIVE CLAUSES (संबंधवाचक उपवाक्य)

### 📌 2. Relative Pronouns & Adverbs Master Matrix

Relative Clause वह आश्रित उपवाक्य (Dependent Clause) है जो अपने पूर्ववर्ती संज्ञा या सर्वनाम (**Antecedent**) की विशेषता बताता है या उसके विषय में अतिरिक्त सूचना प्रदान करता है।

| शब्द (Connector) | किसके लिए प्रयुक्त होता है? (Antecedent Reference) | व्याकरणिक भूमिका (Grammatical Role) | आदर्श उदाहरण (Model Sentence) |
|:---:|---|---|---|
| **WHO** | केवल व्यक्तियों (Persons) के लिए | **Subjective (कर्ता कारक)** — इसके तुरंत बाद Verb आती है | The boy **who** won the race is my cousin. |
| **WHOM** | केवल व्यक्तियों (Persons) के लिए | **Objective (कर्म कारक)** — इसके तुरंत बाद Subject + Verb आती है | The girl **whom** you met yesterday is my sister. |
| **WHOSE** | व्यक्तियों एवं सजीवों के लिए (अधिकार दर्शाने हेतु) | **Possessive (संबंध कारक)** — इसके तुरंत बाद Noun आता है | The man **whose** car was stolen has reported to the police. |
| **WHICH** | वस्तुओं (Things), पशुओं (Animals) एवं पक्षियों के लिए | Subjective अथवा Objective | The book **which** is on the table is mine. |
| **THAT** | व्यक्तियों, वस्तुओं एवं पशुओं दोनों के लिए (विशेष शर्तों में) | Subjective अथवा Objective | All **that** glitters is not gold. |
| **WHERE** | स्थानों (Places) के लिए | Relative Adverb (स्थान-सूचक) | This is the school **where** I studied. |
| **WHEN** | समय (Time) के लिए | Relative Adverb (समय-सूचक) | It was 2020 **when** the pandemic started. |
| **WHY** | कारणों (Reasons) के लिए | Relative Adverb (कारण-सूचक) | This is the reason **why** he left early. |

---

### 🛠️ 3. Step-by-Step Sentence Synthesis Rules (दो वाक्यों को जोड़ने की विधि)

#### 📘 Rule A.1: 'WHO' द्वारा दो वाक्यों को जोड़ना
- **नियम:** 'Who' का प्रयोग व्यक्तियों के लिए होता है। दूसरे वाक्य में पहले वाक्य के व्यक्ति के लिए आए सर्वनाम (*he, she, they*) को हटाकर उसके स्थान पर 'Who' लगाया जाता है।
- **स्थिति 1 (जब Antecedent पहले वाक्य का कर्ता हो):**
  * Sentence 1: *The boy is my brother.*
  * Sentence 2: *He is standing there.*
  * Synthesis: **The boy who is standing there is my brother.**
- **स्थिति 2 (जब Antecedent पहले वाक्य का कर्म हो):**
  * Sentence 1: *I know the doctor.*
  * Sentence 2: *He treated your father.*
  * Synthesis: **I know the doctor who treated your father.**

#### 📗 Rule A.2: 'WHOM' द्वारा जोड़ना
- **नियम:** 'Whom' का प्रयोग कर्म (Object) के रूप में होता है। दूसरे वाक्य में आए कर्म कारक सर्वनाम (*him, her, them*) को पूरी तरह हटा दिया जाता है।
  * Sentence 1: *The lady is a renowned teacher.*
  * Sentence 2: *You met her at the station.*
  * Synthesis: **The lady whom you met at the station is a renowned teacher.**
  * Sentence 1: *This is the boy.*
  * Sentence 2: *The teacher praised him yesterday.*
  * Synthesis: **This is the boy whom the teacher praised yesterday.**

#### 📙 Rule A.3: 'WHOSE' द्वारा जोड़ना
- **नियम:** 'Whose' संबंध (Possession) दर्शाता है। दूसरे वाक्य में आए संबंधवाचक सर्वनाम (*his, her, their, its*) को हटाकर उसके स्थान पर 'whose' लगाया जाता है।
  * Sentence 1: *I met a boy.*
  * Sentence 2: *His father is a military officer.*
  * Synthesis: **I met a boy whose father is a military officer.**
  * Sentence 1: *The woman was crying.*
  * Sentence 2: *Her purse was snatched.*
  * Synthesis: **The woman whose purse was snatched was crying.**

#### 📕 Rule A.4: 'WHICH' द्वारा जोड़ना
- **नियम:** वस्तुओं या पशु-पक्षियों के लिए 'which' का प्रयोग होता है। दूसरे वाक्य से *it* या *they/them* को हटा दिया जाता है।
  * Sentence 1: *The horse won the race.*
  * Sentence 2: *It was black in colour.*
  * Synthesis: **The horse which was black in colour won the race.**
  * Sentence 1: *This is the computer.*
  * Sentence 2: *My father purchased it yesterday.*
  * Synthesis: **This is the computer which my father purchased yesterday.**

#### 📓 Rule A.5: 'THAT' के अनिवार्य प्रयोग की विशिष्ट स्थितियां (Super-Important!)
निम्नलिखित विशेष स्थितियों में 'which' या 'who' के स्थान पर केवल **'THAT'** का प्रयोग ही सही माना जाता है:
1. **Superlative Degree के बाद:**
   * This is the **best** movie **that** I have ever watched.
   * Mohan is the **wisest** man **that** ever lived.
2. **विशेष अनिश्चयवाचक शब्दों के बाद (All, Same, Only, None, Any, Little, Few, Nothing):**
   * All **that** glitters is not gold.
   * Man is the only animal **that** can speak.
   * This is the same pen **that** I lost yesterday.
   * There is nothing **that** can worry him now.
3. **जब एक व्यक्ति और एक जानवर/वस्तु दोनों Antecedent हों:**
   * The farmer and his bull **that** fell into the well were rescued safely.

#### 📒 Rule A.6: 'WHERE' एवं 'WHEN' द्वारा जोड़ना
- **WHERE:** दूसरे वाक्य से स्थान-सूचक शब्द (*there, here, in that place*) हटा दिए जाते हैं:
  * Sentence 1: *This is the village.*
  * Sentence 2: *I was born there.*
  * Synthesis: **This is the village where I was born.**
- **WHEN:** दूसरे वाक्य से समय-सूचक शब्द (*then, at that time*) हटा दिए जाते हैं:
  * Sentence 1: *It was midnight.*
  * Sentence 2: *The thief entered the house then.*
  * Synthesis: **It was midnight when the thief entered the house.**

---
❓ PART B: FRAMING QUESTIONS (प्रश्न निर्माण)

### 📌 4. Wh-words Meaning & Question Formulation Architecture दिए गए कथन (Answer Statement) से प्रश्न बनाते समय दो बातों का ध्यान रखना आवश्यक है: 1. **सूचना को हटाना (Omit the Answer part):** जिस शब्द या सूचना के लिए प्रश्न बनाया जा रहा है, वह प्रश्न में शामिल नहीं होनी चाहिए! 2. **प्रश्नवाचक वाक्य-संरचना (Inversion Pattern):** Helping Verb को Subject से पहले रखना और अंत में प्रश्न चिह्न (?) लगाना अनिवार्य है। $$\mathbf{\text{Wh-Word} + \text{Helping Verb} + \text{Subject} + \text{Main Verb} + \text{Remaining Words} + \mathbf{?}}$$ ### 📊 Master Wh-Words Function Matrix: | Wh-Word | क्या जानने के लिए प्रयुक्त होता है? | क्या हटाना है? (Omit from Answer) | उदाहरण (Answer $\rightarrow$ Framed Question) | |:---:|---|---|---| | **WHO** | कर्ता व्यक्ति (Subject - Person) | Subject का नाम / सर्वनाम | Ans: Shakespeare wrote Hamlet.
Q: **Who wrote Hamlet?** | | **WHOM** | कर्म व्यक्ति (Object - Person) | Object का व्यक्ति | Ans: I met the Principal yesterday.
Q: **Whom did you meet yesterday?** | | **WHOSE** | स्वामी / अधिकार (Owner / Possession) | Possessive Noun/Pronoun | Ans: This is Rohan's bicycle.
Q: **Whose bicycle is this?** | | **WHAT** | वस्तु, कार्य या व्यवसाय (Thing/Action/Job) | वस्तु या कार्य का विवरण | Ans: He is an engineer.
Q: **What is he?**
Ans: I am reading a novel.
Q: **What are you reading?** | | **WHICH** | चुनाव / विकल्प (Choice among options) | चुनी गई वस्तु / व्यक्ति | Ans: I like the red car.
Q: **Which car do you like?** | | **WHERE** | स्थान (Place) | स्थान का नाम (in Jaipur, at school) | Ans: She lives in Jodhpur.
Q: **Where does she live?** | | **WHEN** | समय (Time) | समय-सूचक शब्द (at 7 a.m., yesterday) | Ans: The train arrives at 6:00 p.m.
Q: **When does the train arrive?** | | **WHY** | कारण / उद्देश्य (Reason / Purpose) | because, so, to + $V_1$, for + reason | Ans: He wept because he had lost his purse.
Q: **Why did he weep?** | | **HOW** | तरीका, दशा या साधन (Manner/State/Means) | by bus, happily, fine | Ans: I go to school by bicycle.
Q: **How do you go to school?** | | **HOW MANY** | गणनीय संख्या (Countable Quantity) | संख्या (two, five, many) | Ans: There are forty students in my class.
Q: **How many students are there in your class?** | | **HOW MUCH** | अगणनीय मात्रा (Uncountable Quantity) | मात्रा (two litres, much money) | Ans: He needs five thousand rupees.
Q: **How much money does he need?** | | **HOW FAR** | दूरी (Distance) | दूरी (ten kilometres, two miles) | Ans: Delhi is 250 km from here.
Q: **How far is Delhi from here?** | | **HOW LONG** | समयावधि (Duration of Time) | for two hours, since Monday | Ans: She stayed in London for three years.
Q: **How long did she stay in London?** | | **HOW OFTEN** | आवृत्ति (Frequency) | twice a week, daily, seldom | Ans: He visits his village twice a month.
Q: **How often does he visit his village?** | --- ### ⚠️ The Do/Does/Did Trap in Question Framing: जब कथन में कोई स्पष्ट सहायक क्रिया (*is, am, are, was, were, has, have, will, can*) न हो, तो Present Simple और Past Simple में सहायक क्रिया **do, does, did** लाई जाती है: - कथन में $V_1$ (बहुवचन कर्ता) हो $\rightarrow$ **Do + Subject + $V_1$** * Ans: They live in Bikaner. $\rightarrow$ Q: **Where do they live?** - कथन में $V_1 + s/es$ (एकवचन कर्ता) हो $\rightarrow$ **Does + Subject + $V_1$** * Ans: Sneha teaches English. $\rightarrow$ Q: **What does Sneha teach?** - कथन में $V_2$ (भूतकाल) हो $\rightarrow$ **Did + Subject + $V_1$** * Ans: Columbus discovered America. $\rightarrow$ Q: **What did Columbus discover?** (नोट: discovered नहीं, discover आएगा!) --- ### 🟢 Yes/No Type Question Framing (Helping Verb Inversion) यदि दिया गया कथन **"Yes"** अथवा **"No"** से प्रारम्भ होता है, तो प्रश्न Wh-word से नहीं, बल्कि **Helping Verb** से बनाया जाता है: $$\mathbf{\text{Helping Verb} + \text{Subject} + \text{Main Verb} + \text{Rest of Sentence} + \mathbf{?}}$$ - **Rule:** 'Yes' या 'No' को हटा दें और Helping Verb को आगे ले आएं: * Ans: Yes, I am ready. $\rightarrow$ Q: **Are you ready?** * Ans: Yes, he has completed his work. $\rightarrow$ Q: **Has he completed his work?** * Ans: No, I did not break the glass. $\rightarrow$ Q: **Did you break the glass?** * Ans: Yes, she likes classical music. $\rightarrow$ Q: **Does she like classical music?** ---
🏷️ PART C: QUESTION TAGS (लघु पुछल्ले प्रश्न)

### 📌 5. The Core Philosophy of Question Tags

Question Tag किसी साधारण कथन के अंत में जोड़ा जाने वाला एक छोटा प्रश्न होता है, जिसका उद्देश्य श्रोता से **सहमति (agreement) या पुष्टि (confirmation)** प्राप्त करना होता है।
- *Example:* You are a student, **aren't you?** (तुम एक विद्यार्थी हो, है ना?)

---

### ⚡ 6. The 4 Fundamental Laws of Question Tags

```
Law 1: सकारात्मक कथन (Positive Sentence) ───────► नकारात्मक टैग (Negative Tag with Contracted Form)
Law 2: नकारात्मक कथन (Negative Sentence) ───────► सकारात्मक टैग (Positive Tag without 'not')
Law 3: Tag में केवल और केवल उपयुक्त PRONOUN (he, she, it, they, we, you, I) ही आता है, NOUN कभी नहीं!
Law 4: Tag के अंत में प्रश्न चिह्न (?) और कथन के बाद अल्पविराम (,) लगाना अनिवार्य है।
```

$$\mathbf{\text{Positive Statement}, \quad \text{Auxiliary} + \mathbf{n't} + \text{Pronoun}?}$$
$$\mathbf{\text{Negative Statement}, \quad \text{Auxiliary} + \text{Pronoun}?}$$

### 🔤 Standard Contracted Negative Forms (संक्षिप्त रूप):
- `is not` $\rightarrow$ **isn't**
- `are not` $\rightarrow$ **aren't**
- `am not` $\rightarrow$ **aren't** *(विशेष अपवाद!)*
- `was not` $\rightarrow$ **wasn't**
- `were not` $\rightarrow$ **weren't**
- `have not` $\rightarrow$ **haven't**
- `has not` $\rightarrow$ **hasn't**
- `had not` $\rightarrow$ **hadn't**
- `will not` $\rightarrow$ **won't** *(अति महत्वपूर्ण!)*
- `shall not` $\rightarrow$ **shan't** *(अति महत्वपूर्ण!)*
- `cannot` $\rightarrow$ **can't**
- `could not` $\rightarrow$ **couldn't**
- `do not` $\rightarrow$ **don't**
- `does not` $\rightarrow$ **doesn't**
- `did not` $\rightarrow$ **didn't**
- `must not` $\rightarrow$ **mustn't**

---

### 🔥 7. The 8 Critical Board Exceptions & Traps (जहाँ 90% छात्र गलती करते हैं!)

#### 💥 Exception 1: "I am..." का टैग (The 'aren't I' Exception)
- जब कथन **"I am..."** (Positive) हो, तो उसका Tag **"aren't I?"** होता है (क्योंकि अंग्रेजी में *amn't* कोई शब्द नहीं होता):
  * Statement: I am an honest boy. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **aren't I?**
  * Statement: I am late today. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **aren't I?**
- परन्तु यदि कथन नकारात्मक हो (**"I am not..."**), तो Tag सामान्यतः **"am I?"** ही होता है:
  * Statement: I am not guilty. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **am I?**

#### 💥 Exception 2: "Let's / Let us" वाले वाक्य
- जब वाक्य **"Let's"** या **"Let us"** (प्रस्ताव/सुझाव) से प्रारम्भ हो, तो उसका Tag सदैव **"shall we?"** होता है:
  * Statement: Let's play cricket. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **shall we?**
  * Statement: Let us go for a morning walk. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **shall we?**
- परन्तु यदि वाक्य **"Let him / Let her / Let them / Let the boys"** (अनुमति) से प्रारम्भ हो, तो Tag **"will you?"** होता है:
  * Statement: Let him do his work. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **will you?**

#### 💥 Exception 3: Imperative Sentences (आज्ञा/प्रार्थना वाले वाक्य)
- सामान्य आज्ञावाचक वाक्यों (Orders, Requests) का Tag **"will you?"** अथवा **"won't you?"** होता है:
  * Statement: Open the window. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **will you? / won't you?**
  * Statement: Please lend me your pen. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **will you?**
- नकारात्मक आज्ञावाचक वाक्यों (Don't...) का Tag सदैव **"will you?"** (Positive) होता है:
  * Statement: Don't make a noise. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **will you?**
  * Statement: Don't tell a lie. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **will you?**
- डांटने या अधीरता व्यक्त करने वाले वाक्यों में **"can't you?"** का प्रयोग होता है:
  * Statement: Shut your mouth. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **can't you?**

#### 💥 Exception 4: अर्ध-नकारात्मक शब्द (Semi-Negative Words in Statement)
यदि वाक्य में निम्नलिखित नकारात्मक शब्द मौजूद हों, तो वाक्य का अर्थ नकारात्मक माना जाता है और उसका Tag **सकारात्मक (Positive)** बनता है:
$$\mathbf{\text{seldom, rarely, barely, hardly, scarcely, neither, nor, none, nobody, no one, nothing, few, little}}$$
- *Example 1:* Barking dogs **seldom** bite. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **do they?** (bite = $V_1$, dogs = they, seldom = negative $\rightarrow$ do they?)
- *Example 2:* He has **hardly** any money. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **has he?**
- *Example 3:* She **rarely** visits her relatives. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **does she?**
- *Example 4:* There is **little** milk in the jug. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **is there?** ('little' = नगण्य/नकारात्मक)
- *⚠️ Note (A few / A little):* 'A few' और 'A little' सकारात्मक होते हैं, अतः इनका Tag **नकारात्मक** बनेगा:
  * There is **a little** milk in the jug. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **isn't there?**

#### 💥 Exception 5: Everyone, Everybody, Someone, Nobody (The 'THEY' Pronoun Rule)
जब कथन का कर्ता *Everyone, Everybody, Someone, Somebody, Anyone, Anybody, No one, Nobody* हो, तो Tag में Pronoun के रूप में **"THEY"** का प्रयोग होता है।  
चूंकि 'They' बहुवचन है, इसलिए Tag की Verb भी **बहुवचन (Plural)** होगी:
- Statement: **Everyone** was present. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **weren't they?** (❌ *wasn't they* गलत है!)
- Statement: **Somebody** has stolen my pen. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **haven't they?** (❌ *hasn't they* गलत है!)
- Statement: **Nobody** came to the party. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **did they?** ('Nobody' नकारात्मक है $\rightarrow$ Tag सकारात्मक)
- Statement: **No one** knows the secret. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **do they?**

#### 💥 Exception 6: Everything, Something, Nothing (The 'IT' Pronoun Rule)
जब कर्ता वस्तु-सूचक अनिश्चयवाचक सर्वनाम (*Everything, Something, Nothing, Anything*) हो, तो Tag में Pronoun **"IT"** का प्रयोग होता है:
- Statement: **Everything** is fine. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **isn't it?**
- Statement: **Nothing** happened yesterday. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **did it?** ('Nothing' नकारात्मक है $\rightarrow$ Tag सकारात्मक)

#### 💥 Exception 7: 'There' वाले वाक्य
यदि वाक्य 'There' से प्रारम्भ होता है, तो Tag का Subject भी **"there"** ही रहता है:
- Statement: There are forty students in the class. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **aren't there?**
- Statement: There was no water in the well. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **was there?**

#### 💥 Exception 8: This / That एवं These / Those
- 'This' और 'That' का Tag Pronoun **"it"** होता है:
  * Statement: This is your bicycle. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **isn't it?**
- 'These' और 'Those' का Tag Pronoun **"they"** होता है:
  * Statement: Those are nice flowers. $\rightarrow$ Tag: **aren't they?**

---
🚫 8. Mistake Busters: शीर्ष 7 छात्र गलतियां एवं उनका समाधान

1. **Mistake 1:** Tag में Noun लिख देना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* Ram is playing, isn't Ram?
   * ✔️ *Correct:* Ram is playing, **isn't he?**
2. **Mistake 2:** Full form में 'not' लिखना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* She is singing, is not she?
   * ✔️ *Correct:* She is singing, **isn't she?** (सदैव Contracted n't ही मान्य है)।
3. **Mistake 3:** 'I am' का टैग 'amn't I' लिख देना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* I am right, amn't I?
   * ✔️ *Correct:* I am right, **aren't I?**
4. **Mistake 4:** Question Framing में उत्तर का भाग शामिल कर देना:
   * कथन: He went to Jaipur yesterday. (Frame with 'Where')
   * ❌ *Wrong:* Where did he go to Jaipur yesterday?
   * ✔️ *Correct:* Where did he go yesterday? ('to Jaipur' उत्तर था, उसे हटाना अनिवार्य है!)
5. **Mistake 5:** 'Did' के बाद $V_2$ लिख देना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* When did the train arrived?
   * ✔️ *Correct:* When did the train **arrive**?
6. **Mistake 6:** 'Whom' और 'Who' में भ्रम:
   * Subject जानने हेतु $\rightarrow$ **Who**; Object (सजीव) जानने हेतु $\rightarrow$ **Whom**.
7. **Mistake 7:** 'Hardly/Seldom' वाले वाक्यों में Negative Tag लगा देना:
   * ❌ *Wrong:* He hardly works, doesn't he?
   * ✔️ *Correct:* He hardly works, **does he?**

chapters.title: RBSE Class 10 English Grammar: Unit 6 — Determiners

content.value:
**विषय:** English (Compulsory), Code 02  
**Current syllabus:** 2026–27  
**Syllabus weight:** Determiners are listed for 2 marks within the 8-mark Grammar component. The exact question format is not prescribed. This unit is original practice, not an official question bank.
1. What determiners do

Determiners come before a noun and help identify or quantify it: *a book, the book, my book, these books, some water, three books*. Common groups are articles, demonstratives, possessives, quantifiers, numbers, and question words. A noun phrase normally does not take two competing central determiners: say *my book* or *the book*, not *the my book*.
2. Quick rules

| Group | Use | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **a / an** | One nonspecific singular countable noun. Choose by the following **sound**, not spelling. | *a uniform*, *an hour* |
| **the** | A specific or already identified noun; also many unique references. | *the book you lent me*, *the sun* |
| **this / that** | Singular; near / farther in the usual physical or discourse context. | *this chair*, *that building* |
| **these / those** | Plural; near / farther in the usual context. | *these notes*, *those hills* |
| **my, your, his, her, its, our, their** | Possession or association; use one instead of an article before the noun. | *her bag*, *our school* |
| **some / any** | *Some* is common in affirmative statements and offers; *any* is common in questions and negatives. Context can change the choice. | *some milk*, *Would you like some tea?*, *Is there any milk?* |
| **many / much** | *Many* with plural count nouns; *much* with uncountable nouns. | *many students*, *much time* |
| **few / a few; little / a little** | *Few/little* stress scarcity; *a few/a little* mean a small but positive amount. | *few chairs*, *a few chairs*; *little hope*, *a little hope* |
| **each / every** | Refers to members individually; normally takes a singular noun and singular verb. | *Each child has a card.* |
| **either / neither** | Refers to one or none of two; normally takes a singular noun. | *Either route is safe.* |
| **both / all** | *Both* for two; *all* for a group or an uncountable whole. | *both teams*, *all the water* |
| **which / what / whose** | Ask about selection, information, or possession before a noun. | *Which bus? What colour? Whose coat?* |

### Countable and uncountable nouns

Use *many/few* with plural countable nouns (*many apples, a few questions*) and *much/little* with uncountable nouns (*much rice, a little advice*). In ordinary affirmative statements, *a lot of* often sounds more natural than *much* or *many*: *We have a lot of homework.*

### Articles: sound and reference

- *A* precedes a consonant sound: *a European country*, *a useful idea*.
- *An* precedes a vowel sound: *an orange*, *an honest answer*.
- Use *the* when the listener can identify which one: *Please close the door.*
- Do not force an article before every plural or uncountable noun: *Books can be useful; Water is essential.*
3. Common errors

| Incorrect | Correct | Why |
|---|---|---|
| *an university* | *a university* | *University* begins with the consonant sound /j/. |
| *many homework* | *much homework* / *a lot of homework* | *Homework* is uncountable in this use. |
| *much students* | *many students* | *Students* is plural and countable. |
| *the my pencil* | *my pencil* | Do not place an article before a possessive determiner. |
| *each students* | *each student* | *Each* is followed by a singular count noun. |
| *few water* | *little water* | *Water* is uncountable. |
4. Practice: choose the best determiner

Choose one answer for each blank. Read the full sentence; some determiners depend on meaning and context.

1. We saw ___ elephant near the river. (a / an / the)
2. ___ sun rises in the east. (A / An / The)
3. ___ students in this group have submitted their projects. (Much / Many / Every)
4. There is ___ water left; you can use it for tea. (a few / a little / many)
5. Have you received ___ messages from the teacher? (any / much / little)
6. There are ___ clean cups on the shelf, enough for our two visitors. (a few / little / much)
7. We have ___ time before the bus arrives, so let us finish this page. (a little / many / few)
8. ___ of the two routes will take us to the station. (Either / Every / Much)
9. ___ student must write a name on the answer sheet. (Every / Many / Several)
10. Nisha bought ___ notebooks for the new term. (two / much / a little)
11. I have visited Jaipur ___ times. (several / much / every)
12. ___ book here is mine; the one near you is yours. (This / These / Those)
13. ___ eggs do we need for the recipe? (How much / How many / How few)
14. There isn't ___ sugar in the jar. (many / much / a few)
15. Arif has ___ friends in his new class and enjoys spending time with them. (a few / little / much)
16. Please return ___ information sheet I gave you this morning. (a / the / an)
17. She ate ___ orange and then chose ___ banana. (a, an / an, a / the, an)
18. ___ Ganga is an important river in India. (A / The / An)
19. ___ of my parents work at schools. (Both / Every / Much)
20. He gave us ___ honest answer. (a / an / the)
21. ___ people attended the village meeting, so the hall was nearly full. (Many / Much / A little)
22. I need ___ help with this question, please. (some / many / a few)
23. Would you like ___ more tea? (some / many / few)
24. ___ answer in the list explains the word most clearly? (Which / Much / Every)
25. ___ umbrella is this? (Whose / How many / These)
5. Answer key with brief reasons

1. **an** — *elephant* begins with a vowel sound.  
2. **The** — the sun is treated as unique in this reference.  
3. **Many** — *students* is plural and countable.  
4. **a little** — *water* is uncountable; the sentence means a small usable amount remains.  
5. **any** — common in a neutral question.  
6. **a few** — *cups* is plural countable and the sentence says a small positive number is available.  
7. **a little** — a small amount of time remains.  
8. **Either** — one of two routes; singular verb *will take*.  
9. **Every** — singular *student*.  
10. **two** — a number before a plural count noun.  
11. **several** — a number greater than two but not specified.  
12. **This** — singular *book* and the near-location cue *here*.  
13. **How many** — *eggs* is plural countable.  
14. **much** — *sugar* is uncountable.  
15. **a few** — a small positive number of friends.  
16. **the** — the sheet is identified by the relative clause and earlier mention.  
17. **an, a** — vowel sound in *orange*; consonant sound in *banana*.  
18. **The** — conventional use with this river name.  
19. **Both** — refers to two parents.  
20. **an** — *honest* begins with a vowel sound because *h* is silent.  
21. **Many** — *people* is plural countable.  
22. **some** — a polite request for an unspecified amount of help.  
23. **some** — a conventional offer; *any* could occur in other question contexts.  
24. **Which** — asks the reader to select from a known list.  
25. **Whose** — asks about possession.
6. Sources and scope

- [RBSE Class X English syllabus 2026–27](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf), PDF pp. 3–4: Determiners are listed for 2 marks within Grammar.
- [Cambridge English Grammar Today: Determiners](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/grammar/british-grammar/determiners-the-my-some-this) and [Determiners: position and order](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/grammar/british-grammar/determiners-position-and-order): categories, reference, quantity, and order.
- [Cambridge: much and many](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/us/grammar/british-grammar/much-many-a-lot-of-lots-of-quantifiers) and [British Council: a, an, the](https://learnenglish.britishcouncil.org/grammar/a1-a2-grammar/articles-a-an-the): countability and article sound rules.

The exercises are original practice. They are not attributed to an RBSE paper, and the table of rules gives common patterns rather than every exception or dialectal variation.

### Section A: Reading Skills (Weightage: 20 Marks | Two Unseen Passages)

**विषय:** अंग्रेजी (English Compulsory) | **विषय कोड:** 02  
**कक्षा:** 10वीं (माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर — RBSE)  
**इकाई ID:** `wr_ch01` | **खंड:** Section A (Reading Comprehension)  
**निर्धारित अंक भार:** 20 अंक (दो unseen passages का कुल)  
**पाठ्यक्रम में निर्दिष्ट प्रकार/लंबाई:** discursive passage 400–450 words; case-based factual passage 200–250 words; कुल 600–700 words। Syllabus comprehension, interpretation, analysis, inference, evaluation और vocabulary जाँचता है; अलग-अलग passage के अंक या question counts तय नहीं करता।

---
🌟 स्मार्ट गाइड प्रवेश: 10 सेकंड में सेक्शन A का सार (Topper's Mindset)

> 💡 **शिक्षक की विशेष सलाह (Examiner's Secret Insight):**  
> Unseen passages के लिए 20 अंक निर्धारित हैं। प्रश्न स्थानीय/वैश्विक बोध के साथ विश्लेषण, अनुमान और शब्दावली भी जाँच सकते हैं; उत्तर केवल सीधे passage से उठाना हर प्रश्न के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं।  
> बोर्ड परीक्षक केवल तीन चीजें देखता है:
> 1. क्या छात्र ने प्रश्न का टेंस और सर्वनाम (Tense & Pronouns) सही बदला है?
> 2. क्या छात्र ने पैसेज की पूरी 4-5 पंक्तियाँ बिना सोचे-समझे नकल (blind copy-paste) तो नहीं कर दीं?
> 3. क्या वोकैबुलरी (Synonym/Antonym/One word) का उत्तर उसी Part of Speech (संज्ञा का संज्ञा, क्रिया का क्रिया) में दिया गया है?
> 
> नीचे दी गई scan technique और passage exercises अभ्यास हैं; वे पूर्ण अंक या बोर्ड के सभी प्रश्न-प्रकारों की गारंटी नहीं देते।

---
1. Current passage types and lengths (no per-passage marks specified)

| पैसेज | निर्धारित प्रकार | शब्द-सीमा | प्रश्नों का सामान्य उद्देश्य |
|:---|:---|:---:|:---|
| **1** | Discursive | 400–450 words | Comprehension, inference, analysis, vocabulary |
| **2** | Case-based factual with visual input (e.g., data/chart) | 200–250 words | Comprehension, interpretation, analysis, vocabulary |
| **कुल** | Reading Skills | 600–700 words | 20 marks overall; per-passage split/question count not specified |

---
2. 5-मिनट रिवर्स स्कैन तकनीक एवं 6 गोल्डन नियम (Smart Exam Strategies)

### 🎯 तकनीक 1: रिवर्स स्कैन विधि (The Reverse Scanning Method)
विद्यार्थी अक्सर पहले पूरा पैसेज पढ़ने में 15-20 मिनट नष्ट कर देते हैं और फिर प्रश्नों पर आते हैं। टॉपर छात्र ऐसा कभी नहीं करते!
1. **चरण 1 (Step 1 - First 60 Seconds):** पैसेज पढ़ने से पहले सीधे **प्रश्नों (Questions) को पढ़ें**। 
2. **चरण 2 (Step 2 - Underline Key Anchors):** प्रत्येक प्रश्न में मुख्य 'एंकर वर्ड्स' (Name, Year, Place, Specific Verb, Technical term) को रेखांकित करें।
3. **चरण 3 (Step 3 - Targeted Skimming):** अब पैसेज को तेजी से ऊपर से नीचे की ओर स्कैन करें। जैसे ही प्रश्न का की-वर्ड या उसका समानार्थी शब्द दिखे, रुकें।
4. **चरण 4 (Step 4 - The 2-Sentence Window):** उस की-वर्ड वाली पंक्ति तथा उसके ठीक आगे और पीछे वाली पंक्ति को ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ें। 95% मामलों में उत्तर इसी 2-वाक्य की खिड़की में होता है।
5. **चरण 5 (Step 5 - Own Words Adjustment):** उत्तर को अपनी भाषा में सटीक और संक्षिप्त रूप में लिखें।

---

### 🎯 तकनीक 2: वोकैबुलरी (Synonym / Antonym) खोजने का 4-स्टेप फॉर्मूला
बोर्ड में अक्सर पूछा जाता है:  
* *"Find the word from the passage which means: 'very tired' (Para 2)"*  
* *"Find the opposite of 'cruel' from the passage. (Para 3)"*

इसे हल करने के अचूक नियम:
* **नियम A: Part of Speech मैचिंग (The Grammar Twin Rule):**  
  - यदि दिया गया शब्द **Adjective (विशेषण)** है, तो पैसेज से उत्तर भी अनिवार्य रूप से Adjective ही होगा! (जैसे: *famous -> renowned*; *sad -> gloomy*)
  - यदि शब्द **Verb (क्रिया)** है, तो उत्तर भी Verb होगा और उसका Form (V1/V2/V3/V-ing) भी समान होगा! (जैसे: *started -> commenced*; *looking for -> searching*)
  - यदि शब्द **Noun (संज्ञा)** है, तो उत्तर Noun ही होगा! (जैसे: *bravery -> valour*; *poverty -> destitution*)
* **नियम B: पैराग्राफ सीमा का पालन:** यदि प्रश्न किसी पैराग्राफ का संकेत देता है, तो पहले वहीं उत्तर खोजें; प्रश्न के अनुसार आसपास का संदर्भ भी जाँचें।
* **नियम C: रिप्लेसमेंट टेस्ट (Substitution Test):** जो शब्द आपको उत्तर लगता है, उसे प्रश्न वाले वाक्य में रखकर देखें। क्या अर्थ जस का तस रहता है? यदि हाँ, तो वही सही उत्तर है।

---

### 🎯 तकनीक 3: Wh- शब्दों का सटीक प्रत्युत्तर चार्ट (Wh- Question Decoding Chart)

| प्रश्न शब्द (Wh- Word) | परीक्षक क्या जानना चाहता है? (Expectation) | उत्तर की शुरुआत कैसे करें? (Opening Anchor) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **What** | वस्तु, कार्य, घटना या विचार (Thing, Action, Concept) | "The reason was..." / "[Subject] did [Action]..." |
| **Why** | कारण, उद्देश्य (Reason, Motive, Cause) | "Because..." / "In order to + V1..." / "So that..." |
| **Where** | स्थान, दिशा (Place, Location, Direction) | "At [Place]" / "In [Location]..." |
| **When** | समय, दिन, वर्ष, अवसर (Time, Date, Era, Occasion) | "In the year [Year]" / "When [Event happened]..." |
| **Who** | व्यक्ति, पात्र, कर्ता (Person, Character, Agent) | "[Name of the person/entity]..." |
| **How** | तरीका, प्रक्रिया, मात्रा (Manner, Process, Extent) | "By + V-ing..." / "With the help of..." |
| **How many / How much** | संख्या / मात्रा (Number / Quantity) | सटीक संख्या या परिमाण सीधे लिखें। |

---
3. सामान्य उत्तर-लेखन समस्याएँ (Practice guidance; not an official marking scheme)

| ❌ विद्यार्थी की सामान्य गलती (Common Blunder) | ⚠️ बोर्ड परीक्षक का रिएक्शन | ✅ अभ्यास के लिए उपयोगी तरीका (Practice Guidance) |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **गलती 1: जरूरत से ज्यादा passage कॉपी करना।** | इससे उत्तर अप्रासंगिक या अस्पष्ट हो सकता है; कोई निश्चित अंक-कटौती यहाँ प्रमाणित नहीं है। | प्रश्न के लिए जरूरी जानकारी चुनें और निर्देशानुसार अपने शब्दों में संक्षेप में उत्तर दें। |
| **गलती 2: काल (Tense) की गड़बड़ी:** प्रश्न *"Why did the boy cry?"* है, लेकिन उत्तर में *"The boy cries because..."* लिखा है। | इससे उत्तर की भाषा/अर्थ प्रभावित हो सकते हैं; कोई निश्चित अंक-कटौती यहाँ प्रमाणित नहीं है। | संदर्भ और प्रश्न के काल के अनुरूप क्रिया चुनें: *"The boy cried because..."* |
| **गलती 3: सर्वनाम (Pronouns) का अस्पष्ट संदर्भ।** | पाठक यह न समझ पाए कि सर्वनाम किसके लिए है। | जरूरत हो तो नाम, *the author*, या *the narrator* लिखकर संदर्भ स्पष्ट करें। |
| **गलती 4: Vocabulary उत्तर में संख्या का मेल न होना:** *"friends"* के लिए singular *"companion"* चुनना। | उत्तर का व्याकरणिक रूप प्रश्न से मेल नहीं खा सकता। | passage में ऐसा शब्द चुनें जो अर्थ और वाक्य-रचना दोनों में फिट बैठे। |

---
4. 8 संपूर्ण विस्तृत हल किए गए बोर्ड मॉडल पैसेज (8 Exhaustive Solved Board Passages)

---

### 📝 मॉडल पैसेज 1: तथ्यात्मक गद्यांश — जल संरक्षण एवं राजस्थान के पारंपरिक जल स्रोत (Factual Passage: Water Conservation)
*(Word Count: ~165 words | Marks: 7 | Factual Nature)*

**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:**

Water is the foundation of life, and in an arid state like Rajasthan, every single drop is considered more precious than pearls. For centuries, the people of the Thar Desert developed ingenious traditional methods of rainwater harvesting to survive severe droughts. Among these, the 'Bawari' (stepwell), 'Tanka' (underground circular tank), and 'Johad' (earthen check dam) played a monumental role in water security.

A 'Tanka' is traditionally constructed in the central courtyard or near houses in western Rajasthan. It is a covered underground pit where clean rainwater collected from specially prepared artificial catchment areas called 'Agor' is channeled through wire-meshed pipes. This stored water remains cool throughout scorching summers and suffices a family's drinking needs for an entire year. Sadly, modern piped water supply led many rural households to neglect these ancient structures. However, frequent climate changes and groundwater depletion are forcing communities to revive these time-tested sustainable systems.

#### Board Questions (अंक: 7):
1. Why is water considered more precious than pearls in Rajasthan? (1 Mark)
2. What are the three traditional rainwater harvesting structures mentioned in the passage? (1 Mark)
3. Describe the construction and functioning of a 'Tanka'. (1 Mark)
4. What is an 'Agor'? (1 Mark)
5. Why did rural households neglect the traditional water structures in recent decades? (1 Mark)
6. What is forcing rural communities to revive ancient rainwater systems today? (1 Mark)
7. Find the word from the passage which means: **'very dry / lacking water'** (Para 1). (1 Mark)

#### Practice model solutions and suggested answers:
* **Q1. Solution:** Water is considered more precious than pearls in Rajasthan because Rajasthan is an arid (dry) state prone to severe droughts where water is essential for basic survival.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Exact reason stated without superfluous words)*
* **Q2. Solution:** The three traditional water harvesting structures mentioned are: (i) Bawari (stepwell), (ii) Tanka (underground tank), and (iii) Johad (earthen check dam).  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Complete listing)*
* **Q3. Solution:** A Tanka is a covered underground pit constructed in courtyards. It stores clean rainwater channeled from catchments through mesh pipes, keeping it cool and drinkable for an entire year.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Captures both construction and functioning)*
* **Q4. Solution:** An 'Agor' is a specially prepared artificial catchment area from which rainwater is collected and directed into a Tanka.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Precise definition from text)*
* **Q5. Solution:** Rural households neglected these ancient structures due to the arrival and availability of modern piped water supply.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Cause-effect clearly framed)*
* **Q6. Solution:** Frequent climate changes and rapid groundwater depletion are compelling communities to revive ancient rainwater harvesting systems.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Two key drivers identified)*
* **Q7. Solution:** **Arid** (From Para 1: "arid state").  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Exact Adjective matching)*

---

### 📝 मॉडल पैसेज 2: तथ्यात्मक गद्यांश — डॉ. ए.पी.जे. अब्दुल कलाम का प्रेरक जीवन (Biographical Passage: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam)
*(Word Count: ~170 words | Marks: 7 | Factual & Inspiring)*

**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:**

Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam, popularly revered as the 'Missile Man of India', was born into a humble Tamil Muslim family in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu, on 15 October 1931. His father, Jainulabdeen, was an honest boat owner and imam, while his mother, Ashiamma, was a generous homemaker. To support his family during difficult financial phases in his early childhood, young Kalam distributed newspapers door-to-door before attending morning school.

Despite financial hardships, his insatiable curiosity and passion for learning guided him toward aerospace engineering at the Madras Institute of Technology. He joined the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and later the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), where he directed India's first satellite launch vehicle (SLV-III) project. Kalam believed firmly that perseverance, humility, and steadfast dreams possess the power to conquer any obstacle. Serving as the 11th President of India from 2002 to 2007, he endeared himself particularly to schoolchildren, constantly igniting their minds to dream big and serve the motherland.

#### Board Questions (अंक: 7):
1. Where and when was Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam born? (1 Mark)
2. What did young Kalam do to support his family financially? (1 Mark)
3. Name the two premier scientific institutions where Dr. Kalam served. (1 Mark)
4. What role did Dr. Kalam play in India's satellite program? (1 Mark)
5. According to Dr. Kalam, what qualities can overcome any obstacle? (1 Mark)
6. During which years did Dr. Kalam serve as the President of India? (1 Mark)
7. Find the word in the passage which is the opposite of: **'wealth / affluence'** (Para 2). (1 Mark)

#### Practice model solutions and suggested answers:
* **Q1. Solution:** Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was born on 15 October 1931 in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Date and place exact)*
* **Q2. Solution:** To assist his family financially, young Kalam distributed newspapers door-to-door before attending his morning school.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Action clearly expressed in past tense)*
* **Q3. Solution:** The two premier scientific institutions are: (i) DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation) and (ii) ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation).  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Both institutions named correctly)*
* **Q4. Solution:** He directed India's first indigenous satellite launch vehicle project, the SLV-III, at ISRO.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Specific designation and project)*
* **Q5. Solution:** According to Dr. Kalam, perseverance, genuine humility, and steadfast dedication to dreams can overcome any obstacle.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Key virtues listed)*
* **Q6. Solution:** Dr. Kalam served as the 11th President of India from 2002 to 2007.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Exact tenure)*
* **Q7. Solution:** **Hardships** (Para 2: "financial hardships"; opposite of affluence/wealth).  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Grammatically correct opposite)*

---

### 📝 मॉडल पैसेज 3: विमर्शकारी गद्यांश — इंटरनेट, सोशल मीडिया और किशोर मानसिक स्वास्थ्य (Discursive Passage: Digital Age & Youth)
*(Word Count: ~225 words | Marks: 8 | Analytical / Discursive)*

**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:**

The rapid proliferation of smartphones and high-speed internet has revolutionized how humanity communicates, learns, and entertains itself. For the youth, the digital realm provides instant access to global libraries, creative collaborations, and educational webinars. A student sitting in a remote village in Rajasthan can now effortlessly learn advanced coding or English phonetics from world-class instructors with a single click.

However, beneath this dazzling convenience lies a perilous trap. Unregulated screen exposure has led to a catastrophic decline in outdoor physical activity, face-to-face social bonds, and authentic attention spans. Recent psychometric studies reveal that excessive indulgence in social media cultivates a compulsive syndrome commonly termed 'FOMO' (Fear of Missing Out). Adolescents constantly compare their mundane everyday routines with the carefully curated, highly embellished digital highlights of influencers, triggering chronic anxiety, insomnia, and low self-esteem.

Moreover, the blue light emitted by electronic screens disrupts melatonin synthesis, wrecking natural circadian sleep cycles. Therefore, while modern technology remains an indispensable tool for intellectual advancement, teenagers must cultivate deliberate digital hygiene. Digital detox intervals, strict screen curfews during study hours, and regular participation in sports are essential antidotes to modern screen dependency.

#### Board Questions (अंक: 8):
1. In what ways has internet technology benefited students in remote areas? (1 Mark)
2. What negative lifestyle consequences have arisen from excessive screen exposure? (1 Mark)
3. What is 'FOMO' and how does social media trigger it among adolescents? (1 Mark)
4. How does screen usage at night harm the sleep cycle of teenagers? (1 Mark)
5. What three solutions are recommended in the passage to counteract screen dependency? (1 Mark)
6. Choose the correct alternative: Excessive exposure to screens primarily affects: (1 Mark)  
   (A) Only eye vision  
   (B) Melatonin synthesis and sleep cycles  
   (C) Physical height  
   (D) Hearing power  
7. Find the word in the passage which means: **'dangerous / hazardous'** (Para 2). (1 Mark)
8. Find the word in the passage which means: **'necessary / cannot be managed without'** (Para 3). (1 Mark)

#### Practice model solutions and suggested answers:
* **Q1. Solution:** The internet allows rural students to access global libraries, attend online webinars, and learn advanced subjects like coding and English phonetics from top educators worldwide.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Educational empowerment highlighted)*
* **Q2. Solution:** Excessive screen time has led to a drastic decline in physical outdoor games, diminished face-to-face interactions, and shortened attention spans.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Lifestyle drawbacks captured)*
* **Q3. Solution:** 'FOMO' stands for 'Fear of Missing Out'. It is triggered when teenagers compare their routine lives with the unrealistically glamorous digital highlights posted by peers and influencers.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Definition + trigger mechanism explained)*
* **Q4. Solution:** The blue light emitted from screens suppresses the synthesis of melatonin, which disrupts the natural circadian sleep rhythm and leads to insomnia.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Scientific cause explained accurately)*
* **Q5. Solution:** The three recommended antidotes are: (i) digital detox breaks, (ii) strict screen curfews while studying, and (iii) regular participation in physical sports.  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Complete tripartite remedy)*
* **Q6. Solution:** **(B) Melatonin synthesis and sleep cycles**  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Exact option selection)*
* **Q7. Solution:** **Perilous** (Para 2: "beneath this dazzling convenience lies a perilous trap").  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Exact synonym matched)*
* **Q8. Solution:** **Indispensable** (Para 3: "remains an indispensable tool").  
  *(Marking: 1/1 — Exact vocabulary identification)*

---

### 📝 मॉडल पैसेज 4: विमर्शकारी गद्यांश — पर्यावरण प्रदूषण, प्लास्टिक संकट एवं प्रकृति संरक्षण (Discursive Passage: Plastic Pollution)
*(Word Count: ~235 words | Marks: 8 | Discursive / Ecological)*

**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:**

Plastic, once celebrated as the miracle synthetic polymer of the twentieth century owing to its featherweight durability, cost-effectiveness, and water resistance, has evolved into our planet's gravest ecological menace. Because conventional petrochemical plastics are non-biodegradable, every single toothbrush, shopping bag, and disposable spoon manufactured over the last seven decades still lingers somewhere on Earth, either buried in suffocating landfills or floating across oceanic gyres.

Marine ecosystems suffer the most catastrophic devastation. Sea turtles confuse translucent polyethylene bags with edible jellyfish, swallowing them and suffering lethal intestinal blockages. Over decades, solar ultraviolet radiation fragments floating discarded plastics into microscopic particles known as microplastics. These tiny toxic fragments are consumed by plankton and fish, seamlessly infiltrating the marine food chain. Ultimately, through seafood consumption, these carcinogenic compounds enter human digestive systems, causing endocrine disruptions and cellular damage.

To mitigate this environmental apocalypse, mere recycling is insufficient since less than ten percent of global plastic actually gets recycled. Humanity must urgently embrace the philosophy of 'Refuse, Reduce, and Replace'. Nations must enforce blanket bans on single-use cutlery and packaging while subsidizing biodegradable alternatives fashioned from bamboo, jute, bagasse, and hemp. Individual vigilance in carrying cloth tote bags and stainless steel bottles remains our first line of ecological defense.

#### Board Questions (अंक: 8):
1. Why was plastic initially hailed as a wonder material in the twentieth century? (1 Mark)
2. Why does plastic waste persist on Earth for centuries without decomposing? (1 Mark)
3. How do sea turtles fall victim to floating plastic debris? (1 Mark)
4. What are microplastics and how do they infiltrate human bodies? (1 Mark)
5. Why is recycling alone inadequate to solve the global plastic crisis? (1 Mark)

### 📝 मॉडल पैसेज 5: तथ्यात्मक गद्यांश — योग एवं समग्र स्वास्थ्य लाभ (Factual Passage: Yoga and Holistic Health)
*(Word Count: ~175 words | Marks: 7 | Health / Factual)*

**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:**

Originating thousands of years ago in ancient India, Yoga is not merely a sequence of physical postures (asanas), but a profound science of uniting the body, mind, and consciousness. The word 'Yoga' derives from the Sanskrit root 'Yuj', which signifies to join or unite. In modern society, where sedentary desk occupations and psychological stress have created a global epidemic of hypertension and diabetes, regular practice of yoga serves as a comprehensive preventive medicine.

Pranayama, the conscious regulation of vital breath, oxygenates blood vessels, enhances lung vital capacity, and calms an overstimulated autonomic nervous system. Furthermore, meditative techniques like Dhyana foster psychological resilience, enabling practitioners to maintain inner tranquility amidst chaotic circumstances. Unlike vigorous weightlifting which strains ligaments, yoga enhances musculoskeletal flexibility, lubricates joint cartilage, and improves posture without incurring bodily exhaustion. Recognizing its holistic contributions to human well-being, the United Nations General Assembly proclaimed 21 June as the International Day of Yoga in 2014, making this ancient Indian legacy a global celebration of wellness.

#### Board Questions (अंक: 7):

4. How does Dhyana help human beings psychologically? (1 Mark)
5. How is yoga different and safer compared to heavy weightlifting? (1 Mark)
6. When was 21 June declared as the International Day of Yoga and by whom? (1 Mark)
7. Find the word in the passage that means: **'peace / calm state of mind'** (Para 2). (1 Mark)

#### Practice model solutions and suggested answers:

  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q2. Solution:** Yoga counters modern desk-bound sedentary habits and mental tension, preventing chronic lifestyle ailments such as hypertension and diabetes.  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*

  *(Marking: 1/1)*

  *(Marking: 1/1)*

  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q6. Solution:** 21 June was declared the International Day of Yoga in 2014 by the United Nations General Assembly.  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q7. Solution:** **Tranquility** (Para 2: "maintain inner tranquility").  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*

### 📝 मॉडल पैसेज 6: विमर्शकारी गद्यांश — पुस्तकें: हमारी सबसे सच्ची मित्र (Discursive Passage: The Value of Books)
*(Word Count: ~220 words | Marks: 8 | Cultural / Value-Based)*

**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:**

Of all the intellectual inventions devised by human civilization, the written book remains the most potent vehicle of wisdom, empathy, and timeless companionship. Friends may drift away, wealth may evaporate during catastrophic misfortunes, and youthful physical vigor inevitably fades, but noble books stand by us steadfastly through all seasons of fortune and adversity. A home devoid of books is likened by thinkers to a room without windows, trapped in sterile gloom.

Reading great literature transports us across the boundaries of time, geography, and culture. Sitting comfortably in our modest room, we can converse intimately with Socrates in Athens, traverse Elizabethan theatres with William Shakespeare, or explore the profound non-violent philosophy of Mahatma Gandhi. Books expand our intellectual horizons and demolish narrow provincial prejudices. They teach us to perceive reality from diverse human perspectives, refining our natural capacity for compassion.

However, in this frenetic era of instant algorithmic reels and 15-second entertainment clips, the serene habit of sustained, deep reading is endangered. Superficial browsing scatters the intellect, leaving minds restless. To cultivate profound cognitive abilities and emotional maturity, young learners must consciously carve out dedicated time each evening to read thought-provoking classic books.

#### Board Questions (अंक: 8):
1. Why are noble books considered superior to mortal human companions and wealth? (1 Mark)
2. What metaphor is used in the passage to describe a house without books? (1 Mark)
3. How does reading transport an individual across time and geography? (1 Mark)
4. In what way does reading literature develop emotional empathy in people? (1 Mark)
5. Why is the habit of deep reading declining among youth today? (1 Mark)
6. Choose the correct statement according to the passage: (1 Mark)  
   (A) Social media clips improve deep intellect  
   (B) Books abandon human beings during misfortune  
   (C) Books expand intellectual horizons and dismantle narrow prejudices  
   (D) Socrates was an Elizabethan dramatist

8. Find the antonym of: **'profound / deep'** from Para 3. (1 Mark)

  *(Marking: 1/1)*

  *(Marking: 1/1)*

  *(Marking: 1/1)*

  *(Marking: 1/1)*

  *(Marking: 1/1)*

### 📝 मॉडल पैसेज 7: तथ्यात्मक गद्यांश — स्वामी विवेकानंद और शिकागो धर्म संसद (Historical Passage: Swami Vivekananda)
*(Word Count: ~185 words | Marks: 7 | Historical & Cultural)*

**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:**

On 11 September 1893, a momentous chapter in world cultural history was scripted when Swami Vivekananda, a young monk in saffron robes from India, addressed the Parliament of Religions in Chicago. When he stepped onto the rostrum and uttered his resonant opening words, "Sisters and Brothers of America!", an audience of seven thousand delegates spontaneously rose and erupted into thunderous, two-minute-long applause.

Before Vivekananda's electrifying discourse, Western audiences largely viewed the Orient through biased prisms of superstition and backwardness. Vivekananda dismantled these condescending misconceptions by explaining the core philosophy of Vedanta—that all religions represent distinct pathways converging toward the same supreme divine reality, just as diverse rivers originating in mountains ultimately merge into the boundless ocean. He championed universal tolerance and mutual acceptance, declaring that true spiritual enlightenment lies not in sectarian dogmatism, but in recognizing divinity within all humanity. His speech transformed him overnight into a revered global icon of interfaith brotherhood and established India's spiritual prestige globally.

#### Board Questions (अंक: 7):

  *(Marking: 1/1)*

  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q7. Solution:** **Sectarian dogmatism** (or **Dogmatism**; Para 2).  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*

### 📝 मॉडल पैसेज 8: विमर्शकारी गद्यांश — अनुशासन: सफलता और चरित्र की रीढ़ (Discursive Passage: Discipline in Student Life)
*(Word Count: ~220 words | Marks: 8 | Moral & Analytical)*

**Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow:**

Discipline is frequently misunderstood by young minds as an oppressive set of arbitrary curbs designed by elders to restrict individual liberty. In reality, authentic discipline is not bondage; it is the ultimate bridge that connects abstract human dreams with tangible worldly accomplishments. Without self-discipline, the most sparkling intellectual genius remains barren, just like a roaring locomotive engine without steel railway tracks inevitably derails and crashes into oblivion.

Nature operates under sublime, unwavering discipline. The sun never fails to illuminate the morning skies, seasons cycle in predictable harmony, and celestial planets rotate along precise gravitational orbits. If nature were to turn capricious and abandon its orderly rhythms, the universe would instantly collapse into chaotic ruins. Similarly, in a school or civil society, discipline establishes social harmony and ensures fair opportunities for all.

In student life, self-discipline encompasses punctual time management, persistent academic focus, physical tidiness, and reverent behavior toward teachers and peers. It trains the human mind to subordinate immediate fleeting desires—such as mindless mobile gaming or procrastination—to long-term goals. Those who conquer their impulsive instincts in youth build unshakeable character and command honor throughout their careers.

#### Board Questions (अंक: 8):
1. What is the common misconception teenagers hold regarding discipline? (1 Mark)
2. How is discipline described as the bridge between dreams and achievements? (1 Mark)
3. What metaphor of the locomotive is used to illustrate lack of discipline? (1 Mark)
4. What happens if nature abandons its disciplined laws? (1 Mark)
5. What habits reflect self-discipline in a student's daily routine? (1 Mark)
6. Choose the correct antonym of the word **'oppressive / restrictive'**: (1 Mark)  
   (A) Compulsory  
   (B) Liberating  
   (C) Severe  
   (D) Stern  
7. Find the word in the passage that means: **'unpredictable / erratic'** (Para 2). (1 Mark)
8. Find the word in the passage that means: **'delaying tasks / postponing'** (Para 3). (1 Mark)

#### Practice model solutions and suggested answers:

  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q2. Solution:** Discipline transforms vague desires into real achievements by giving structure and consistency to human effort.  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q3. Solution:** A genius without discipline is compared to a powerful locomotive without railway tracks, which derails and destroys itself.  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q4. Solution:** If nature abandons its orderly laws, the universe will immediately collapse into total chaos and destruction.  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q5. Solution:** In student life, discipline is reflected through punctuality, consistent focus on studies, neatness, and respectful conduct toward others.  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q6. Solution:** **(B) Liberating**  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q7. Solution:** **Capricious** (Para 2: "If nature were to turn capricious").  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*
* **Q8. Solution:** **Procrastination** (Para 3: "gaming or procrastination").  
  *(Marking: 1/1)*

6. फटाफट परीक्षा पूर्व चीट शीट (Pre-Exam Rapid Cheat Sheet)

1. **पहला काम:** प्रश्न पहले पढ़ें -> फिर पैसेज स्कैन करें (रिवर्स स्कैनिंग)।
2. **सटीक उत्तर खिड़की:** प्रश्न के की-वर्ड वाली लाइन और उसके आगे-पीछे का वाक्य ही उत्तर होता है।
3. **टेंस अनुशासन:** यदि प्रश्न में **"did"** है, तो उत्तर की क्रिया को **Past Tense (V2)** में अवश्य बदलें।
4. **सर्वनाम परिवर्तन:** पैसेज के "I / We" को उत्तर में "He / She / The author / They" में बदलें।
5. **शब्दावली का नियम:** Adjective का पर्यायवाची Adjective, Noun का Noun, Verb का Verb ही होगा।
6. **कोई लाइन अंधाधुंध न छापें:** केवल आवश्यक तथ्य उठाएं और उत्तर को 1-2 पंक्तियों में सीमित रखें।
7. **नेगेटिव मार्किंग नहीं है:** वोकैबुलरी का कोई भी प्रश्न खाली न छोड़ें; अनुमान लगाकर सर्वोत्तम शब्द अवश्य लिखें।
8. **अंक भार का ध्यान:** 1 अंक के प्रश्न में 1 या 2 सटीक वाक्य पर्याप्त हैं; निबंध न लिखें।

---
7. 15-मिनट आत्म-मूल्यांकन बोर्ड टेस्ट (Board Standard Self-Test)

**अभ्यास समय: 15 मिनट | Self-check: 10 practice points (not a reproduced RBSE paper)**

### Passage 1 (7 Marks):
Early rising is a blessing for human health and intellect. A morning walker enjoys the purest oxygenated breeze before vehicular pollution chokes the city. The mind is peaceful, free from worldly distractions, enabling scholars and creators to produce their finest work. Furthermore, one who rises early finishes assignments well before deadlines, avoiding nerve-wracking haste.

### Passage 2 (8 Marks):
True patriotism does not consist merely in waving national flags during cricket matches or shouting emotional slogans on national holidays. Genuine patriotism is reflected in conscientious daily citizenship—obeying traffic regulations, conserving public property, keeping neighborhoods spotless, and paying fair taxes honestly. A corrupt person who cheats the public treasury while loudly singing the national anthem is a traitor in disguise. Real love for one's motherland demands selfless dedication to the upliftment of the underprivileged and preserving communal harmony.

6. Choose the correct alternative: The word 'underprivileged' refers to: (1 Mark)  
   (A) Very wealthy elites  
   (B) Poor and disadvantaged people  
   (C) Sports personalities

7. Find the word in the passage which means: **'honest and responsible / dutiful'**. (1 Mark)
8. Find the antonym of **'harmony'** from common vocabulary. (1 Mark)

1. Formal letter: practice checklist (official component rubric नहीं)

| जाँच-बिंदु | क्या देखें? |

| **Expression** | औपचारिक tone, स्पष्ट वाक्य, सही grammar और spelling। |

4. मिस्टेक बस्टर्स: बोर्ड परीक्षक कहाँ 1 से 2 अंक काटते हैं? (Mistake Busters)

| सामान्य गलती | इससे क्या समस्या हो सकती है? | बेहतर अभ्यास |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **गलती 1: 'Your's faithfully' में Apostrophe लगाना:** छात्र `Your's` या `your's` लिख देते हैं। | यह मानक लिखित अंग्रेज़ी में गलत रूप है; कोई निश्चित अंक-कटौती यहाँ प्रमाणित नहीं है। | **`Yours faithfully`** या **`Yours sincerely`** लिखें। |
| **गलती 2: संकुचित दिनांक लिखना (e.g., 12/03/26):** अंकगणितीय रूप में दिनांक लिख देना। | गैर-पेशेवर माना जाता है। | हमेशा विस्तारित दिनांक लिखें: **12 March 2026** या **March 12, 2026**। |
| **गलती 3: ई-मेल में प्राप्तकर्ता/विषय अस्पष्ट छोड़ना:** `To:` field में नाम और address गड्डमड्ड करना। | ई-मेल पूरक अभ्यास है; यह guide कोई RBSE ई-मेल format या अंक-कटौती प्रमाणित नहीं करती। | ई-मेल अभ्यास में प्राप्तकर्ता और subject अलग-अलग, स्पष्ट fields में दें। |
| **गलती 4: अनौपचारिक पत्र में Subject लिखना:** मित्र या माता-पिता को लिखते समय `Subject: Congratulating on birthday` लिख देना। | अनौपचारिक पत्र में विषय नहीं होता; यह अनावश्यक औपचारिकता है। | Informal Letter में कभी भी **Subject पंक्ति न लिखें**। सीधे Salutation से शुरू करें। |
| **गलती 5: पत्र के मध्य में दाएँ-बाएँ कूदना:** पता बाएँ, दिनांक दाएँ, समापन दाएँ लिख देना। | पुराने इंडेंटेड स्टाइल में अंक काटे जा सकते हैं। | सम्पूर्ण पत्र **Left Margin (बाईं ओर)** से ही प्रारंभ करें (Modern Block Style)। |
