* **आदर्श हल (Core Body Lines):** *"Incidents of mobile and purse snatching by bike-borne miscreants have increased alarmingly near Shastri Nagar park. Women and senior citizens are terrified of venturing out after dusk. I request you to increase police patrolling in the evening."*

### 📌 विगत वर्ष 5 (RBSE Board 2019):
* **प्रश्न:** Write a letter to your uncle thanking him for a wonderful wristwatch sent by him as a birthday gift.
* **आदर्श हल (Core Body Lines):** *"Thank you immensely for the elegant wristwatch you gifted me on my 16th birthday. It is not only beautiful but also very useful for managing time during examination hours. Every time I check the time, it reminds me of your affection."*

### 📌 विगत वर्ष 6 (RBSE Board 2018):
* **प्रश्न:** Write an application to the Headmaster of your school requesting him to issue your Character Certificate.
* **आदर्श हल (Core Body Lines):** *"I passed Class 10 from your school with 88% marks. I am seeking admission to a polytechnic college, which requires a Character Certificate. Kindly issue the certificate at an early date."*

### 📌 विगत वर्ष 7 (RBSE Board 2017):
* **प्रश्न:** Write a letter to the Postmaster complaining against the irregular delivery of letters by the area postman.
* **आदर्श हल (Core Body Lines):** *"The postman of our area does not deliver mail regularly. Important interview call letters, bank statements, and wedding invites are either delivered weeks late or dumped carelessly on verandas. Please direct the postman to be diligent."*

### 📌 विगत वर्ष 8 (RBSE Board 2016):
* **प्रश्न:** Write an email to the District Education Officer (DEO) requesting to provide sports equipment for your school playground.
* **आदर्श हल (Core Body Lines):** *"Our school football and cricket teams have qualified for the state-level tournament, but we lack quality bats, balls, and goal nets. We request your department to sanction sports grants for our school."*

### 📌 विगत वर्ष 9 (RBSE Board 2015):
* **प्रश्न:** Write a letter to your father requesting him to permit you to join an educational tour to Jaipur and Agra.
* **आदर्श हल (Core Body Lines):** *"Our school is organizing a four-day educational tour to historical monuments in Jaipur and Agra next month under teacher supervision. The tour fee is Rs. 1500. Kindly grant me permission and send the required amount."*

### 📌 विगत वर्ष 10 (RBSE Board 2014):
* **प्रश्न:** Write a letter to the Station House Officer (SHO) reporting the theft of your bicycle from the school bicycle stand.
* **आदर्श हल (Core Body Lines):** *"I parked my black Hero Atlas bicycle (Frame No. 89765) in the school stand at 8:00 AM today. When classes ended at 2:00 PM, the bicycle was missing. Please register my FIR and help trace my stolen bicycle."*

---
7. फटाफट परीक्षा पूर्व चीट शीट (Pre-Exam Rapid Cheat Sheet)

1. **लेआउट संरेखण:** सभी चीजें बाएँ मार्जिन (Left Margin) से शुरू करें।
2. **दिनांक शैली:** हमेशा `15 March 2026` लिखें (संख्या/माह/वर्ष)।
3. **विषय की स्पष्टता:** केवल Formal पत्र और Email में Subject लिखें (अधिकतम 5-7 शब्द)।
4. **इन्फॉर्मल में नो-सब्जेक्ट:** माता-पिता और मित्रों के पत्रों में **कभी भी Subject न लिखें**।
5. **संबोधन का चयन:**
   - अधिकारी/संपादक: `Sir / Madam`
   - मित्र: `Dear [Name]`
   - माता-पिता: `Respected Father / Dear Mother`
6. **समापन (Subscription):**
   - अधिकारियों को: `Yours faithfully`
   - शिक्षकों को: `Yours obediently`
   - संपादकों/व्यावसायिक: `Yours truly / Yours sincerely`
   - मित्रों/रिश्तेदारों को: `Yours lovingly / Your loving friend`
7. **ईमेल हेडर:** `To:` बॉक्स में अनिवार्य रूप से लोअरकेस ईमेल आईडी लिखें।
8. **शब्द सीमा:** 80-100 शब्दों में बात को स्पष्ट और मर्यादित रखें।

---
8. 15-मिनट आत्म-मूल्यांकन बोर्ड टेस्ट (15-Minute Self-Test)

**अभ्यास समय: 15 मिनट | Self-check: writing checklist; no separate official task mark given**

### प्रश्न (Choose Any ONE - 5 Marks):
* **विकल्प A (Letter):** You are Naresh/Neha residing at 25, Adarsh Nagar, Sriganganagar. Write a formal letter to the District Collector complaining against the unauthorized construction and encroachment on public roads causing massive traffic jams.  
* **विकल्प B (Email):** Draft an official email to the Principal of your school (`principal.gsss@gmail.com`) requesting permission to set up an English Literary Club in the school.

---

### मॉडल उत्तर-कुंजी एवं स्व-जाँच मानदंड (Self-Evaluation Checklist)
* **लेआउट जाँच:** क्या प्रेषक का पता, दिनांक, प्रापक का पद सही क्रम में बाएँ हैं? (हाँ = 2 अंक)
* **विषय-वस्तु जाँच:** क्या समस्या/अनुरोध का कारण और समाधान स्पष्ट लिखा गया है? (हाँ = 2 अंक)
* **व्याकरण जाँच:** क्या 'Yours' बिना apostrophe के लिखा गया है और Tense सही है? (हाँ = 1 अंक)
 * **स्व-मूल्यांकन:** उपयोगी विवरण, format और स्पष्ट भाषा की जाँच करें; task-specific official marks विभाजित नहीं हैं।

**Syllabus source correction, 13 October 2026:** Scope/marks above use the [Madhyamik Class 10 syllabus, PDF pp. 3–5](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf), not the separate Praveshika scheme. This correction does not certify the remaining exercise keys.

chapters.title: Unit 3: Story Writing (Outline-Based) — Exhaustive Smart Study Guide

content.value: माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर (RBSE Class 10 English - Paper Code: 02)

### Section B: Writing Skills (story is one listed task option)

**विषय:** अंग्रेजी (English Compulsory) | **विषय कोड:** 02  
**कक्षा:** 10वीं (माध्यमिक शिक्षा बोर्ड राजस्थान, अजमेर — RBSE)  
**इकाई ID:** `wr_ch03` | **खंड:** Section B (Writing Skills)  
**पाठ्यक्रम स्थिति:** Writing Skills (12 marks overall) में report/essay/story/blog task में से एक विकल्प हो सकता है; syllabus किसी story-specific अंक-विभाजन का उल्लेख नहीं करता।  
**शब्द सीमा:** 100–120 words (current syllabus); prompt के दिए outline/instructions का पालन करें।

---
🌟 स्मार्ट गाइड प्रवेश: 10 सेकंड में स्टोरी राइटिंग का सार (Topper's Formula)

> **Current exam note:** Story is one option in the 100–120-word report/essay/story/blog task within the 12-mark Writing Skills section. The syllabus gives no story-specific score split and does not make a title or moral universally mandatory.
> 
> शीर्षक और moral तभी शामिल करें जब prompt माँगे या वे कहानी के लिए उपयुक्त हों। नीचे की checklists अभ्यास-सुझाव हैं; ये आधिकारिक scoring rubric नहीं।
> 
> नीचे दिए गए नियम, time connectors और model stories का अभ्यास करें। प्रश्न-चयन और अंक की गारंटी नहीं है।

---
1. Story-writing practice checklist (official mark allocation नहीं)

| जाँच-बिंदु | क्या देखें? |
|:---|:---|
| **Prompt/outline** | सभी जरूरी संकेत शामिल हों और कहानी का क्रम स्पष्ट हो। |
| **Language** | Tense consistent, dialogue/description readable, spelling and punctuation checked. |
| **Ending** | कहानी का समाधान/अंत prompt से मेल खाए; moral only if requested. |

---
2. रूपरेखा विस्तार की 5-चरणीय तकनीक (5-Step Story Expansion Formula)

```
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │        THE 5-STEP OUTLINE EXPANSION BLUEPRINT          │
        └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
    ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
    ▼                               ▼                               ▼
[STEP 1: TITLE]             [STEP 2: OPENING]               [STEP 3: BODY]
Select concise,             "Once upon a time..."           Convert clues to
evocative title from        Establish setting &             Past Tense (V2) with
clues or central lesson.    introduce main characters.      smooth connectives.
    │                                                               │
    └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                    ▼
                        [STEP 4: CLIMAX & RESULT]
                        Problem reaches turning point
                        and delivers natural consequence.
                                    │
                                    ▼
                        [STEP 5: MORAL / LESSON]
                        Clear proverb placed at the
                        bottom: "Moral: Honesty is..."
```

### 🎯 5 useful story-writing suggestions (follow the prompt first)
1. **नियम 1: काल का अटल नियम (Past Tense Rule):**  
   रूपरेखा में संकेत हमेशा Present Indefinite में दिए होते हैं (जैसे: *a dog finds a bone... crosses a bridge... drops the bone* )। आपको लिखते समय इसे अनिवार्य रूप से **Past Tense (V2)** में बदलना होगा:  
   *Once a dog **found** a bone... He **was crossing** a bridge... The bone **dropped** into the water.*
2. **रूपरेखा:**  
   prompt के जरूरी संकेतों को शामिल करें और उनके बीच तार्किक संबंध बनाएँ। Prompt के निर्देश को प्राथमिकता दें।
3. **नियम 3: समय संयोजक शब्दों (Time Connectives) का प्रयोग:**  
   कहानी को जीवंत और प्रवाहपूर्ण बनाने के लिए इन शब्दों का उपयोग करें:  
   *Once upon a time... One fine day... Soon... Suddenly... Unfortunately... Meanwhile... At last... Eventually...*
4. **शीर्षक:** prompt माँगे या उपयुक्त लगे तो संक्षिप्त शीर्षक दें; centering, capitals या underlining की कोई सार्वभौमिक syllabus शर्त नहीं दी गई है।
5. **नैतिक शिक्षा:** moral केवल तब जोड़ें जब prompt माँगे या वह स्वाभाविक रूप से उपयोगी हो।

---
3. मिस्टेक बस्टर्स: बोर्ड परीक्षा में कहाँ कटते हैं अंक? (Mistake Busters)

| सामान्य गलती | इससे क्या समस्या हो सकती है? | बेहतर अभ्यास |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **भूल 1: prompt के निर्देशों को छोड़ना:** कहानी में जरूरी outline points शामिल न करना। | इससे उत्तर अधूरा हो सकता है; कोई निश्चित अंक-कटौती यहाँ प्रमाणित नहीं है। | पहले prompt पढ़ें; title/moral तभी दें जब माँगा गया हो या कथा के लिए उपयोगी हो। |
| **भूल 2: रूपरेखा के वाक्यों को mechanically copy करना:** tense/context न देखना। | tense consistency और clarity प्रभावित हो सकती है; कोई निश्चित अंक-कटौती यहाँ प्रमाणित नहीं। | समय-क्रम देखकर consistent tense चुनें और prompt के सभी जरूरी बिंदु स्वाभाविक रूप से जोड़ें। |
| **भूल 3: कहानी बहुत छोटी या अस्पष्ट रखना।** | आवश्यक घटनाक्रम/कारण छूट सकते हैं; निश्चित न्यूनतम शब्द संख्या यहाँ प्रमाणित नहीं। | Current syllabus की 100–120 शब्द सीमा और prompt का पालन करें। |
| **भूल 4: असंगत नैतिक शिक्षा जोड़ना:** कहानी एकता की शक्ति पर है और moral *"Greed is a curse"* लिखना। | इससे कहानी का निष्कर्ष असंगत हो सकता है; अलग अंक-कटौती प्रमाणित नहीं है। | केवल prompt के अनुरूप या स्वाभाविक रूप से प्रासंगिक moral दें। |

---
4. 12 संपूर्ण हल की गई बोर्ड मॉडल कहानियाँ (12 Exhaustive Solved Board Stories)

---

### 📖 मॉडल 1: संघे शक्ति कलौ युगे — बूढ़ा किसान और उसके चार झगड़ालू बेटे (Union is Strength)
* **Outline:** *An old farmer... four sons... always quarrelling... farmer falls ill... worried about sons... calls them... gives a bundle of sticks... asks to break... none can break... unties the bundle... gives single stick each... break easily... advises unity... moral.*

```
                             UNION IS STRENGTH
                             
Once upon a time, an old farmer lived in a village. He had four sons. They were 
always quarrelling among themselves. The farmer tried his best to advise them, 
but all in vain. 

As the farmer grew old and fell critically ill, he worried about their future. 
One day, he called all his sons to his bedside. He handed them a bundle of dry 
sticks and asked each son to break it. One by one, all four sons tried with all 
their might, but none could break the tied bundle.

Then, the wise father untied the bundle and gave a single stick to each son. 
Now, they broke the individual sticks effortlessly in a second. The father 
smiled and advised, "My dear sons, if you remain united like the bundle, no 
enemy can harm you. But if you quarrel and divide, anyone will crush you easily." 
The sons realized their folly, promised to live unitedly, and never fought again.

Moral: United we stand, divided we fall. (Union is strength.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 2: लोभी कुत्ता और पानी में परछाई (The Greedy Dog)
* **Outline:** *A dog... hungry... finds a bone at a butcher's shop... runs away... crosses a stream over a bridge... looks into water... sees own reflection... thinks another dog with bigger bone... barks... bone falls into water... sad... moral.*

```
                              THE GREEDY DOG
                              
Once upon a time, there was a dog who was very hungry. He roamed everywhere in 
search of food. Luckily, he found a juicy bone outside a butcher's shop. He 
picked it up in his mouth and ran toward the lonely woods to enjoy his meal in 
peace.

On his way, he had to cross a narrow wooden bridge over a clear stream. As he 
walked across, he stopped and looked down into the water. He saw his own reflection 
in the crystal-clear water. Being foolish and greedy, he thought that there was 
another dog holding a larger piece of bone.

Greed overpowered his senses. He wanted to snatch that bone too. As soon as he 
opened his mouth to bark, the bone slipped from his jaws and dropped into the deep 
water. It sank to the bottom and was lost forever. The greedy dog was left with 
nothing but repentance and an empty stomach.

Moral: Greed is a curse. (Do not covet what belongs to others.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 3: मधुमक्खी और दयालु कबूतर (The Dove and the Bee)
* **Outline:** *A bee... falls into a stream... struggling to survive... a dove sitting on a tree sees... drops a broad leaf... bee climbs up... dries wings... flies away... a hunter aims at dove... bee stings hunter's hand... arrow misses... dove flies away safe... moral.*

```
                          THE DOVE AND THE BEE
                          
One hot summer day, a little honeybee flew to a mountain stream to drink water. 
While drinking, a sudden gust of wind blew her into the swirling water. She was 
drowning and struggling desperately for life.

A gentle dove sitting on a branch of a nearby banyan tree noticed the helpless 
bee. Taking pity on the drowning insect, the dove quickly plucked a broad green 
leaf and dropped it right beside the bee. The bee climbed onto the leaf, dried 
her wet wings in the warm sun, and safely flew away to her hive.

A few days later, a cruel hunter entered the forest. He spotted the beautiful 
dove resting on a branch and drew his bow, aiming an arrow at her. The grateful 
bee saw the grave danger. She instantly darted down and stung the hunter's hand 
fiercely. The hunter cried out in sharp agony, and his arrow missed the target. 
Hearing the commotion, the dove immediately took flight and escaped unharmed.

Moral: Do good, have good. (One good turn deserves another.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 4: चरवाहा लड़का और झूठा भेड़िया (The Shepherd Boy and the Wolf)
* **Outline:** *A shepherd boy... grazes sheep near a village... feels bored... plays a prank... cries "Wolf! Wolf!"... villagers rush with sticks... boy laughs... no wolf... plays trick again... villagers angry... real wolf comes... boy cries for help... nobody believes... wolf kills sheep... boy weeps... moral.*

```
                       THE SHEPHERD BOY AND THE WOLF
                       
Once upon a time, a shepherd boy was employed to graze a flock of sheep near the 
edge of a dark forest. To relieve his boredom, he decided to play a mischievous 
trick on the villagers.

He climbed up a high boulder and shouted at the top of his voice, "Wolf! Wolf! 
Help! The wolf is attacking the sheep!" Hearing his panicked cries, the kind-hearted 
villagers left their farm work and ran with sticks and sickles to rescue him. 
When they arrived out of breath, they found no wolf. The boy burst into arrogant 
laughter, mocking their anxiety. The annoyed villagers returned to their work. 
A few days later, the foolish boy repeated the same false prank, irritating the 
villagers even more.

One evening, a ferocious wolf actually emerged from the dense shadows and attacked 
the flock. Terrified, the boy screamed frantically, "Wolf! Please help me! A real 
wolf is here!" But this time, the villagers thought he was lying again and ignored 
his screams. The wolf slaughtered many sheep and injured the boy. 

Moral: A liar is never believed, even when he speaks the truth.
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 5: सच्चा मित्र मुसीबत में ही पहचाना जाता है (Two Friends and the Bear)
* **Outline:** *Two friends... Vijay and Raju... walk through a dense forest... promise to help each other... sudden appearance of a bear... Vijay climbs a tall tree... Raju cannot climb... lies flat on the ground... holds breath... bear sniffs ears... thinks dead... bear walks away... Vijay climbs down... asks what bear said... moral.*

```
                        TWO FRIENDS AND THE BEAR
                        
Two close friends, Vijay and Raju, were travelling together through a deep and 
dangerous forest. Knowing the hazards of wild animals, they pledged to stand by 
each other in times of peril.

Suddenly, a massive brown bear emerged from behind the bushes, growling loudly. 
Without sparing a thought for his friend, Vijay panicked, bolted forward, and 
quickly scrambled up a tall tree. Raju, who did not know how to climb trees, 
found himself stranded on the ground. 

Remembering that bears do not touch dead bodies, Raju instantly threw himself 
flat on the dusty ground and held his breath, pretending to be lifeless. The 
heavy beast lumbered up to him, sniffed around his ears, face, and chest, and 
judged him to be a corpse. The bear quietly walked away into the thicket. 

When the danger had passed, Vijay climbed down from the tree and asked jokingly, 
"Dear Raju, what secret did the bear whisper into your ear?" Raju replied coldly, 
"The bear advised me never to trust a selfish friend who abandons his companion 
in times of danger."

Moral: A friend in need is a friend indeed.
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 6: खरगोश और कछुए की दौड़ (The Hare and the Tortoise)
* **Outline:** *A hare... proud of speed... mocks a slow-moving tortoise... tortoise challenges hare to a race... fox acts as judge... race begins... hare runs fast... far ahead... decides to take a nap under a shady tree... tortoise walks slowly and steadily... reaches finish line... hare wakes up... loses... moral.*

```
                       THE HARE AND THE TORTOISE
                       
Once upon a time, a proud hare lived in a green valley. He was extremely boastful 
about his swift running speed and frequently ridiculed a gentle tortoise for his 
plodding pace. Tired of his daily insults, the tortoise quietly challenged the 
hare to a running race.

The amused hare accepted the challenge with arrogance. A wise fox was appointed 
the judge, and the race commenced. The hare darted off like an arrow and covered 
half the distance within minutes. Looking back, he saw the tortoise far behind, 
crawling inch by inch. 

Thinking he had ample time to spare, the overconfident hare lay down under a cool, 
leafy tree to take a brief nap. The soothing breeze soon put him into a deep 
slumber. Meanwhile, the tortoise kept walking steadily, never pausing for a single 
moment. He quietly passed the sleeping hare and reached the victory post. 
When the hare woke up and rushed to the finish line, he found the tortoise crowned 
with victory.

Moral: Slow and steady wins the race. (Pride goes before a fall.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 7: चतुर लोमड़ी और मूर्ख कौवा (The Fox and the Crow)
* **Outline:** *A crow... finds a piece of cheese... perches on a branch... hungry fox smells cheese... wants it... flatters crow... praises black feathers and sweet voice... asks crow to sing... foolish crow feels proud... opens beak to sing 'Caw-Caw'... cheese falls... fox grabs and runs... moral.*

```
                         THE FOX AND THE CROW
                         
One morning, a hungry crow managed to steal a delicious piece of cheese from a 
baker's kitchen window. Delighted with his prize, he flew to the branch of a tall 
neem tree to feast upon it at leisure.

A cunning fox strolling nearby caught the appetizing aroma of the cheese. Looking 
up, he saw the crow holding the succulent morsel firmly in his beak. The witty 
fox devised an immediate plan to deceive the foolish bird. He walked to the base 
of the tree, bowed politely, and said, "Good morning, handsome Crow! How splendid 
your glossy feathers shine today! Surely, a bird with such royal beauty must possess 
a divine and melodious voice. Will you not enchant me with a sweet song?"

Flattered by the deceitful praise, the vain crow was overwhelmed with pride. 
Forgetting caution, he opened his wide beak to sing a loud "Caw! Caw!". The moment 
he opened his mouth, the cheese slipped and fell straight to the ground. The fox 
snapped it up greedily, swallowed it whole, and trotted away, laughing.

Moral: Beware of sweet flatterers. (Vanity leads to loss.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 8: शेर और कृतज्ञ चूहा (The Lion and the Mouse)
* **Outline:** *A lion... sleeping under a tree... a little mouse plays on his body... lion wakes up in fury... catches mouse with paws... mouse begs for mercy... promises to help some day... lion laughs and lets him go... hunters spread a rope net... lion trapped and roars... mouse hears... nibbles ropes... lion freed... moral.*

```
                         THE LION AND THE MOUSE
                         
A mighty lion, the king of the forest, was fast asleep under the cool shade of an 
oak tree. A playful little mouse, unaware of the sleeping monarch, began scampering 
up and down his golden mane. 

Woken from his peaceful slumber, the majestic lion roared in fury and trapped the 
tiny creature beneath his massive paw. Terrified, the trembling mouse pleaded 
piteously, "O noble King of beasts, forgive my unintentional trespass! Spare my 
worthless life, and who knows, I may repay your kindness some day." The lion chuckled 
at the absurd thought of a fragile mouse helping the king of the jungle, but feeling 
generous, he lifted his paw and let the mouse scurry away.

A few months later, the lion was ensnared in a hunter's strong rope net. The great 
beast roared in helpless agony. Recognizing the royal voice, the little mouse rushed 
to the scene. Without losing a second, he began gnawing through the thick hemp 
ropes with his sharp teeth. Soon, the knots snapped, and the grateful lion walked out 
free.

Moral: Mercy brings its own reward. (Even the smallest friend can be of great help.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 9: बुद्धिमान कौवा और मटके का पानी (The Thirsty Crow)
* **Outline:** *A crow... very thirsty... flies across dry lands... finds a pitcher in a garden... water at the bottom... beak cannot reach... thinks of an idea... sees pebbles nearby... picks pebbles one by one... drops into pitcher... water level rises... drinks water... flies away happy... moral.*

```
                          THE THIRSTY CROW
                          
On a blistering afternoon in June, a crow felt intensely thirsty. Parched and 
exhausted, he flew across parched barren fields and villages in search of drinking 
water, but all ponds and wells had dried up.

Just as his strength was failing, he spotted a tall earthen pitcher lying in a 
deserted cottage garden. He flew down eagerly and peered inside. To his sorrow, 
there was only a tiny quantity of water remaining at the very bottom. He extended 
his neck, but his beak could not reach the refreshing water.

Instead of despairing, the wise crow looked around and noticed a pile of small 
pebbles lying near a brick wall. A brilliant plan flashed in his sharp mind. 
One by one, he picked up the pebbles in his beak and dropped them patiently into 
the pitcher. With every pebble dropped, the water level gradually rose higher. 
Soon, the water touched the brim. The triumphant crow drank to his heart's content, 
quenched his burning thirst, and flew away cheerfully into the blue sky.

Moral: Where there is a will, there is a way. (Necessity is the mother of invention.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 10: सोने के अंडे देने वाली हंसिनी (The Goose That Laid Golden Eggs)
* **Outline:** *A poor countryman... owns a magical goose... goose lays one golden egg every morning... countryman becomes rich... becomes greedy... thinks goose has stomach full of gold... wants all gold at once... kills goose with knife... finds no gold inside... loses everything... weeps in grief... moral.*

```
                 THE GOOSE THAT LAID GOLDEN EGGS
                 
Once upon a time, a humble farmer lived in a small village. Fortune smiled upon 
him when he purchased a magical white goose. To his utter delight, the remarkable 
bird began laying a pure golden egg every single morning.

The farmer sold the golden eggs in the town market and quickly grew prosperous. 
He built a luxurious mansion, bought lavish clothes, and lived comfortably. 
However, as his wealth multiplied, unquenchable greed consumed his moral sanity. 
He began thinking, "Why should I wait every day for a single egg? Surely, the bird's 
stomach must be an enormous storehouse filled with countless nuggets of gold. 
If I cut her open, I will become the wealthiest landlord in one single day!"

Blind with avarice, he seized a sharp kitchen knife and mercilessly slaughtered 
the harmless goose. But upon cutting her open, he was horrified to discover that 
her anatomy was exactly like any ordinary bird. There was not a speck of gold 
inside. Stricken with despair, he wept bitterly, realizing that his wicked greed 
had destroyed his eternal source of fortune.

Moral: Greed breeds grief. (Those who desire all often lose everything.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 11: दर्जी और बुद्धिमान हाथी (The Tailor and the Elephant)
* **Outline:** *A king's elephant... passes a tailor's shop daily on way to river... tailor gives fruits and buns... they become friends... one day tailor in bad temper... elephant stretches trunk as usual... tailor pricks needle into trunk... elephant feels pain... goes to river... fills trunk with muddy water... returns... squirts mud over all new clothes... tailor ruined... moral.*

```
                       THE TAILOR AND THE ELEPHANT
                       
A royal temple elephant passed through a busy market street every morning to take 
his ritual bath in the holy river. Along his regular path stood the shop of a 
tailor. The tailor was fond of the gentle creature and fed him ripe bananas and 
fresh buns every day. A bond of warm companionship grew between them.

One morning, the tailor was in an irritable temper due to business disputes. As 
usual, the elephant halted affectionately at his shop window and stretched his 
long trunk inside, expecting his customary treat. Instead of feeding him, the cruel 
tailor picked up a long needle and viciously pricked the elephant's sensitive trunk. 
The gentle giant winced in sharp pain, quietly withdrew his wounded trunk, and 
walked on toward the river without showing anger.

After bathing, the clever elephant filled his trunk with slimy, black ditch water. 
On his journey back, he halted outside the tailor's shop and squirted a powerful 
stream of filthy mud straight into the room. All the freshly stitched expensive 
silk garments prepared for royal weddings were completely ruined. The tailor wept 
in agony, realizing that malice brings swift retribution.

Moral: Tit for tat. (Harm watch, harm catch.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 12: ईमानदार लकड़हारा और जलपरी (The Honest Woodcutter)
* **Outline:** *A poor woodcutter... cuts wood near a deep river... iron axe slips from hand... falls into deep water... weeps helplessly... Goddess of Water appears... dives in... brings golden axe... woodcutter says "Not mine"... dives again... brings silver axe... refuses again... brings iron axe... happily accepts... Goddess pleased with honesty... gifts all three axes... moral.*

```
                      THE HONEST WOODCUTTER
                      
Once upon a time, an honest woodcutter was chopping dry firewood from a tree 
branch hanging over the deep waters of a rushing river. Suddenly, his iron axe 
slipped from his sweaty grip, splashed into the deep currents, and sank out of sight. 

Being poor, the axe was his sole means of livelihood. He sat on the sandy bank 
and wept bitterly. Moved by his genuine distress, the beautiful Goddess of the 
River emerged from the swirling water and asked the cause of his grief. Upon hearing 
his plight, the Goddess plunged into the river and reappeared holding a glittering 
axe of pure gold. "Is this your lost axe?" she asked. The woodcutter shook his 
head and replied, "No, kind Mother, this costly axe does not belong to me."

The Goddess dived a second time and brought forth a shining axe made of pure 
silver. Again, the truthful man refused, saying it was not his tool. Finally, 
she plunged down a third time and retrieved his rusty old iron axe. Seeing his 
real tool, the woodcutter's face lit up with joy, and he exclaimed, "Yes! That is 
my axe!" Delighted by his unwavering truthfulness, the Goddess rewarded him with 
both the gold and silver axes alongside his iron one.

Moral: Honesty is the best policy.
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 13: मूर्ख कौवे और चालाक सियार (The Stork and the Fox)
* **Outline:** *A cunning fox... invites a stork to dinner... serves thin soup in a shallow plate... fox laps it easily... stork's long bill cannot reach... remains hungry... stork invites fox... serves minced food in a narrow long-necked jar... stork eats easily with beak... fox licks mouth outside... realizes mistake... moral.*

```
                        THE FOX AND THE STORK
                        
Once upon a time, a mischievous fox decided to play an unkind trick on his 
neighbor, a graceful stork. He invited the stork to his den for dinner. The 
unsuspecting stork gladly accepted the friendly invitation.

When dinner was served, the sly fox poured delicious, aromatic soup into two 
wide, shallow plates. The fox easily lapped up his meal with his broad tongue. 
However, the poor stork, with her long and slender beak, could not take a single 
drop and stayed completely hungry. The fox laughed slyly at her helplessness. 
The gentle stork politely thanked him and departed without showing anger.

A few days later, the stork invited the fox to dine with her. She prepared a 
fragrant dish of tender meat and fish and served it in two tall jars with long, 
narrow necks. The stork easily plunged her slender bill into the vessel and relished 
the feast. The hungry fox could only sniff the tempting aroma and lick the outside 
of the glass rim, unable to squeeze his snout inside. He hung his head in deep 
shame, learning that a person who mocks others must be prepared to face the same 
treatment.

Moral: Do unto others as you would have them do unto you. (Tit for tat.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 14: राजा रॉबर्ट ब्रूस और मकड़ी (King Bruce and the Spider)
* **Outline:** *King Robert Bruce of Scotland... defeated six times by English invaders... hides in a dark cave... despair and gloom... sees a tiny spider... trying to reach its web on high ceiling... falls down six times... tries seventh time... reaches web successfully... Bruce inspired... gathers army... fights battle... wins freedom... moral.*

```
                      KING BRUCE AND THE SPIDER
                      
Robert Bruce, the brave King of Scotland, fought six desperate wars to liberate 
his beloved motherland from ruthless foreign invaders. Unfortunately, his army was 
crushed every time, and he was forced to flee for his life. Weary and heartbroken, 
he took refuge inside a desolate mountain cave, ready to abandon all hope.

As he lay on the damp stone floor contemplating his miserable defeat, his eyes 
fell upon a tiny spider hanging from the ceiling by a slender thread. The little 
insect was trying desperately to swing herself from one rocky ledge to another 
to build her web. 

Bruce watched with keen curiosity. One, two, three, four, five, six times the tiny 
creature fell to the ground, yet she never gave up. On the seventh courageous 
attempt, the spider exerted all her strength, swung across the void, and anchored 
her thread firmly onto the rock wall. 

A surge of electrifying inspiration ignited the king's spirit. He sprang to his 
feet and shouted, "If a tiny spider can triumph after six failures, surely a king 
can do the same!" Bruce rallied his scattered soldiers, fought a valiant battle, 
and routed the enemy completely, winning Scotland's freedom forever.

Moral: Try, try, and try again until you succeed. (Perseverance is the key to success.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 15: घमंडी बारहसिंगा और उसके सुंदर सींग (The Stag and His Horns)
* **Outline:** *A stag... drinks water at a pool... sees reflection... admires magnificent branched antlers... hates his thin, ugly legs... hears hunter's hounds barking... runs swiftly... thin legs carry him fast... antlers get entangled in low tree branches... hounds catch him... dying stag realizes... moral.*

```
                       THE STAG AND HIS HORNS
                       
A handsome stag was drinking cool, clear water from a woodland pool on a calm 
morning. Looking down at the still surface, he gazed at his reflection. He was 
enamored of the royal majesty of his curved, branched antlers and praised their 
matchless beauty. However, when he looked down at his slender, spindly legs, he 
felt disgusted and cursed nature for giving him such plain and ugly limbs.

Suddenly, the loud baying of hunters' hounds echoed through the trees. Terrified, 
the stag leaped forward into a frantic run. His despised thin legs carried him 
swiftly across the open meadows like the wind, leaving the pursuing pack of hounds 
far behind. 

However, as he plunged into a thick forest path, his sprawling, branch-like antlers 
became hopelessly entangled in the dense overhanging boughs of a wild tree. He 
tugged frantically, but could not free his head. Within moments, the fierce hounds 
caught up with him and dragged him down. As he lay gasping his last breath, he 
sighed with bitter sorrow, "Alas! The legs I despised were saving my life, while the 
horns I admired so foolishly have caused my tragic doom."

Moral: All that glitters is not gold. (Do not judge worth by outward appearances.)
```

---

### 📖 मॉडल 16: मूर्ख गधा और शेर की खाल (The Donkey in Lion's Skin)
* **Outline:** *A washerman's donkey... underfed and weak... washerman finds a dead lion's skin... drapes skin over donkey... turns donkey loose into green farm fields at night... farmers mistake for real lion... run away in fear... donkey eats rich crops... grows fat... one moonlit night hears other donkeys braying... brays aloud... farmers discover reality... beat him with heavy sticks... moral.*

```
                    THE DONKEY IN LION'S SKIN
                    
A poor washerman owned a lazy donkey. Because business was slow, the washerman 
could not provide enough fodder, and the poor animal grew emaciated and weak. 
One chilly afternoon, while walking through the jungle, the washerman stumbled 
upon the carcass of a royal lion. A cunning scheme flashed in his mind.

He carefully skinned the beast, brought the hide home, and draped it over the back 
of his donkey. At nightfall, he drove the disguised donkey into the lush green 
wheat fields belonging to nearby farmers. The local villagers caught a glimpse of 
the beast from afar, mistook it for a ferocious man-eating lion, and fled in terror. 
For weeks, the donkey gorged himself upon the sweetest green crops and grew plump 
and strong.

One moonlit night, while feasting peacefully in a cucumber patch, the donkey heard 
the distant braying of fellow donkeys from a nearby meadow. Overcome with sudden 
delight, he forgot his royal disguise and lifted his snout to bray a loud, grating 
"Hee-Haw! Hee-Haw!". Hearing the unmistakable donkey bray, the enraged farmers 
realized how they had been fooled. They rushed into the field armed with heavy clubs 
and thrashed the foolish creature within an inch of his life.

Moral: Clothes do not make the man. (A fool cannot hide his foolishness for long.)
```

---

6. फटाफट परीक्षा पूर्व चीट शीट (Pre-Exam Rapid Cheat Sheet)

1. **Format:** Top center = **TITLE** (Capitalized/Bold); Bottom left = **Moral:** (Proverb).
2. **Tense Rule:** Always write in **Simple Past Tense (V2 / was / were)**. Never copy present tense clues directly.
3. **Paragraph Structure:** 2 to 3 paragraphs: Opening -> Climax -> Resolution.
4. **Length:** Follow the current syllabus range of 100–120 words and the prompt. Any shorter models elsewhere in this guide are supplementary practice, not current-length templates.
5. **Time Anchors:** Use *Once upon a time, One day, Soon, Suddenly, At last, Meanwhile*.
6. **Clue Coverage:** Ensure every single outline clue is incorporated naturally.
7. **Self-check:** prompt के सभी निर्देश पूरे हैं, कहानी 100–120 शब्द की है और tense consistent है। यह आधिकारिक mark split नहीं।

---
7. 15-मिनट आत्म-मूल्यांकन बोर्ड टेस्ट (15-Minute Self-Test)

**अभ्यास समय: 15 मिनट | Self-check: use the checklist above (not a separate official mark allocation)**

### प्रश्न:
Write a story in about 80 words using the outline given below. Give a suitable title and a moral to it:

*A hungry fox... walks into a vineyard... sees ripe juicy grapes hanging from high trellis... mouth waters... jumps high... fails to reach... jumps again and again... exhausted... walks away saying "Grapes are sour, I will fall sick"... moral.*

---

### मॉडल उत्तर-कुंजी एवं मूल्यांकन मानदंड (Marking Key for Self-Test)
* **Title (1 Mark):** **THE FOX AND THE SOUR GRAPES**
* **Story Body (2 Marks):** Past Tense sentences detailing the fox's hunger, effort to leap, exhaustion, and walking away.
* **Moral (1 Mark):** *Moral: It is easy to dislike what you cannot attain.*

**Syllabus source correction, 13 October 2026:** Scope/marks above use the [Madhyamik Class 10 syllabus, PDF pp. 3–5](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf), not the separate Praveshika scheme. This correction does not certify the remaining exercise keys.

> **Current exam note:** RBSE 2026–27 includes an analytical paragraph of 100–120 words on a map, chart, graph or cues within the 12-mark Writing Skills section. The syllabus does not give this individual task a separate mark split. The checklist and examples below are practice guidance.

---
1. Analytical paragraph practice checklist (official mark allocation नहीं)

| जाँच-बिंदु | क्या देखें? |
|:---|:---|
| **Data selection** | मुख्य प्रवृत्ति/तुलना चुनें; सभी आँकड़े दोहराना जरूरी नहीं। |
| **Analysis** | सही आंकड़ों का संदर्भ सहित उपयोग करें; तथ्य और inference अलग रखें। |
| **Structure and language** | 100–120 शब्दों में coherent paragraph, accurate grammar and units. |

---
2. विजुअल स्टिमुलस डिकोडिंग तकनीक (Visual Stimulus Decoding Formula)

```
        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │      VISUAL STIMULUS / PICTURE DECODING FORMULA        │
        └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
    ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
    ▼                               ▼                               ▼
[STEP 1: CENTRAL THEME]     [STEP 2: ACTION ELEMENTS]       [STEP 3: VALUE MESSAGE]
Identify the core message   Observe human activities,       What moral, civic duty,
(e.g., Cleanliness drive,   instruments, background         or social awareness does
saving water, road safety). setting, and key symbols.       the image evoke?
    │                                                               │
    └───────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                                    ▼
                      [STEP 4: TENSE DISCIPLINE]
                      • Present Tense for general issues
                        (Pollution, Water, Morning Walk).
                      • Past Tense for events celebrated
                        (Annual Function, Prize Distribution).
```

### 🎯 वाक्य निर्माण के 5 शक्तिशाली आरंभकर्ता (5 High-Yield Sentence Starters):
1. *"The given visual depicts a thought-provoking scene of..."* (चित्र की थीम स्पष्ट करना)
2. *"It vividly highlights the burning problem / noble concept of..."* (मुख्य समस्या/अवधारणा)
3. *"In the foreground, we can observe people actively engaged in..."* (विजुअल विवरण)
4. *"This scene underscores the urgent necessity to..."* (सामाजिक आवश्यकता)
5. *"In conclusion, it inspires every responsible citizen to..."* (सशक्त समापन)

---
3. मिस्टेक बस्टर्स: बोर्ड परीक्षक कहाँ अंक काटते हैं? (Examiner's Mistake Busters)

| सामान्य गलती | इससे क्या समस्या हो सकती है? | बेहतर अभ्यास |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **भूल 1: बिना Title के पैराग्राफ लिखना।** | कोई सार्वभौमिक title requirement या अलग अंक-कटौती syllabus में निर्दिष्ट नहीं है। | prompt title माँगे तो दें; अन्यथा स्पष्ट शुरुआत और coherent paragraph पर ध्यान दें। |
| **भूल 2: अत्यधिक सरल या दोहराव वाली भाषा।** | इससे विचार और तुलना अस्पष्ट हो सकते हैं; निश्चित marks split प्रमाणित नहीं है। | सरल, सटीक भाषा और जरूरी linking words इस्तेमाल करें। |
| **भूल 3: काल (Tense) का घालमेल:** *Annual Function* का वर्णन करते समय आधी पंक्तियाँ Present में और आधी Past में लिख देना। | व्याकरण के अंक कट जाते हैं। | यदि आयोजित हो चुके उत्सव का वर्णन है, तो पूरी तरह **Simple Past Tense** में लिखें; यदि सामान्य विषय (जैसे Morning Walk) है, तो **Simple Present Tense** में लिखें। |
| **भूल 4: शब्द-सीमा की अनदेखी:** उत्तर निर्धारित सीमा से बहुत कम या अधिक लिखना। | कोई सार्वभौमिक कटौती यहाँ प्रमाणित नहीं है। | RBSE syllabus की 100–120 शब्द सीमा और प्रश्न के निर्देश मानें। |

4. Analytical paragraph practice models (14 examples)

---

### 🖼️ मॉडल 1 (Visual Stimulus): स्वच्छ भारत अभियान (Swachh Bharat Abhiyan / Clean India Mission)
* **Prompt/Visual Clue:** *A picture showing school students holding brooms, sweeping school premises, collecting plastic waste in blue and green dustbins, and planting saplings.*

```
                       SWACHH BHARAT ABHIYAN
                       
The given visual vividly depicts dedicated school students actively participating 
in the 'Swachh Bharat Abhiyan' (Clean India Mission). Armed with brooms, dustpans, 
and trash bags, these young volunteers are enthusiastically cleaning their school 
campus and surrounding pathways. 

They are segregating wet and dry refuse into green and blue dustbins, demonstrating 
scientific waste management. In the background, teachers and students are planting 
shady saplings to enrich biodiversity. 

Cleanliness is indeed next to godliness. A pristine environment prevents fatal 
vector-borne diseases such as malaria and dengue while creating an aesthetically 
pleasing atmosphere for intellectual learning. This inspiring visual conveys the 
vital civic message that maintaining public hygiene is not merely a government 
duty, but a sacred collective responsibility of every patriotic citizen.
```

### 🖼️ मॉडल 2 (Visual Stimulus): जल संरक्षण एवं वर्षा जल संचयन (Water Conservation & Rainwater Harvesting)
* **Prompt/Visual Clue:** *A diagram/picture showing rooftop rainwater harvesting, a pipeline connected to an underground recharge pit, a drying tap with a drop falling, and parched agricultural land.*

```
                    SAVE WATER — SAVE LIFE
                    
The presented visual highlights the crucial imperative of water conservation through 
rooftop rainwater harvesting. It showcases rainwater from the roof being filtered 
and channeled through perforated conduits into an underground storage reservoir 
and recharge borewell. 

Water is the very elixir of existence, yet reckless wastage and rapid deforestation 
have depleted groundwater aquifers to perilous levels, especially across arid 
regions like Rajasthan. The dripping tap symbolizes that every single drop of water 
squandered today accelerates tomorrow's ecological catastrophe. 

By reviving traditional storage structures like Tankas and adopting modern rooftop 
harvesting, households can achieve complete drinking water independence throughout 
scorching summers. We must adopt the pledge: "Conserve water today to secure humanity's 
tomorrow."
```

```
road safety regulations. It illustrates disciplined commuters halted behind the 
stop line at a red signal while pedestrians traverse the road safely along the

Two-wheeler riders are prudently wearing ISI-marked protective helmets, while the

and reckless mobile phone usage while driving turn public roads into fatal slaughterhouses. 
Speed thrills but kills. 

Adhering to basic traffic discipline, maintaining lane decorum, and respecting 
pedestrian rights safeguard precious human lives. Traffic regulations are crafted 
not to impede our mobility, but to ensure that every commuter returns home safely 
to their waiting families.
```

### 🖼️ मॉडल 4 (Visual Stimulus): वृक्षारोपण एवं पर्यावरण सुरक्षा (Plantation: Green Rajasthan, Clean Rajasthan)
* **Prompt/Visual Clue:** *Children and elderly citizens planting saplings in a public park, watering young plants, birds nesting in leafy boughs, and a sunny clear skyline.*

```
                 TREE PLANTATION: OUR GREEN LIFELINE
                 
The given visual depicts an inspiring community tree plantation drive. Citizens of 
all age groups—from cheerful schoolchildren to venerable elders—are working in 
unison, digging soil pits, planting fresh saplings, and watering them tenderly. 

Trees represent the veritable green lungs of our biosphere. They absorb toxic carbon 
emissions, release life-giving oxygen, mitigate catastrophic global warming, and 
anchor soil to prevent desertification. Deforestation brings devastating heatwaves, 
erratic droughts, and species extinction. 

Planting trees restores ecological balance, brings refreshing monsoon showers, and 
provides sanctuary to birds and wildlife. Each person ought to adopt and nurture 
at least five saplings to celebrate birthdays and festivals. A greener planet is the 
noblest inheritance we can bestow upon posterity.
```

### 📝 मॉडल 5 (Verbal Prompt): विद्यालय का वार्षिक उत्सव (Annual Function of Our School)

```
The Annual Prize Distribution Function of Government Senior Secondary School was

board results.

and an inspiring English drama advocating girl-child literacy. The Chief Guest 
distributed glittering trophies and certificates to academic toppers and sports 
champions. In his presidential address, he exhorted students to cultivate moral 
integrity and diligent work habits. The memorable gala concluded with the singing 
of the National Anthem.
```

### 📝 मॉडल 6 (Verbal Prompt): प्रातःकालीन सैर के स्वास्थ्य लाभ (The Morning Walk)
* **Verbal Prompt:** *Early rising... cool breeze... lush green park... physical exercise... mental peace... fit body... doctors advise.*

```
                    THE BLESSINGS OF A MORNING WALK
                    
A brisk morning walk is widely acknowledged as the simplest, most economical, and 
beneficial form of physical exercise for individuals of every age. Rising early at 
dawn allows one to inhale crisp, oxygen-rich air before vehicular pollution chokes 
the bustling city streets. 

Walking briskly through a dew-kissed green park accelerates blood circulation, 
strengthens cardiovascular endurance, and regulates blood sugar and hypertension. 
The serene morning environment, accompanied by the sweet chirping of birds, dispels 
mental exhaustion and infuses positive intellectual vitality for the rigorous day 
ahead. 

Medical practitioners unanimously advise at least thirty minutes of morning walking 
to combat modern sedentary lifestyle disorders. It acts as a natural tonic, keeping 
the human physique robust, agile, and cheerful throughout the day.
```

### 📝 मॉडल 7 (Verbal Prompt): स्वतंत्रता दिवस समारोह (Independence Day Celebration in School)
* **Verbal Prompt:** *15 August... national festival... tricolor flag hoisted by Principal... march past... national anthem... patriotic speeches... distribution of sweets.*

```
                     INDEPENDENCE DAY CELEBRATION
                     
Our school celebrated the 79th Independence Day on 15 August with solemn patriotic 
fervor and boundless enthusiasm. The school campus was exquisitely embellished with 
tricolor flags, buntings, and floral rangolis. 

At 8:00 AM sharp, our revered Principal unfurled the National Tricolor amidst thunderous 
applause. The NCC cadets and scout contingents presented a crisp, synchronised March 
Past and rendered a royal salute. All present sang the National Anthem in unision. 

Students delivered soul-stirring bilingual speeches recalling the supreme sacrifices 
of immortal martyrs like Bhagat Singh, Subhas Chandra Bose, and Mahatma Gandhi.

address, the Principal urged the youth to dedicate their talents to national
```

### 📝 मॉडल 8 (Verbal Prompt): मतदान का महत्व (The Value of Voting in a Democracy)
* **Verbal Prompt:** *Right to vote... 18 years... backbone of democracy... no cash or caste bias... electing honest leaders... every single vote counts.*

```
                    THE VALUE OF VOTING IN A DEMOCRACY
                    
Voting is not merely an optional civil privilege; it is the fundamental constitutional 
pillar upon which a robust and vibrant democracy rests. In India, the Constitution 
guarantees universal adult franchise to every citizen who attains eighteen years 
of age, irrespective of caste, creed, gender, or economic status. 

Each ballot cast is a powerful democratic weapon that shapes national governance, 
infrastructure, economic policy, and public welfare. Indifference toward voting 
allows corrupt and incompetent leaders to capture power. 

Citizens must exercise their sacred franchise with conscientious responsibility, 
rising above communal, caste, or monetary enticements. Electing clean, visionary, 
and progressive representatives is essential to steer our nation toward prosperity. 
Always remember: "A vigilant voter is the true architect of an enlightened democracy."
```

### 📝 मॉडल 9 (Verbal Prompt): मेरे जीवन का लक्ष्य (My Aim in Life)
* **Verbal Prompt:** *Definite purpose... becoming a dedicated teacher... spreading literacy... uplifting rural students... noble profession... serving motherland.*

```
                           MY AIM IN LIFE
                           
A human life without a well-defined ambition is akin to a rudderless vessel adrift 
upon stormy seas. Having contemplated various careers, my cherished ambition is to 
become an inspiring and devoted English teacher in a rural government secondary 
school. 

Teaching is not merely a commercial livelihood, but a sacred nation-building mission. 
In rural Rajasthan, thousands of bright, economically disadvantaged children are 
deprived of quality English language and modern digital skills. 

I aspire to illuminate young rural minds with foundational conceptual knowledge, 
instill unshakeable moral character, and train them to crack competitive national 
examinations with confidence. By transforming rural classrooms into vibrant centers 
of curiosity, creativity, and values, I hope to render my humble contribution toward
```

* **Verbal Prompt:** *Modern technology... instant communication... online learning... excessive addiction... gaming... distractions... balanced usage.*

```
video lectures, and instant communication across the globe in a millisecond. 

However, unregulated usage transforms this technological boon into a perilous curse. 
Excessive mobile addiction among teenagers leads to chronic sleep deprivation, 
severe visual impairment, social isolation, and academic ruin caused by endless video 
gaming and short reels. Cyberbullying and privacy risks further threaten young minds.

humanity.
```

6. फटाफट परीक्षा पूर्व चीट शीट (Pre-Exam Rapid Cheat Sheet)

1. **Top Center Title:** Always give a bold, capitalized **HEADING** (e.g., **SWACHH BHARAT ABHIYAN**).
2. **Opening Hook:** Connect directly to the theme in sentence 1 (*"The visual vividly showcases..."*).
3. **Word Length:** Keep strictly within **60 to 80 words** (8 to 10 compact sentences).
4. **Tense Rule:**
   - General topics / habits / social issues: **Simple Present Tense**
   - Past events / celebrations / witnessed accidents: **Simple Past Tense**
5. **No Point-wise Writing:** Write in a **single, unified, well-knit paragraph**. Do not use bullet points or numbered lists.
6. **Sentence Transitions:** Use connectors like *Furthermore, Consequently, Therefore, In addition, In conclusion*.
7. **Concluding Vision:** Finish with a memorable value statement or patriotic civic message.

7. 15-मिनट आत्म-मूल्यांकन बोर्ड टेस्ट (15-Minute Self-Test)

**अभ्यास समय: 15 मिनट | Self-check: use the checklist above (not a separate official mark allocation)**

### प्रश्न (Choose Any ONE - 4 Marks):
* **Option A (Visual Stimulus):** Look at the visual given in your imagination showing *school students carrying saplings and planting them along a roadside with the banner "Each One, Plant One"*, and write a paragraph in about 70 words.  
* **Option B (Verbal Prompt):** Write a paragraph in about 70 words on **'A House on Fire'** using following clues:  
  *Sudden cry of fire... thick black smoke... people rushing with buckets... helpless cries... arrival of fire brigade... ladders and water jets... people rescued safe.*

---

### मॉडल उत्तर-कुंजी एवं मूल्यांकन मानदंड (Marking Key for Self-Test)
* **Title (1/2 Mark):** **A HOUSE ON FIRE** / **COMMUNITY TREE PLANTATION**
* **Relevance & Content (2 Marks):** Accurate flow covering clues; sensory details (thick smoke, screaming, sirens, water hoses).
* **Grammar & Tense (1 Mark):** Flawless Past Tense (*caught fire, rushed, arrived, sprayed, rescued*).
* **Punctuation & Cleanliness (1/2 Mark):** Zero capitalization errors, no spelling slips.
 * **Self-check:** verify accurate data selection, analysis, coherent expression, and 100–120 words; no individual mark split is stated.

**Syllabus source correction, 13 October 2026:** Scope/marks above use the [Madhyamik Class 10 syllabus, PDF pp. 3–5](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf), not the separate Praveshika scheme. This correction does not certify the remaining exercise keys.

1. A practical approach

1. Read the prompt and underline the task type, audience, purpose, and every required outline point.
2. Plan a clear order before writing. A report usually records an event; an essay develops a position or explanation; a blog post addresses readers directly in an accessible voice.
3. Include the supplied points without adding unsupported facts. Use paragraphs where they improve readability.
4. Count the words. Aim for 100–120 words, as stated in the current syllabus.
5. Check tense, agreement, spelling, punctuation, and whether the ending completes the task.

The syllabus does not prescribe a single heading, byline, greeting, or paragraph template for these three forms. Follow any format cues in the actual examination prompt. The structures below are practice options, not mandatory board rules.
2. Practice prompts and sample answers

### A. Report

**Prompt:** Your school held a one-day science exhibition. Write a report using these points: date and venue, opening, student exhibits, visitor response, prizes, closing.

**Sample report (105 words):**

### Students Present Ideas at Science Exhibition

Our school organised a science exhibition in the auditorium on 12 September. The principal opened the programme and welcomed parents, teachers and students from nearby schools. More than thirty teams displayed working models on water conservation, renewable energy, road safety and simple machines. Visitors asked questions, and the student presenters explained how their models worked. A rainwater-harvesting model and a low-cost solar cooker received special attention. A panel of science teachers judged the exhibits and awarded certificates to the best three teams. The principal thanked the participants and volunteers at the closing. The exhibition gave students a chance to explain scientific ideas through practical demonstrations.

### B. Essay

**Prompt:** Write an essay on the value of reading, using these points: knowledge, vocabulary, imagination, informed choices, balanced use of digital media.

**Sample essay (114 words):**

Reading is a useful habit because it helps us learn beyond the classroom. Books, newspapers and reliable digital articles introduce new ideas and strengthen vocabulary. Stories develop imagination, while biographies and history help readers understand different lives and decisions. Regular reading can also improve concentration and make written communication clearer. However, readers should choose reliable sources and think critically instead of accepting every claim they encounter. Digital media makes reading convenient, but notifications and endless scrolling can interrupt attention. Setting aside a short period each day for focused reading is a practical way to build the habit. Reading does not solve every problem, but it gives us knowledge and perspectives for making informed choices.

### C. Blog post

**Prompt:** Write a blog post for your school website on making the school campus less wasteful. Use these points: reusable bottles, labelled bins, reducing paper, student participation, weekly review.

**Sample blog post (107 words):**

### Small Changes for a Cleaner Campus

Can our school reduce waste without making daily routines difficult? We can start with simple choices. Carrying a reusable bottle avoids disposable cups, and clearly labelled bins help students separate paper, plastic and food waste. Teachers can share notices digitally when possible and use both sides of worksheets. These steps work best when students take part, so each class could choose a rotating campus team to remind others and report problems. A short weekly review would show which changes are helping and where bins or signs need improvement. A cleaner campus is not created in one day. It grows from habits that the whole school practises consistently.
3. Self-check before submission

- Did I write the requested form and address the stated audience?
- Did I use all the outline points without inventing data?
- Is the response between 100 and 120 words?
- Does each sentence connect clearly to the task?
- Did I check verb forms, subject–verb agreement, articles, spelling, and punctuation?
4. Source and scope

- [RBSE Madhyamik Class X English syllabus 2026–27](https://rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in/anudeshika-etc/10_2027.pdf), PDF p. 4: Writing Skills 12 marks overall; formal letter, analytical paragraph, and a Report / Essay / Story / Blog task in 100–120 words using outlines. The source does not allocate marks separately among the alternative task types.

The sample answers are author-written practice. They are not past-paper answers or official marking schemes. Format expectations can vary with the wording of the actual prompt.

---
भाग 1: पुराना प्रश्न-पत्र प्रारूप और अभ्यास विषय (वर्ष-दावे अप्रमाणित)

नीचे दिया गया खंडवार प्रारूप ऐतिहासिक अभ्यास सामग्री है। इसे RBSE के 2014–2024 पेपरों का सत्यापित विश्लेषण या 2026–27 का वर्तमान प्रारूप न मानें।

### 1.1 खंडवार अंकभार एवं परीक्षा प्रारूप (Section-wise Marks Distribution)

| Section | Area / Topic | Marks | Question Typology | Focus Skills |

| **Section C** | **Grammar** | **12 M** | Tenses (4M), Reported Speech (2M), Concord (2M), Voice (2M), Tags/Framing (2M) | Structural rules, Adverbial cues, Transformational accuracy |
| **Section D** | **First Flight (Prose)** | **20 M** | Extracts (6M) + Short Answers (6M) + Long Answer (8M) | Thematic depth, Character traits, Critical appreciation |

---

### 1.2 अभ्यास के लिए शामिल विषय

यह अध्याय व्याकरण, लेखन और निर्धारित पाठों के अभ्यास प्रश्न देता है। सत्यापित RBSE प्रश्न-पत्र, प्रश्न-संख्या और पृष्ठ-संदर्भ के बिना वर्षवार अंक तथा पुनरावृत्ति प्रतिशत प्रकाशित नहीं किए जा सकते; इसलिए अप्रमाणित आवृत्ति तालिका हटाई गई है।

---
भाग 2: 🏆 टॉपर्स की उत्तर-पुस्तिका डिकोड (Topper Presentation Secrets)

परीक्षा-उत्तर लिखने के लिए सामान्य प्रस्तुति सुझाव। इनका संबंध किसी सत्यापित टॉपर नमूने या निश्चित अंक से स्थापित नहीं है:

### 2.1 पत्र, ईमेल एवं कहानी के आदर्श फॉर्मेट लेआउट (Standard Formatting Boxes)

### 2.2 टॉपर्स के 6 अचूक प्रस्तुति सिद्धांत (6 Golden Presentation Pillars)

1. **Section-wise Clear Header:** प्रत्येक खंड को पृष्ठ के केंद्र में स्पष्ट बोल्ड लिखें: `═════ SECTION - C: GRAMMAR ═════`। खंडों के प्रश्न कभी न मिलाएँ।
2. **Two-Pen Combination:** प्रश्न संख्या, शीर्षक, सब-हेडिंग व विषय काले पेन से; मुख्य विवरण नीले पेन से लिखें। मुख्य पात्रों व उद्धरणों के नीचे स्केल से अंडरलाइन करें।
3. **Format Boxes:** Email Writing (`To:`, `Cc:`, `Bcc:`, `Subject:`) को स्केल से आयताकार बॉक्स में बंद करें। कहानी में ऊपर `TITLE:` और अंत में `Moral:` स्पष्ट लिखें।
4. **Complete Grammar Sentences:** व्याकरण में केवल (a, b) न लिखकर पूरा वाक्य लिखें और भरे गए शब्द को रेखांकित करें: `She has lived here since 2015.`
5. **Word Limit Discipline:** 20-30 शब्द के प्रश्न में 2-3 चुस्त वाक्य ही लिखें; अनावश्यक विस्तार से वर्तनी व व्याकरण की गलतियाँ बढ़ती हैं।
6. **Zero Scratch Technique:** गलत शब्द पर स्याही का गुच्छा न बनाएं; केवल स्केल से एक हल्की क्षैतिज रेखा खींचें। अंत में `THE END` लिखकर शेष रिक्त पृष्ठों पर तिरछी रेखा खींचें।

भाग 4: चयनित अभ्यास प्रश्न (आवृत्ति सत्यापित नहीं)

### 🔤 [A] व्यावहारिक व्याकरण हॉटस्पॉट्स (Grammar Hotspots: Q1 to Q10)
1. **Rule of 'Before' & 'After' in Past Perfect:**  
   - `Past Perfect (had + V3) + before + Past Simple (V2)` -> The train **had left** before we reached.  
   - `Past Simple (V2) + after + Past Perfect (had + V3)` -> We arrived after the bell **had rung**.  
   *Exam Alert:* RBSE बोर्ड में 'before' वाला वाक्य हर दूसरे साल दोहराया जाता है।
2. **Interrupting Action with 'When' & 'While':**  
   - `was/were + V1-ing` interrupted by `Past Simple (V2)` -> She **was cooking** when the phone rang.
3. **First Conditional Rule:**  
   - `If + Present Simple (V1/V1+s/es), Future Simple (will/shall + V1)` -> If it rains, we **will stay** home.
4. **Adverbial Cues for Present Perfect:**  
   - *already, just, yet, so far* -> He has **already eaten**; I have not seen it **yet**.
5. **Universal Truths in Indirect Speech:**  
   - Tense never changes for scientific truths -> Teacher said that water **boils** at 100°C.
6. **Interrogative Speech Connectors:**  
   - Yes/No questions use `if/whether`; Wh-questions keep the Wh-word; invert verb-subject order to assertive (`Subject + Verb`).
7. **Concord with 'Neither...nor' & 'Either...or':**  
   - Verb agrees with the nearest subject -> Neither the teacher nor the students **were** present.
8. **Plural Nouns with Singular Meaning:**  
   - *Mathematics, Physics, News, Politics* take singular verbs -> Mathematics **is** easy with practice.
9. **Imperative Sentences in Passive Voice:**  
   - `Let + Object + be + V3` -> Open the door -> **Let the door be opened.**
10. **Question Tag Polarity:**  
    - Positive sentence -> Negative tag (`He is rich, isn't he?`); Negative sentence -> Positive tag (`They don't know, do they?`).

### 📖 [B] First Flight (Prose) रिकरिंग प्रश्न (Prose Highlights: Q11 to Q20)
11. **Lencho's Faith:** Why did Lencho not show surprise at the money? -> His faith in God was so absolute that receiving money seemed natural; he only got angry at finding 30 pesos short.
12. **Mandela's Courage:** What did courage mean to Nelson Mandela? -> Courage is not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it; a brave man conquers fear.
13. **Seagull's Catalyst:** What compelled the young seagull to fly? -> Intense hunger made him dive for fish from his mother's beak, forcing his wings to flap open.
14. **Black Aeroplane Mystery:** Who was the strange pilot? -> An unidentified black plane guided him through dark storm clouds without instruments, reflecting divine help or his inner subconscious instinct.
15. **Anne's Talkative Habit:** How did Anne justify talking in essays? -> She cited talking as a student trait inherited from her mother that cannot be eliminated.
16. **Goan Baker's Status:** What proves bakers were prosperous in Goa? -> Their plump physique ("jackfruit appearance") testified to their thriving family business.
17. **Coorgi Bravery:** What is the military pride of Coorg? -> The Coorg Regiment is one of the most decorated, and General Cariappa, India's first Army Chief, was a Coorgi.
18. **Valli's Self-Respect:** Why did Valli refuse the conductor's free drink? -> She had high self-respect, refusing charity and keeping strictly to her own saved coins.
19. **Kisa Gotami's Realization:** Why did Buddha ask for mustard seeds? -> To teach her that death touches every family, and mourning dead loved ones cannot bring them back.
20. **The Proposal Farce:** What does Chekhov satirize in 'The Proposal'? -> The greed and hypocrisy of wealthy landowners who quarrel bitterly over trivial land yet marry for money.

### 🖋️ [C] First Flight (Poetry) रिकरिंग प्रश्न (Poetry Highlights: Q21 to Q30)
21. **Dust of Snow Catalyst:** How did snow change Frost's mood? -> Snow shaken down by a crow from a poisonous hemlock tree transformed his gloomy day into joyful relief.
22. **Fire and Ice Symbolism:** What do they represent? -> Fire = burning lust, desire, greed; Ice = cold hatred, indifference, intolerance.
23. **Tiger's Captivity:** Contrast the caged tiger with the wild tiger. -> In a cage, he stalks quietly behind bars; in the wild, he lurks in tall grass near water holes to hunt deer.
24. **Poetic Devices in 'Tiger in the Zoo':** -> Oxymoron ("quiet rage"), Metaphor ("pads of velvet quiet"), Personification ("He stalks in vivid stripes").
25. **The Ball Poem Epistemology:** What does the lost ball teach? -> It teaches the boy to understand the nature of loss and take personal responsibility in a world of possessions.
26. **Amanda's Escapism:** Name Amanda's 3 imaginary identities. -> (1) A peaceful mermaid in a green sea, (2) An orphan roaming barefoot, (3) Rapunzel in a quiet tower.
27. **The Trees Symbolism:** What does trees moving out signify? -> Women breaking out of domestic confinement into the open sunlight of social equality.
28. **Metaphor in 'Fog':** How is fog depicted? -> Fog is compared to a little cat that sits silently on its haunches watching the city before creeping away.
29. **Custard's True Valor:** How did Custard prove himself? -> While boastful pets fled in terror, cowardly Custard swallowed the pirate whole, proving true bravery acts in crisis.
30. **For Anne Gregory:** What is divine vs. human love? -> Men love women superficially for external yellow hair; only God loves a person purely for the inner soul.

### 🐾 [D] Footprints Without Feet रिकरिंग प्रश्न (Supplementary: Q31 to Q40)
31. **Tricki's Real Sickness:** What was wrong with Tricki? -> No clinical disease, only acute indigestion and obesity caused by Mrs. Pumphrey's constant rich delicacies.
32. **Hari Singh's Return:** Why did Hari Singh return to Anil? -> He valued literacy and self-respect; Anil's education could make him a truly respected man.
33. **Ausable's Secret Weapon:** How did Ausable outsmart Max? -> Through quick wit and psychological trickery (imaginary balcony and police knock) rather than physical weapons.
34. **Horace Danby's Motive:** Why did Horace rob once a year? -> He stole solely to purchase rare, expensive collector books through undercover agents.
35. **Griffin's Lawlessness:** Why was Griffin considered lawless? -> He used his brilliant invisibility discovery to set fire to his landlord's house and steal clothes and money.
36. **Ebright's Scientific Drive:** What drove Richard Ebright's success? -> A first-rate mind, insatiable curiosity, and the will to win for the right reasons.
37. **The Necklace Moral:** What is the lesson of Matilda's tragedy? -> Unbridled vanity and discontent lead to ruinous poverty; be content with what you have.
38. **The Irony of the Necklace:** What was the final revelation? -> Madame Forestier's lost necklace was a cheap imitation worth 500 francs, which cost Matilda 10 years of slavery.
39. **Bholi's Metamorphosis:** Why did Sulekha refuse Bishamber? -> Educated by her loving teacher, she rejected an old, limping, greedy man who demanded a humiliating dowry.
40. **Think-Tank's Blunder:** How did Humpty Dumpty save Earth? -> The Martian ruler thought the cracked egg was him, believed Earthlings planned to shatter Mars, and fled.

### ✍️ [E] लेखन व पठन कौशल हॉटस्पॉट्स (Writing & Reading Hotspots: Q41 to Q50)
41. **Unseen Passage Title Strategy:** Skim first and last lines; extract a 2-4 word theme noun phrase (*Value of Trees, Time Management*).
42. **Vocabulary Search Method:** Match parts of speech. For an adjective clue, locate an adjective in the passage; for past tense verbs, search for `-ed` verbs.
43. **Formal Letter Salutations:** Use `Sir` / `Madam` with `Yours faithfully` for officials/editors; use `Respected Sir` with `Yours obediently` for school principals.
44. **Email Address Standard Format:** Lowercase, no spaces, correct domain (e.g., `principal.gsss@rajasthan.gov.in`).
45. **Story Connectors:** Connect outline hints using *Once, Soon, Suddenly, At last, Therefore* in Past Indefinite tense.
46. **Story Scoring Trick:** Always write `TITLE:` at top and `Moral:` at the end. These carry 2 out of 4 total marks!
47. **Paragraph Writing on Visual Prompts:** Start with an introductory sentence, explain reasons and results in 3-4 sentences, and conclude with an inspiring takeaway.
48. **Word Limit Control:** Keep letters strictly 100-120 words. Writing too much invites spelling slips and deducts marks.
49. **Passive Subject Deletion:** Omit vague agents (*someone, people, they, the police*) when the receiver or action is the main focus.
50. **Clear presentation:** Use legible handwriting, clear question numbers, and restrained underlining where it improves readability. Presentation alone does not guarantee marks.

### 5.2 परीक्षा कक्ष में 4 सामान्य गलतियाँ और उनसे बचाव (Mistake Busters)

1. **Reading Passage में पूरा पैराग्राफ छापना:** प्रश्न का सटीक उत्तर अपनी भाषा में 1-2 वाक्यों में दें; पूरा पैराग्राफ न उतारें।

4. **Literature में शब्द सीमा से अधिक लिखना:** 2 अंक वाले प्रश्न में 20-30 शब्द पर्याप्त हैं। सही कीवर्ड्स ही पूरे अंक दिलाते हैं।
